And in this manner they are able to put a check on the tendency for negativities—such as ignorant liking and ignorant disliking—to disturb their peace of mind."}

corpus_segments:27254.acip: [D10] DE LTAR NGES PA'I BYED LAS NI, DE'I TSE SNGON PO DE 'DZIN PA RNAM PA CAN GYI SEMS SNGON 'DZIN DBANG SHES LA BDAN {%BDEN} PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA YONGS SUM BOR {%SU MA BOR} YANG, SNGON PO LA PHYI ROL GYI DON DU MNGON BAR ZHEN PA KUN BRTAGS MNGON GYUR MGO GNON PA'I TSUL GYIS SPANGS PA'O,,
corpus_segments:27254.wylie: [d10] de ltar nges pa'i byed las ni, de'i tshe sngon po de 'dzin pa rnam pa can gyi sems sngon 'dzin dbang shes la bdan {%bden} par mngon par zhen pa yongs sum bor {%su ma bor} yang, sngon po la phyi rol gyi don du mngon bar zhen pa kun brtags mngon gyur mgo gnon pa'i tshul gyis spangs pa'o
corpus_segments:27254.english: And what will this ascertainment do for us?  We would have to say, first of all, that it is not the case that we would be able then to reject the attraction we feel with our sense perception—with the state of mind holding to blue, the state of mind which has taken on a subject aspect—as it grasps to the blue and is strongly attracted to the idea that it exists in reality.  Nonetheless, it is the case that we are able to rid ourselves of the manifest form of our learned attraction to the idea that the blue is an outer object—and this is accomplished through an act of suppressing it.

We would have to say, first of all, that it is not the case that we would be able then to reject the attraction we feel with our sense perception—with the state of mind holding to blue, the state of mind which has taken on a subject aspect—as it grasps to the blue and is strongly attracted to the idea that it exists in reality.  Nonetheless, it is the case that we are able to rid ourselves of the manifest form of our learned attraction to the idea that the blue is an outer object—and this is accomplished through an act of suppressing it."}

corpus_segments:27256.acip: [D12] NGAG DON NI, LHAN CIG DMIGS NGES KYI RTAGS LAS SNGON PO SNGO SNANG DBANG SHES DANG RDZAS GZHAN MIN PAR NGES PA'I BLO CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYIS SNGON PO PHYI ROL GYI DON DU ZHEN PA'I SGRO 'DOGS KUN BRTAGS MNGON GYUR MGO GNON NUS TE, KHYAD KYIS SNGON PO SEMS KYI DANG GNYID {%KYI BDAG NYID} YIN PAR NGES PA'I BLO TSAD MA GZHAN LA LTOS MED DU 'DREN NUS PA'I PHYIR,
corpus_segments:27256.wylie: [d12] ngag don ni, lhan cig dmigs nges kyi rtags las sngon po sngo snang dbang shes dang rdzas gzhan min par nges pa'i blo chos can, khyod kyis sngon po phyi rol gyi don du zhen pa'i sgro 'dogs kun brtags mngon gyur mgo gnon nus te, khyad kyis sngon po sems kyi dang gnyid {%kyi bdag nyid} yin par nges pa'i blo tshad ma gzhan la ltos med du 'dren nus pa'i phyir
corpus_segments:27256.english: Here then is how we express the meaning of the statement here, in a syllogism: Let us consider the state of mind where we ascertain—through a reason which helps us ascertain that they are perceived together—the fact that the blue does not consist of any substance separate from the sense awareness which has taken on an aspect of the blue. This state of mind acts to suppress the manifest appearance of the learned tendency to exaggerate the reality of the situation, where we believe that the blue is an outer object; Because this state has the power to elicit—without depending on any other factor—an accurate state of mind where we ascertain that the blue is part and parcel with the mind itself. The third level of deep practice

The third level of deep practice"}

corpus_segments:27457.acip: DANG PO NI, NGAR 'DZIN GYI 'JIG LTAS NGA YIR 'DZIN PA'I 'JIG LTA SKYED PAS, SEMS CAN 'DI RNAMS NI DANG POR TE BDAG GI BAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA'I 'JIG LTA'I SNGA ROL TU, NGAR 'DZIN PA'I 'JIG LTAS RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MIN PA'I BDAG RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD DO SNYAM NAS, NGA ZHES PA'I DON 'DI NYID DU STE LA BDEN PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PAR BYED DO,,
corpus_segments:27457.wylie: dang po ni, ngar 'dzin gyi 'jig ltas nga yir 'dzin pa'i 'jig lta skyed pas, sems can 'di rnams ni dang por te bdag gi bar mngon par zhen pa'i 'jig lta'i snga rol tu, ngar 'dzin pa'i 'jig ltas rang bzhin gyis yod pa min pa'i bdag rang bzhin gyis yod do snyam nas, nga zhes pa'i don 'di nyid du ste la bden par mngon par zhen par byed do
corpus_segments:27457.english: We begin with the first. The version of the view of destruction where we hold to a “me” triggers the version where we hold to some “mine.” Thus all suffering beings first (that is, before they give rise to the view of destruction where they begin wanting what is “mine”) give rise to the view of destruction where they want a “me,” talking about something which is a thing that is itself—which exists “in reality.” This is a view of “me” which thinks to itself that a person who could never exist in & of themselves does exist in & of themselves.

The version of the view of destruction where we hold to a “me” triggers the version where we hold to some “mine.” Thus all suffering beings first (that is, before they give rise to the view of destruction where they begin wanting what is “mine”) give rise to the view of destruction where they want a “me,” talking about something which is a thing that is itself—which exists “in reality.” This is a view of “me” which thinks to itself that a person who could never exist in & of themselves does exist in & of themselves."}

corpus_segments:27697.acip: 'DIS NI GDAGS GZHI PHUNG PO LA BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN MA PHYIN NA, BTAGS CHOS GANG ZAG LA BDEN PAR 'DZIN PA'I ZHEN YUL YANG SUN MI PHYIN PAS, GANG ZAG BDEN MED DU MA RTOGS PA'I PHYIR, GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED MTSAN NYID RDZOGS PA MA RTOGS PAR BSTAN NO,,
corpus_segments:27697.wylie: 'dis ni gdags gzhi phung po la bden par zhen pa'i zhen yul sun ma phyin na, btags chos gang zag la bden par 'dzin pa'i zhen yul yang sun mi phyin pas, gang zag bden med du ma rtogs pa'i phyir, gang zag gi bdag med mtshan nyid rdzogs pa ma rtogs par bstan no
corpus_segments:27697.english: What's being said here is that—if we are not able to use this realization to rip out the object that the belief in the thing we label ourselves (the parts of us) believes is real—then we will fail, in turn, to rip out the object that our tendency to think that things are real believes is real when it focuses on the result of the labeling: the person themselves. And then we will fail to realize that the person has no reality; and then we will fail to reach a realization which is complete in every respect as it sees that the person is not themselves.

And then we will fail to realize that the person has no reality; and then we will fail to reach a realization which is complete in every respect as it sees that the person is not themselves."}

corpus_segments:27767.acip: RJE BTZUN GYIS YUL GANG LA JI 'DRA BA ZHIG TU DMIGS PAS, 'KHOR BA LAS MI THAR BA BSHAD PA ZHUS PA'I LAN DU, BDAG NI 'KHOR BA LAS 'DA' BA DANG, MYANG 'DAS 'THOB PAR 'GYUR RO SNYAM DU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I TSUL GYIS RTOG PAR BYED PAS, MI RTAG PA LA SOGS PA BSGOMS PA NA,
corpus_segments:27767.wylie: rje btsun gyis yul gang la ji 'dra ba zhig tu dmigs pas, 'khor ba las mi thar ba bshad pa zhus pa'i lan du, bdag ni 'khor ba las 'da' ba dang, myang 'das 'thob par 'gyur ro snyam du bden par zhen pa'i tshul gyis rtog par byed pas, mi rtag pa la sogs pa bsgoms pa na
corpus_segments:27767.english: And so the Holy One is requesting an explanation of what object a person needs to focus upon—and in what way—in order to fail to free themselves from the cycle of suffering. The response given to him is that there are people who meditate upon the aspects of impermanence and so on, but in a way in which they are imagining to themselves that things are real as they think to themselves, “I will go beyond the cycle of pain; I will reach nirvana.”

corpus_segments:27851.acip: DE LA GZUNG BA PHYI ROL LA ZHEN PA SPONG BA'I DON NI, PHYI ROL GYI DON TSAD MAS GRUB KYANG, PHYI ROL BDEN GRUB RIGS PAS KHEGS PA DBU MA PA LTAR GTAN LA PHAB PA'I DON BSGOMS NAS BDEN ZHEN SPONG BA DANG,
corpus_segments:27851.wylie: de la gzung ba phyi rol la zhen pa spong ba'i don ni, phyi rol gyi don tshad mas grub kyang, phyi rol bden grub rigs pas khegs pa dbu ma pa ltar gtan la phab pa'i don bsgoms nas bden zhen spong ba dang
corpus_segments:27851.english: What does it mean then when we say that a person has “rid oneself of a belief in objects of the mind—outer objects”? It could mean that we have meditated upon the way as those of the Middle Way school describe it—showing how, although outer objects are confirmed by accurate perception, the idea that outer objects could exist in truth is disproved by reasoning—and through this meditation we have been able to rid ourselves of this particular belief that a thing could exist in truth.

corpus_segments:27866.acip: DE LA CHOS KYI DBYINGS ZHES PA NI NYI KHRI SNANG BA LAS, DE LA RTOG PA DANG RNAM PAR RTOG PA NI DNGOS PO DANG DE'I MTSAN MA LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PA STE, DE MED PA'I PHYIR CHAGS PA MED PA NYID DU RIG PAR BYA'O, ,YOD PAR MA GYUR PA NYID NI CHOS THAMS CAD KYI DE BZHIN NYID DO,,
corpus_segments:27866.wylie: de la chos kyi dbyings zhes pa ni nyi khri snang ba las, de la rtog pa dang rnam par rtog pa ni dngos po dang de'i mtshan ma la mngon par zhen pa ste, de med pa'i phyir chags pa med pa nyid du rig par bya'o, ,yod par ma gyur pa nyid ni chos thams cad kyi de bzhin nyid do
corpus_segments:27866.english: As for this expression, “sphere of reality,” we see it explained in the Illumination of the Twenty Thousand: When we talk about “thinking that something is there” or “imagining that something is there,” we're referring to a belief in things, and the indicators of things. And you should understand that—since these don't even exist—the attachment to them doesn't really exist either. The ultimate nature of things is in fact nothing other than this same quality, of not even existing.

corpus_segments:28135.wylie: nam snying gi mdor rtsa ltung rnams kyis sngon bskyed pa'i dge rtsa 'joms pa dang, bslab btus las, rnyed bkur la lhag par zhen pas khyim la lta ba dang, mngon pa'i nga rgyal gyis khengs pa dang chos spong bas kyang sngon bskyed pa'i dge ba zad par byed cing, dge ba'i chos kyis rgyas par mi 'gyur bar gsungs pas
corpus_segments:28135.english: The Sutra of the Essence of the Sky describes how root downfalls can destroy the store of good deeds that we have built up previously. The Compendium of the Trainings says that looking to a household while entertaining a strong desire for honor and offerings; arrogance born from overweening pride; and giving up the teachings can all as well finish off good seeds that we have previously planted—and also prevent the growth of our past good deeds.

corpus_segments:28199.acip: GSUM PA NI, RANG STE PHRA BA'I 'JIG LTA'I BDAG TU LTA BA DANG 'BREL BA STE DE SNGON DU 'GRO BA'I BDAG DANG, SEMS CAN SOGS RANG RKYA BA'I RDZAS YOD DU 'DZIN PA RAGS PA'I GANG ZAG GI BDAG DANG BDAG GI BAR 'DZIN PA DANG, PHUNG KHAMS SKYE MCHED LA BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I CHOS KYI BDAG 'DZIN RNAMS YONGS SU ZAD PAR 'GYUR RO,,
corpus_segments:28199.wylie: gsum pa ni, rang ste phra ba'i 'jig lta'i bdag tu lta ba dang 'brel ba ste de sngon du 'gro ba'i bdag dang, sems can sogs rang rkya ba'i rdzas yod du 'dzin pa rags pa'i gang zag gi bdag dang bdag gi bar 'dzin pa dang, phung khams skye mched la bden par zhen pa'i chos kyi bdag 'dzin rnams yongs su zad par 'gyur ro
corpus_segments:28199.english: This brings us to our third point from above: a description of what it is we rid ourselves of at the fourth level. And then everything related to seeing things as themselves is finished off completely—which is to say, everything related to seeing things as themselves as we do this in the subtle form of the view of destruction. This involves the tendency to believe in a self-nature which is the precursor for this view; the tendency to believe in the gross form of a self-nature to a person in the case where we are holding living beings & such as existing in a self-standing, substantial way (in addition to thinking this way about what is possessed by such a being); and the tendency to believe in a self-nature to the parts of a person: the heaps, the categories, & the doors of sense—thinking that these are real.

And then everything related to seeing things as themselves is finished off completely—which is to say, everything related to seeing things as themselves as we do this in the subtle form of the view of destruction. corpus_segments:28384.english: The horse or elephant does appear to the first, but nothing more: they don't believe it is real. The animal appears to the second as well, and they also believe it's real. The creature does not appear to the third, nor do they believe it is real.

corpus_segments:28461.acip: 'O NA BDAG GI 'DI ZHES ZHES PA'I RANG 'GREL LAS, 'DI NI BDAG GI'O SNYAM DU NGAR 'DZIN PA'I YUL LAS GZHAN PA'I DNGOS PO'I RNAM PA MA LUS PA LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PA YIN NO, ZHES MIG LA SOGS PA'I GZHI LA DMIGS NAS 'DI NI BDAG GI YIN NO SNYAM DU ZHEN PA BDAG GIR 'DZIN PAR BSHAD PA JI LTAR YIN SNYAM NA,
corpus_segments:28461.wylie: 'o na bdag gi 'di zhes zhes pa'i rang 'grel las, 'di ni bdag gi'o snyam du ngar 'dzin pa'i yul las gzhan pa'i dngos po'i rnam pa ma lus pa la mngon par zhen pa yin no, zhes mig la sogs pa'i gzhi la dmigs nas 'di ni bdag gi yin no snyam du zhen pa bdag gir 'dzin par bshad pa ji ltar yin snyam na
corpus_segments:28461.english: The following question might then arise in ones mind: Now then; at the point where it mentions “We say of them 'mine',” the autocommentary also states that “when we say 'mine,' we hold a false belief in all entities other than the object we hold when we say 'me'.” What about this particular reference, which seems to be saying that when we focus on objects such as the eye and believe in them, wrongly—thinking that “this is mine”—then this is the tendency to hold things as “mine”?
corpus_segments:28461.raw: {"course": "ILL", "acip": "'O NA BDAG GI 'DI ZHES ZHES PA'I RANG 'GREL LAS, 'DI NI BDAG GI'O SNYAM DU NGAR 'DZIN PA'I YUL LAS GZHAN PA'I DNGOS PO'I RNAM PA MA LUS PA LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PA YIN NO, ZHES MIG LA SOGS PA'I GZHI LA DMIGS NAS 'DI NI BDAG GI YIN NO SNYAM DU ZHEN PA BDAG GIR 'DZIN PAR BSHAD PA JI LTAR YIN SNYAM NA,", "wylie": "'o na bdag gi 'di zhes zhes pa'i rang 'grel las, 'di ni bdag gi'o snyam du ngar 'dzin pa'i yul las gzhan pa'i dngos po'i rnam pa ma lus pa la mngon par zhen pa yin no, zhes mig la sogs pa'i gzhi la dmigs nas 'di ni bdag gi yin no snyam du zhen pa bdag gir 'dzin par bshad pa ji ltar yin snyam na", "english": "The following question might then arise in ones mind: Now then; at the point where it mentions “We say of them 'mine',” the autocommentary also states that “when we say 'mine,' we hold a false belief in all entities other than the object we hold when we say 'me'.” What about this particular reference, which seems to be saying that when we focus on objects such as the eye and believe in them, wrongly—thinking that “this is mine”—then this is the tendency to hold things as “mine”?"}

corpus_segments:28462.acip: DE NI MIG SOGS RNAMS BDAG GI BAR MTHONG NAS BDAG GI BA LA BDEN PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA'I DON YIN GYI, BDAG GI BA'I MTSAN GZHI MIG SOGS DMIGS PAR STON PA MIN TE, DE LTAR MA YIN NA 'JIG LTA DANG CHOS KYI BDAG 'DZIN GNYIS MI 'GAL BAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
corpus_segments:28462.wylie: de ni mig sogs rnams bdag gi bar mthong nas bdag gi ba la bden par mngon par zhen pa'i don yin gyi, bdag gi ba'i mtshan gzhi mig sogs dmigs par ston pa min te, de ltar ma yin na 'jig lta dang chos kyi bdag 'dzin gnyis mi 'gal bar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:28462.english: The point of this reference though is to say that we see the eye and so on as being something of mine, and then hold the false belief that it is something of mine in a real sense. This is not though meant to indicate that we are directing our perceptions towards the eye and so on as a classical example of the concept of “mine.” If this were not the case, then the two of the view of destruction and the tendency to believe in a self-nature of things would no longer be mutually exclusive.

corpus_segments:28739.acip: GANG ZHIG GSUNG RAB KYI DON PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR MA RTOGS SHING, 'KHOR BA THOG MA MED PA NAS DNGOS PO BDEN 'DZIN GYI BAG CHAGS BZHAG PA SMIN PA LAS BYUNG BA'I DNGOS PO LA BDEN PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA YUN RING MO NAS 'DRIS PA'I MDZA' BO DANG BRAL BA STE,
corpus_segments:28739.wylie: gang zhig gsung rab kyi don phyin ci ma log par ma rtogs shing, 'khor ba thog ma med pa nas dngos po bden 'dzin gyi bag chags bzhag pa smin pa las byung ba'i dngos po la bden par mngon par zhen pa yun ring mo nas 'dris pa'i mdza' bo dang bral ba ste
corpus_segments:28739.english: And so there are those who have yet to grasp the meaning of the highest of all words in an unerring way; in their hearts, the deep seeds for believing that things are real have been sown, for time with no beginning, here in the cycle of pain. These seeds have ripened, and produced a craving for believing that things are real—and these people must learn to leave behind this friend, who has been so close to them, for so very long.

corpus_segments:29124.acip: CI STE YANG DE LTAR DNGOS PO LA BDEN PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA THAMS CAD GCOD PA NA, BRED SHA 'THON PA THA SNYAD KYI BDEN PA LA BDEN PAR ZHEN PA 'DI GANG KUN BYANG GNYIS KYI 'CHING GROL GYI RGYUR 'GYUR BA, RDZAS TE RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I BDAG NYID 'GA' ZHIG TU SKYE BAR 'GYUR BA CIG BYA DGOS SO ZHES SMRA NA, DE SKAD DU SMRA BA LA NI TSIG TZAM ZHIG LHAG MAR LUS PAR 'GYUR RO,,
corpus_segments:29124.wylie: ci ste yang de ltar dngos po la bden par mngon par zhen pa thams cad gcod pa na, bred sha 'thon pa tha snyad kyi bden pa la bden par zhen pa 'di gang kun byang gnyis kyi 'ching grol gyi rgyur 'gyur ba, rdzas te rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i bdag nyid 'ga' zhig tu skye bar 'gyur ba cig bya dgos so zhes smra na, de skad du smra ba la ni tshig tsam zhig lhag mar lus par 'gyur ro
corpus_segments:29124.english: Well now, how is it? Suppose that, as we've described it, people start to eliminate all of their tendencies to grasp to things existing in reality. Then though their faces take on a certain look of panic, and they start feeling a strong belief that nominal reality though must be real. That is, they begin to say that there must exist objects which act as causes behind the bondage and the liberation going on with the negative side of things, and the enlightened side of things. And they feel that these causes must be creating some number of entities which are substantial; that is, which exist by definition. But these kinds of proclamations end up just being all words, and nothing else.

corpus_segments:29237.acip: GAL TE KUN GZHI RNAM SHES KHAS MI LEN KYANG DGE MI DGE'I BAG CHAGS 'JOG PA DANG, BAG CHAGS DE SMIN PA LAS 'BRAS BU 'BYUNG BAR 'DOD DGOS TE, 'JUG 'GREL LAS, THOG MA MED PA'I 'KHOR BAR DNGOS PO'I BAG CHAGS BZHAG PA YONGS SU SMIN PA, DNGOS PO LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PA, ZHES DANG, DE 'DRA BA GZHAN YANG MANG DU 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR RO,,
corpus_segments:29237.wylie: gal te kun gzhi rnam shes khas mi len kyang dge mi dge'i bag chags 'jog pa dang, bag chags de smin pa las 'bras bu 'byung bar 'dod dgos te, 'jug 'grel las, thog ma med pa'i 'khor bar dngos po'i bag chags bzhag pa yongs su smin pa, dngos po la mngon par zhen pa, zhes dang, de 'dra ba gzhan yang mang du 'byung ba'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:29237.english: Even if we don't accept the idea of a foundation consciousness, we still have to agree that virtuous and non-virtuous deep seeds can be planted; and that as these seeds ripen, they give forth results. As the autocommentary to Entering the Middle Way puts it, In the cycle of suffering with no beginning, the deep seeds of things have been planted, and have ripened. And we have had a deep belief in those things… And we see many other such references as well.

corpus_segments:29263.wylie: de don dang sbyor ba ni, rgyal po chen po de bzhin du byis pa so so'i skye bo thos pa dang mi ldan pa yang mig gis gzugs rnams mthong nas yid bde bar 'gyur ba'i gzugs rnams la mngon par zhen te, mngon par zhen par gyur nas chags pa skyed par byed do
corpus_segments:29263.english: And then the sutra relates this metaphor to its referent— O great king, infants who have no learning are the same. corpus_segments:29405.acip: DBU SEMS GANG GI LUGS KYIS KYANG DE LTA SEMS CAN RNAMS LA SNANG ZHING, SNANG BA LTAR DU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I ZHE NA {%ZHEN} GZHI DE, ZHEN YUL DES STONG PAR BSTAN PA CIG YOD NA, STONG NYID DE RTOGS PA LAM DU 'GRO BA YIN GYI,
corpus_segments:29405.wylie: dbu sems gang gi lugs kyis kyang de lta sems can rnams la snang zhing, snang ba ltar du bden par zhen pa'i zhe na {%zhen} gzhi de, zhen yul des stong par bstan pa cig yod na, stong nyid de rtogs pa lam du 'gro ba yin gyi
corpus_segments:29405.english: It doesn't matter which system we're talking about—that of the Middle Way, or that of the Mind Only. In either case, there is a basis behind our wrong belief: something that appears to living beings to exist in a certain way, and which they subsequently believe to exist in truth, as it appears to. If there is something that we can point to as being empty of the object that people believe they see, then—and only then—the realization of that sheer absence or emptiness can function as a path.

corpus_segments:29406.acip: SEMS CAN RANG DGA' BA RNAMS KYIS BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN PHYUNG BA'I STONG NYID RTOGS PA LAM DU MI BYED PAR STONG PA GZHAN CIG BDEN PAR SGRUB PA NI, THOG MA MED PA NAS ZHUGS PA'I BDEN ZHEN PHRA RAGS GANG GI YANG GNYEN POR MI 'GRO BAS NGAL BA 'BRAS MED DO,,
corpus_segments:29406.wylie: sems can rang dga' ba rnams kyis bden par zhen pa'i zhen yul sun phyung ba'i stong nyid rtogs pa lam du mi byed par stong pa gzhan cig bden par sgrub pa ni, thog ma med pa nas zhugs pa'i bden zhen phra rags gang gi yang gnyen por mi 'gro bas ngal ba 'bras med do
corpus_segments:29406.english: And suppose we fail to make a path out of coming to a realization of emptiness—an emptiness where we have overthrown that object of belief: the belief of just normal people of the world that things exist in reality. That is, suppose we take some other kind of emptiness to exist, really. This could never serve as an antidote for either one of the forms—more subtle, or more coarse—of the belief in something real which has resided in the hearts of beings for time with no beginning. And as such, the whole exercise would be one in futility.

corpus_segments:29442.acip: DE'I PHYIR PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS KYI SKYE MCHED MED PA KHO NA YIN ZHING, YID KYI RNAM PAR SHES PA LA PHYI ROL DE'I RNAM PA SNANG BA TZAM LA PHYI ROL NYID DU MNGON PAR ZHEN PA NI BZLOG TU MED PAR 'BYUNG NGO,,
corpus_segments:29442.wylie: de'i phyir phyi rol gyi gzugs kyi skye mched med pa kho na yin zhing, yid kyi rnam par shes pa la phyi rol de'i rnam pa snang ba tsam la phyi rol nyid du mngon par zhen pa ni bzlog tu med par 'byung ngo
corpus_segments:29442.english: As such, an outer door of visible form can only be something which does not exist. And what's happening is that we are strongly attached to thinking that the awareness of the thought is an aspect of the outer world—that something which is nothing more than the appearance of being outside is the outside world itself. This attachment occurs in a very compelling way that is difficult to reverse.

And what's happening is that we are strongly attached to thinking that the awareness of the thought is an aspect of the outer world—that something which is nothing more than the appearance of being outside is the outside world itself. corpus_segments:29616.acip: DES NA DBU SEMS SU YI LUGS LA YANG SEMS CAN RNAMS GANG LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PA'I GZHI, PHYI NANG GI CHOS SU SNANG BA 'DI DAG LA BYED PA LA NI MI 'DRA BA MED LA, DE RNAMS STONG PAR STON PA NI GZHI DE LA MNGON ZHEN ZLOG PA'I PHYIR DU YIN PA YANG 'DRA MOD KYANG, ZHEN TSUL LA MI MTHUN TE
corpus_segments:29616.wylie: des na dbu sems su yi lugs la yang sems can rnams gang la mngon par zhen pa'i gzhi, phyi nang gi chos su snang ba 'di dag la byed pa la ni mi 'dra ba med la, de rnams stong par ston pa ni gzhi de la mngon zhen zlog pa'i phyir du yin pa yang 'dra mod kyang, zhen tshul la mi mthun te
corpus_segments:29616.english: Thus we can say that—whether we are speaking about the system of the Middle Way, or to that of the Mind Only—there is no difference in the fact that we are referring to the way that outer & inner entities make their appearance: we are speaking of that foundational state of things which living beings are holding on to. When we clarify that these things are empty, the statement in each of the two systems is similar in that we are attempting to put a stop to how people hold on to this foundation; and yet the way in which each system describes the holding on that people do is incompatible.

When we clarify that these things are empty, the statement in each of the two systems is similar in that we are attempting to put a stop to how people hold on to this foundation; and yet the way in which each system describes the holding on that people do is incompatible."}

corpus_segments:29617.acip: SEMS TZAM PAS NI GZUNG 'DZIN GNYIS PHYI NANG DU RGYANGS CHAD DU SNANG BA LA SNANG BA LTAR DU, GZUNG 'DZIN RDZAS THA DAD DU ZHEN PA YIN LA, DE'I GNYEN POR SNANG BA GZHAN DBANG 'DI CHOS CAN DU BZUNG NAS, GZUNG 'DZIN RDZAS THA DAD DU YOD PA 'GOG PA YIN PAS DGAG GZHI DE DGAG BYA DE YIN PA 'GOG PA YIN NO,,
corpus_segments:29617.wylie: sems tsam pas ni gzung 'dzin gnyis phyi nang du rgyangs chad du snang ba la snang ba ltar du, gzung 'dzin rdzas tha dad du zhen pa yin la, de'i gnyen por snang ba gzhan dbang 'di chos can du bzung nas, gzung 'dzin rdzas tha dad du yod pa 'gog pa yin pas dgag gzhi de dgag bya de yin pa 'gog pa yin no
corpus_segments:29617.english: That is, the Mind Only would say that the belief that people hold to here is that objects and their subjects are essentially separate, as they appear to be when it seems that—for the objects and subjects—those which are inside of us and those which are outside look to exist at a significant distance away from each other. And then as an antidote for this perception, we take what it is that appears—dominated entities—and take them as the subject under logical consideration, and then disprove that it could display any reality where objects & their subjects were essentially separate. Thus, the denial is done by taking this foundational state of things that we deny itself as the object we are denying, and work to deny that.

corpus_segments:29618.acip: DBU MA PA LTAR NA ZHEN TSUL NI SNANG BA LA THA SNYAD PA'I BLOS BZHAG PA MIN PA'I BDEN GRUB TU ZHEN PA YIN LA, DE'I GNYEN POR SNANG BA 'DI CHOS CAN DU BZUNG NAS, DE 'DRA BA'I BDEN PAR MED CES 'GOG STE,
corpus_segments:29618.wylie: dbu ma pa ltar na zhen tshul ni snang ba la tha snyad pa'i blos bzhag pa min pa'i bden grub tu zhen pa yin la, de'i gnyen por snang ba 'di chos can du bzung nas, de 'dra ba'i bden par med ces 'gog ste
corpus_segments:29618.english: Those of the Middle Way describe the belief with which we hold to things in a different way. They say that we hold that things exist in reality—which is to say, we believe that what appears to us is not being established by a nominal state of mind. And then as an antidote for this belief, we start by taking this way that things appear to us as the subject under our logical consideration. Then we deny this appearance by saying, “This is not something which exists as real, in the way we have described that.”

Then we deny this appearance by saying, “This is not something which exists as real, in the way we have described that.”"}

corpus_segments:29619.acip: DE YANG DGAG GZHI DE DGAG BYA YIN PA 'GOG PA YIN TE, SEMS CAN GYIS ZHEN PA NA GZHI DE LA DGAG BYA DE DON GZHAN DU YOD PAR 'DZIN PA MIN PAR, GZHI DE DGAG BYA DE'I NGO BOR ZHEN PA'I PHYIR DANG, STONG PA YANG JI LTAR ZHEN PA DE LTAR DU YOD PAS STONG PAR BSTAN DGOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
corpus_segments:29619.wylie: de yang dgag gzhi de dgag bya yin pa 'gog pa yin te, sems can gyis zhen pa na gzhi de la dgag bya de don gzhan du yod par 'dzin pa min par, gzhi de dgag bya de'i ngo bor zhen pa'i phyir dang, stong pa yang ji ltar zhen pa de ltar du yod pas stong par bstan dgos pa'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:29619.english: This denial is a refusal that the objects which make up the foundation state where we are accomplishing our denial could in fact exist as what we are denying about them. This is not to say that when living beings are engaging in what they believe, they hold this foundation state to exist in some other way than that expressed by the object that we deny; rather, they actually hold that this state exists, in its very essence, as expressed by the object that we deny. Moreover, we have to demonstrate as well that emptiness itself is also empty of existing in the way that we might believe it to.

corpus_segments:29667.acip: SHES BYA DANG SHES PA LA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD MED KYI KHYAD PAR MED PAR STON PA YIN LA, SKRA SHAD MED NA DER SNANG BA'I SHES PA YANG MED CES PA DANG, SGYU MA LA RTA GLANG DU ZHEN PA'I ZHEN YUL MED NA DER 'DZIN PA'I SHES PA YANG MED CES SOGS NI, SLOB DPON 'DI'I LUGS GTAN MIN NO,,
corpus_segments:29667.wylie: shes bya dang shes pa la rang bzhin gyis yod med kyi khyad par med par ston pa yin la, skra shad med na der snang ba'i shes pa yang med ces pa dang, sgyu ma la rta glang du zhen pa'i zhen yul med na der 'dzin pa'i shes pa yang med ces sogs ni, slob dpon 'di'i lugs gtan min no
corpus_segments:29667.english: What this is indicating is that there is no difference between knowable things and the awareness which knows them, as far as existing through some nature of their own, or not. And what this is saying is that—if there is no strand of hair—then neither is there any state of mind which is taking that strand as its aspect. It is absolutely not the position of this master though to say that—if the object that one was thinking was there when we perceived a horse or cow in an illusion didn't really exist—then the state of mind that was grasping to it didn't exist either.

corpus_segments:29861.acip: DE'I PHYIR SEMS TZAM PA 'DI LA 'JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD KYI RGYU GANG YIN PA DE RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS YOD PA MIN PAS, KYE MA KYE HUD GZHAN SEMS TZAM PA'I LTAR NA NGES DON MTHAR THUG PA 'BYED PA'I SHES RAB KYI RTZAL MED PAS GZHAN DBANG GI RDZAS SHES TZAM LA BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I CHAGS PA YI SGO NAS, GZHAN DBANG GI BUM PA SO MA BTANG BAR,
corpus_segments:29861.wylie: de'i phyir sems tsam pa 'di la 'jig rten gyi tha snyad kyi rgyu gang yin pa de rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis yod pa min pas, kye ma kye hud gzhan sems tsam pa'i ltar na nges don mthar thug pa 'byed pa'i shes rab kyi rtsal med pas gzhan dbang gi rdzas shes tsam la bden par zhen pa'i chags pa yi sgo nas, gzhan dbang gi bum pa so ma btang bar
corpus_segments:29861.english: As such, let's consider these followers of the Mind Only. If it is the fact that what we say is that the cause in the parlance of the world is not something that could exist through any essential nature of its own, then oh my gosh! According to these other ones—the Mind Only (since they possess none of the fluency of wisdom which makes distinctions regarding the ultimate point of what was truly intended)—then dominated entities exist only as a mental substance, and are still real. These thinkers are attached to thinking of them thus, as real, and in this manner they approach a clay pot of the concept of dominated entities that was never properly fired.

corpus_segments:30055.acip: DE LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PAS DE DAG SDIG PA CHEN PO DANG SBYOR LA BSOD NAMS DANG YE SHES KYI TSOGS BSAGS PA LAS NYAMS PAR 'GYUR BA

corpus_segments:30055.english: And then because of their strong craving, people like this undertake major negative actions; which means that they begin to fail in their intended accumulation of merit and wisdom.

corpus_segments:30086.acip: DPER NA SMIG CHU NI CHUR MED PAS CHUR ZHEN PA'I RI DVAGS SLU BA BZHIN DU BSTAN PA'I CHOS KYANG BYIS PA MGU BAR BYED KYI, 'PHAGS PA'I YE SHES RNAM PAR DGOD PA'I GTAM NI MIN NO,,
corpus_segments:30086.wylie: dper na smig chu ni chur med pas chur zhen pa'i ri dvags slu ba bzhin du bstan pa'i chos kyang byis pa mgu bar byed kyi, 'phags pa'i ye shes rnam par dgod pa'i gtam ni min no
corpus_segments:30086.english: There is, for example, no water in a mirage; but still a wild animal who sees it will hold strongly to the idea that it is water. Just so, there may be a teaching which was granted that pleases the infants, but which is talk that would never delight the wisdom of a realized being.

Just so, there may be a teaching which was granted that pleases the infants, but which is talk that would never delight the wisdom of a realized being."}

corpus_segments:30090.acip: DE LA DGONGS NAS GSUNGS PA'I DGOS PA NI BYIS PA RNAMS BDAG MED PAS 'JIGS PA SPANG BA DANG, MU STEGS BYED BDAG TU SMRA BA LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PA RNAMS DANG, SNGON DE'I LTA BA LA GOMS PAR BYAS PA RNAMS DE KHO NA NYID LA RIM GYIS DRANG BA'I PHYIR DU
corpus_segments:30090.wylie: de la dgongs nas gsungs pa'i dgos pa ni byis pa rnams bdag med pas 'jigs pa spang ba dang, mu stegs byed bdag tu smra ba la mngon par zhen pa rnams dang, sngon de'i lta ba la goms par byas pa rnams de kho na nyid la rim gyis drang ba'i phyir du
corpus_segments:30090.english: Why were these points then spoken of in terms of allusion? First of all, the Buddha wished to prevent any trepidation that the infants might feel towards the concept that things are not themselves. And he wanted to take those of the River Schools who were so attached to their profession of a self, and those who had, earlier, already accustomed themselves strongly to those ideas, and draw them out, gradually, to the idea of suchness.

corpus_segments:30091.acip: RTAG BRTAN THER ZUG GI SNYING PO YOD PAR BSTAN PAS 'DI LA DA LTAR DANG MA 'ONGS PA'I BYANG SEMS KYIS BDAG TU ZHEN PAR MI BYA BAR GSUNGS TE SGRAS ZIN LTAR GZUNG NA MU STEGS KYI BDAG LA ZHEN PA DANG 'DRA BAS SGRA JI BZHIN PAR ZHEN PAR MI BYA BA'I DON NO,,
corpus_segments:30091.wylie: rtag brtan ther zug gi snying po yod par bstan pas 'di la da ltar dang ma 'ongs pa'i byang sems kyis bdag tu zhen par mi bya bar gsungs te sgras zin ltar gzung na mu stegs kyi bdag la zhen pa dang 'dra bas sgra ji bzhin par zhen par mi bya ba'i don no
corpus_segments:30091.english: And so when we teach that there is a heart nature which is unchanging, stable, and solid, what we are really saying is that present and future bodhisattvas are not to feel any attachment to any self-nature here. If we do take the description of the heart as being something meant literally, then it would indeed end up similar to the attachment that the River Schools have towards some kind of self-nature. And so the point is that we need to avoid doing this.

corpus_segments:30232.acip: DES NA, BYIS PA RNAMS LA SNGON PO LA SOGS PA'I RANG BZHIN MTHONG BA YOD PA MIN TE, YUL RNAMS LA RANG GI NGO BO PHYIN CI LOG PA DAG TU MNGON PAR ZHEN PA'I GNAS SU GYUR PA 'DI NI, BYIS PA 'DI BDEN PAR ZHEN PA RNAMS LA SNANG BAR 'GYUR RO,,
corpus_segments:30232.wylie: des na, byis pa rnams la sngon po la sogs pa'i rang bzhin mthong ba yod pa min te, yul rnams la rang gi ngo bo phyin ci log pa dag tu mngon par zhen pa'i gnas su gyur pa 'di ni, byis pa 'di bden par zhen pa rnams la snang bar 'gyur ro
corpus_segments:30232.english: And for that reason, infants do not experience any sight towards the nature of things like blue and the rest; they live in a state where they have a craving for—they have a completely mistaken impression of—the real nature of the objects around them. This then is how things make their appearance to these infants, who crave some true existence to things.

corpus_segments:30340.acip: DE LTAR NA DE KHO NA NYID KYI DON GTAN LA PHAB PA GOMS PA LAS, RNAL 'BYOR PA 'PHAGS PA'I LAM MNGON SUM DU MDZAD PA'I MNYAM GZHAG GIS SNANG BA'I SPROS PA MA GZIGS PA'I TSUL GYIS DE KHO NA NYID GZIGS PA DE DAG LA CHOS GANG LA YANG BDEN PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA'I RTOG PA THOG MA MED PA NAS GOMS PA RNAMS LDOG PAR 'GYUR TE,
corpus_segments:30340.wylie: de ltar na de kho na nyid kyi don gtan la phab pa goms pa las, rnal 'byor pa 'phags pa'i lam mngon sum du mdzad pa'i mnyam gzhag gis snang ba'i spros pa ma gzigs pa'i tshul gyis de kho na nyid gzigs pa de dag la chos gang la yang bden par mngon par zhen pa'i rtog pa thog ma med pa nas goms pa rnams ldog par 'gyur te
corpus_segments:30340.english: And so it is that when they have accustomed ourselves to establishing just what it is that suchness refers to, the deep practitioner is able to go into a balanced meditation where they can manifest—directly—the path of a realized being. And then this meditation helps them to see suchness, in the manner of not seeing the various ways that things might appear to one as false elaborations. Thus then are such people able to put a stop to any habit of the kind that we have possessed for time with no beginning, of a notion where they feel strongly attached to the idea that any object at all could exist in truth.

And then this meditation helps them to see suchness, in the manner of not seeing the various ways that things might appear to one as false elaborations. Thus then are such people able to put a stop to any habit of the kind that we have possessed for time with no beginning, of a notion where they feel strongly attached to the idea that any object at all could exist in truth."}

corpus_segments:30351.acip: GAL TE DBU MA LA SEMS KYI RANG GI NGO BO'I BDAG NYID KYI DNGOS PO DON DAM PA CI YANG RUNG BA ZHIG YOD PAR GYUR NA NI, DE'I TSE DE LA YOD PAS RTAG GO ZHE'AM, MI RTAG GO ZHES BYA BAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA YANG JI LTAR MTHAR 'GYUR TE, DNGOS PO'I DE KHO NA NYID JI LTA BA BZHIN GYI RJES SU SONG ZHING TSUL BZHIN YID LA BYED PA NYID NI, LTUNG BA'I GNAS SO ZHES BYA BAR RIGS PA MA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS PA BZHIN NO,,
corpus_segments:30351.wylie: gal te dbu ma la sems kyi rang gi ngo bo'i bdag nyid kyi dngos po don dam pa ci yang rung ba zhig yod par gyur na ni, de'i tshe de la yod pas rtag go zhe'am, mi rtag go zhes bya bar mngon par zhen pa yang ji ltar mthar 'gyur te, dngos po'i de kho na nyid ji lta ba bzhin gyi rjes su song zhing tshul bzhin yid la byed pa nyid ni, ltung ba'i gnas so zhes bya bar rigs pa ma yin no, zhes gsungs pa bzhin no
corpus_segments:30351.english: If it were the case that in the middle way there could ever be some kind of ultimately existing entity with some essential nature of its own, then at that point there could exist with that the deluded belief that “this is unchanging,” or “this is changing”; which is to say, there would be a way of holding to an extreme. That is, if a person has reached a place where they see the suchness of entities just as it really is, and if they are thinking of that in a perfectly correct manner, then it would never be appropriate to say of them, “They are at a place where they could fall.”

That is, if a person has reached a place where they see the suchness of entities just as it really is, and if they are thinking of that in a perfectly correct manner, then it would never be appropriate to say of them, “They are at a place where they could fall.”"}

corpus_segments:30384.acip: 'JIG LTAS GZHI GANG LA ZHEN PA 'DI'I DMIGS PA GANG YIN SNYAM DU BRTAGS PA NA, BDAG STE NGA ZHES PA'I NGA NI BDAG TU LTA BA 'DI'I YUL DMIGS PA'O SNYAM DU RTOGS TE, NGAR 'DZIN PA NI BDAG GI YUL CAN YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
corpus_segments:30384.wylie: 'jig ltas gzhi gang la zhen pa 'di'i dmigs pa gang yin snyam du brtags pa na, bdag ste nga zhes pa'i nga ni bdag tu lta ba 'di'i yul dmigs pa'o snyam du rtogs te, ngar 'dzin pa ni bdag gi yul can yin pa'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:30384.english: One may wonder then just what kind of aspect it is that the view of destruction assumes, when it begins to hold its beliefs about any particular object. And what we come to realize is that what this view thinks it sees is what we have called “the self”—which is to say, a certain kind of “me.” It is the “me” which the view of some self thinks it is focused upon. And that is because the tendency to hold to “me” takes, as its object, a “self.”

corpus_segments:30417.wylie: rna ba la sogs pa'i dbang po lnga yid kyis byin gyis brlabs pas yongs su gzung ba'i yul sgra la sogs pa dag la blos zhen par byed la, de nas blos zhen par byas pa'i don la skyes bus sems par byed do
corpus_segments:30417.english: The ear and the rest of the five powers, inspired by the mental sense power, cause the mind to yearn towards sound and the rest: the objects that they hold. And then the soul turns its thoughts towards the objects that the mind has been yearning for.

And then the soul turns its thoughts towards the objects that the mind has been yearning for."}

corpus_segments:30477.acip: MU STEGS KYIS BTAGS PA LTAR GYI BDAG DE RIG PA MIN PA STE DE'I RNAM PAR MI 'DZIN PA'ANG MNGON PAR ZHEN PA'I KHYAD PAR LAS BDAG DANG BDAG GI ZHES BDAG TU LTA BAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
corpus_segments:30477.wylie: mu stegs kyis btags pa ltar gyi bdag de rig pa min pa ste de'i rnam par mi 'dzin pa'ang mngon par zhen pa'i khyad par las bdag dang bdag gi zhes bdag tu lta bar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:30477.english: Which is to say, that self as it is imagined by the River Schools is not something which could ever make sense. And that's because, if it could, then that would mean that even if then we didn't perceive any aspect of it, we could view something as the self—as being “self” or “something of the self”—simply by virtue of a strong wrong belief about it.

corpus_segments:30485.acip: SHES RAB CAN SU ZHIG MU STEGS PAS BTAGS PA'I BDAG RNAM PA DE LTA BU NGAR 'DZIN GYI RTEN DU ZHEN PAR BYED,

corpus_segments:30485.english: What person then of intelligence would get attached to thinking that the support for this kind of a tendency to hold to a “me” would necessarily have to be supplied by the type of self concocted by the River Schools?

corpus_segments:30495.english: They would state first that this object consists of all five of the parts to the person; and that when we say that someone is strongly attached to the idea of a self, this is something that comes from those same five parts.

corpus_segments:30602.acip: DE LTAR NYE BAR LEN PA PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MA DMIGS NA, BDAG DE'I NYE BAR BLANG BAR BYA BA PHUNG PO YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MA YIN NO, ZHES GZUGS SOGS LA YANG BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DOD CHAGS DANG BRAL BA 'THAD PA NYID DO,,
corpus_segments:30602.wylie: de ltar nye bar len pa po rang bzhin gyis grub pa ma dmigs na, bdag de'i nye bar blang bar bya ba phung po yang rang bzhin gyis yod pa ma yin no, zhes gzugs sogs la yang bden par zhen pa'i 'dod chags dang bral ba 'thad pa nyid do
corpus_segments:30602.english: And so what we have here is the statement, “Suppose then that the one who does take these things on could not be someone who existed through some nature of their own. We would have to say in that case that what they did take on—the parts to the person—could never be entities that existed through some nature of their own either.” In that case then it would be perfectly appropriate to say that we were free from the desire which is so hungry to believe that form and the rest are real.

corpus_segments:30731.acip: 'JIG LTA'I CHA NYI SHU PO DE DAG NI MDO LAS RNAM PAR BZHAG LA, DE LTAR 'JOG PA'I RGYU MTSAN NI SNGON DU PHUNG PO RNAMS MA BZUNG BAR 'JIG LTAS BDAG TU MNGON PAR ZHEN PAR MI NUS PAS, RNAM PA BZHI BZHI'I SGO NAS PHUNG PO RNAMS LA DMIGS SHING BDAG LA 'JUG GO
corpus_segments:30731.wylie: 'jig lta'i cha nyi shu po de dag ni mdo las rnam par bzhag la, de ltar 'jog pa'i rgyu mtshan ni sngon du phung po rnams ma bzung bar 'jig ltas bdag tu mngon par zhen par mi nus pas, rnam pa bzhi bzhi'i sgo nas phung po rnams la dmigs shing bdag la 'jug go
corpus_segments:30731.english: These twenty different divisions of the view of destruction are set forth in sutra. The reason for positing them this way is that—without first holding to the parts to the person—the view of destruction would be unable to hold the strong belief in a self. As such, we say that it focuses upon the parts to the person in four types each, and thus engages in the self.

corpus_segments:31763.english: What is the Reason for this? It is all because Those who are Not well versed Still possess A state of mind Where they have Strong craving. And because of this, They undergo Periods when they Are born & destroyed. They are torn From what feels Attractive, and Meet with The undesirable; They achieve The future fate of Those who still have Terrible deeds. The world Has crowded to Worthy objects Of compassion. As such, you— The Conqueror— Have, out of This compassion, Turned your heart Away from peace, Without allowing Yourself to go Into nirvana.

corpus_segments:31764.acip: GANG GI PHYIR NA DE KHO NA NYID KYI DON LA MI MKHAS PAS DNGOS PO LA BDEN PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA'I BLO CAN LAS 'BRAS LA YID CHES PAS LHA DANG MIR SKYE BA YOD PAR LTA BA RNAMS KYIS NI,
corpus_segments:31764.wylie: gang gi phyir na de kho na nyid kyi don la mi mkhas pas dngos po la bden par mngon par zhen pa'i blo can las 'bras la yid ches pas lha dang mir skye ba yod par lta ba rnams kyis ni
corpus_segments:31764.english: And what is the reason for this? It is all because those who are not well versed in the meaning of suchness still possess a state of mind where they have a strong craving for taking entities as existing in truth. Because of this, they put their faith in the laws of karma and its consequences, and thus believe that rebirths as a worldly god or human do exist.

corpus_segments:31767.acip: RGYU 'BRAS KYI DNGOS PO MED PAR ZHEN PA'I BLO CAN LOG PAR LTA BA DANG LDAN PAS NI, SDIG TO CAN GYI 'GRO BA DMYAL BA LA SOGS PA'I NGAN 'GRO DANG, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I SDUG BSNGAL YANG 'THOB PA DE'I PHYIR DANG,

corpus_segments:31767.english: Those who are possessed of wrong view, where they feel a craving for causes & effects which are not even actual things, end up achieving no more than the “future fate of those who still have terrible deeds”—a reference to the realms of hell, and other lower rebirths, along with all the sufferings that we described above.

This then is the one who completed this composition.

corpus_segments:34690.acip: GZHAN GYI SDUG BSNGAL GYIS BDAG LA MI GNOD PA RANG GI SDUG BSNGAL GYIS GZHAN LA MI, GNOD PA DANG 'DRA BAS DE CHED DU SEL BA RANG GI SDUG BSNGAL SEL BA DANG MTSUNGS PA MI, 'THAD DO ZHE NA SKYON MED DE GZHAN GYI SDUG BSNGAL GYIS RANG LA MI GNOD PA LTAR GAL, TE BDAG GI SDUG BSNGAL GYIS GZHAN GYI LUS LA MI GNOD PA DE LTA NA'ANG DE BDAG GI SDUG BSNGAL YIN TE RANG LA BDAG TU ZHEN PAS RANG GI SDUG BSNGAL MI BZOD PA 'BYUNG BA NYID YIN PA DE BZHIN DU SEMS CAN GZHAN YANG BDAG TU GZUNG BA GOMS PAS GZHAN GYI SDUG BSNGAL DAG BDAG LA 'BAB PAR MI 'GYUR YANG DE LTA NA'ANG SEMS CAN GYI SDUG BSNGAL DE BDAG GIS BSAL BAR BYA BA'I SDUG BSNGAL YIN TE SEMS CAN LA RANG GIS BDAG TU ZHEN PAS DE LA SDUG BSNGAL BYUNG NA BZOD PAR DKA' BAR 'GYUR RO
corpus_segments:34690.wylie: gzhan gyi sdug bsngal gyis bdag la mi gnod pa rang gi sdug bsngal gyis gzhan la mi, gnod pa dang 'dra bas de ched du sel ba rang gi sdug bsngal sel ba dang mtshungs pa mi, 'thad do zhe na skyon med de gzhan gyi sdug bsngal gyis rang la mi gnod pa ltar gal, te bdag gi sdug bsngal gyis gzhan gyi lus la mi gnod pa de lta na'ang de bdag gi sdug bsngal yin te rang la bdag tu zhen pas rang gi sdug bsngal mi bzod pa 'byung ba nyid yin pa de bzhin du sems can gzhan yang bdag tu gzung ba goms pas gzhan gyi sdug bsngal dag bdag la 'bab par mi 'gyur yang de lta na'ang sems can gyi sdug bsngal de bdag gis bsal bar bya ba'i sdug bsngal yin te sems can la rang gis bdag tu zhen pas de la sdug bsngal byung na bzod par dka' bar 'gyur ro
corpus_segments:34690.english: One may make yet another objection: Two facts here are the same: the pain that others have doesn't hurt me; and the pain that I have doesn't hurt others. Therefore you are incorrect when you say that I should make very intentional efforts to remove their pain in exactly the same way that I make efforts to remove my own pain. Yet there is no such problem in our reasoning. Suppose you do object this way, and say that your pain never hurts the body of another, any more than their pain hurts you. Even so, their pain is your pain. This is because your own pain is something you find unbearable for just one reason: your habit of grasping to yourself as yourself. Suppose that, just so, you become accustomed to consideringothers yourself as well. Even though it may be true then that the sufferings which others feel may never come and strike you personally, still the sufferingthat these livingbeings feel is your suffering to work to remove, since you'll find it hard to bear it when sufferings come to them, once you have learned to grasp to them as being Contemplation Five Logical proofs for compassion and love

corpus_segments:34982.acip: DAG SA LA GNAS PA'I BYANG SEMS RNAMS KYI RJES THOB KYI NGOR CHOS RNAMS BDEN GRUB, TU SNANG BA YOD KYANG ZHEN PA MED DE GNAS LUGS MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA'I SLOB PA 'PHAGS PA RNAMS LA GZUGS SOGS KYI CHOS RNAMS LA BDEN GRUB KYI SNANG ZHEN GNYIS KA MED PA'I PHYIR
corpus_segments:34982.wylie: dag sa la gnas pa'i byang sems rnams kyi rjes thob kyi ngor chos rnams bden grub, tu snang ba yod kyang zhen pa med de gnas lugs mngon sum du rtogs pa'i slob pa 'phags pa rnams la gzugs sogs kyi chos rnams la bden grub kyi snang zhen gnyis ka med pa'i phyir
corpus_segments:34982.english: Consider now bodhisattvas who have reached one of the pure levels. Even though objects appear to their minds, during what we call the "subsequent period," as something which exists truly, they have no belief in them this way. And this is because neither situation applies to realized beings who are not yet Buddhas and whoare perceiving the real nature of things directly; that is, physical matter and other objects do not appear to them as if they existed truly, and they do not believe that these objects exist that way.

corpus_segments:32289.acip: SBYIN PA SBYIN PA LA BRTZON PA LTA BU NI JI LTAR GNAS PAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON DANG, DE'I 'KHOR GSUM LA BDEN PAR MI ZHEN PA NI JI LTAR BSGRUB PAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON DANG, BDEN MED DU RTOGS PA'I BLO LA SEMS RTZE GCIG TU BYED PA NI SEMS RAB TU GZUNG BAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON DU BSHAD DE, PHAR PHYIN GZHAN LA'ANG SBYAR BAR BYA'O,,
corpus_segments:32289.wylie: sbyin pa sbyin pa la brtson pa lta bu ni ji ltar gnas par bya zhes pa'i don dang, de'i 'khor gsum la bden par mi zhen pa ni ji ltar bsgrub par bya zhes pa'i don dang, bden med du rtogs pa'i blo la sems rtse gcig tu byed pa ni sems rab tu gzung bar bya zhes pa'i don du bshad de, phar phyin gzhan la'ang sbyar bar bya'o
corpus_segments:32289.english: There are a number of expressions here. One is that “We should stay in our giving just as those who are striving in their giving.” Another is “We should try to practice in a way where we have no belief that the three spheres of this act are real.” And they are both to be explained as meaning “Maintain, perfectly, a state of mind where you are single-pointedly absorbed in the understanding that nothing is true.”

corpus_segments:32292.acip: RAB 'BYOR CHOS THAMS CAD THA SNYAD BTAGS PA TZAM DU YOD PA MA GTOGS, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA RDUL TZAM YANG MED PA'I PHYIR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA NI PHYIN CI LOG TU ZHEN PA YIN PAS,
corpus_segments:32292.wylie: rab 'byor chos thams cad tha snyad btags pa tsam du yod pa ma gtogs, rang bzhin gyis grub pa rdul tsam yang med pa'i phyir rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa ni phyin ci log tu zhen pa yin pas
corpus_segments:32292.english: And what Lord Buddha is saying then is: “O Subhuti, every single object in the universe exists only through our projections; they have not a single atom of any other kind of existence—any natural existence. As such, anyone who holds that things could exist through any nature of their own is entertaining a belief which is completely mistaken.

corpus_segments:32293.acip: CI NAS KYANG RANG BZHIN KYIS GRUB PAR ZHEN PA'I MTSAN MAR 'DZIN PA'I 'DU SHES LA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPAS GNAS PAR MI BYA'O,,
corpus_segments:32293.wylie: ci nas kyang rang bzhin kyis grub par zhen pa'i mtshan mar 'dzin pa'i 'du shes la byang chub sems dpas gnas par mi bya'o
corpus_segments:32293.english: “And bodhisattvas never stay in any kind of conception where they hold to the signs of things: where they believe in any way at all that things could exist through any nature of their own.”

corpus_segments:32413.acip: YANG DAG PA'I 'DU SHES ZHES BSHAD PA GANG YIN PA DE NI BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DU SHES MA MCHIS PA'I SLAD DU STE, DES NA BDEN ZHEN MED CING BDEN MED RTOGS PA'I 'DU SHES DE LA YANG DAG PA'I 'DU SHES ZHES DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS SO,,
corpus_segments:32413.wylie: yang dag pa'i 'du shes zhes bshad pa gang yin pa de ni bden par zhen pa'i 'du shes ma mchis pa'i slad du ste, des na bden zhen med cing bden med rtogs pa'i 'du shes de la yang dag pa'i 'du shes zhes de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs so
corpus_segments:32413.english: And this is because this same “correct thinking” is something that could never exist as a kind of thinking where one believed in things as being real. This is precisely why Those Gone Thus have used the expression “thinking correctly” to describe a kind of thinking where one no longer believes in things as being real: where one rather thinks in a way where they have realized that things have no reality.

This is precisely why Those Gone Thus have used the expression “thinking correctly” to describe a kind of thinking where one no longer believes in things as being real: where one rather thinks in a way where they have realized that things have no reality."}

corpus_segments:32423.acip: NGAS BZOD PA'I 'KHOR GSUM BDEN MED DU SHES NAS BZOD PA BSGOMS PAS, THA SNYAD PA'I NGA LA DMIGS NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU BDAG TU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DU SHES NAS GANG ZAG TU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DU SHES KYANG MA BYUNG ZHING,
corpus_segments:32423.wylie: ngas bzod pa'i 'khor gsum bden med du shes nas bzod pa bsgoms pas, tha snyad pa'i nga la dmigs nas nga'o snyam du bdag tu bden par zhen pa'i 'du shes nas gang zag tu bden par zhen pa'i 'du shes kyang ma byung zhing
corpus_segments:32423.english: At that moment I practiced patience, keeping my mind on an understanding of the lack of true existence to each of the three elements to the act of patience. As I focused on the “me” which exists nominally, there came into my mind no conception where I held any belief in some truly existing “me”: and so I had no conception of anything from a truly existing “self” up to a truly existing “person.”

As I focused on the “me” which exists nominally, there came into my mind no conception where I held any belief in some truly existing “me”: and so I had no conception of anything from a truly existing “self” up to a truly existing “person.”"}

corpus_segments:32429.acip: NGA'O SNYAM PA'I BDAG TU ZHEN PA YOD NA GNOD SEMS SOGS 'BYUNG BA NI, RNAM 'GREL LAS, ,BDAG YOD NA NI GZHAN DU SHES, ,BDAG GZHAN CHA LA 'DZIN DANG SDANG, ,'DI DAG DANG NI YONGS 'BREL BAS, ,NYES PA THAMS CAD 'BYUNG BAR 'GYUR, ,ZHES BSHAD PA BZHIN NO,,
corpus_segments:32429.wylie: nga'o snyam pa'i bdag tu zhen pa yod na gnod sems sogs 'byung ba ni, rnam 'grel las, ,bdag yod na ni gzhan du shes, ,bdag gzhan cha la 'dzin dang sdang, ,'di dag dang ni yongs 'brel bas, ,nyes pa thams cad 'byung bar 'gyur, ,zhes bshad pa bzhin no
corpus_segments:32429.english: On this idea that—if we entertain some belief in a self where we say to ourselves, “This is me, ” we will begin as well to entertain thoughts of harming someone—the Commentary on Valid Perception states: Once there is a self, There is the idea of “other”; And then we hold tight To the “self” side And we feel dislike For the “other” side. Once we become enmeshed In these two different sides, Every other problem possible Then starts to come to us.

corpus_segments:32520.acip: RAB 'BYOR BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG ZHIG 'DI SNYAM DU, BDAG GIS GANG DU 'TSANG RGYA BA'I GNAS KYI ZHING GI BKOD PA PHUN SUM TSOGS PA RNAM PAR DON DAM PAR BSGRUB PAR BYA'O ZHES ZHEN CING TSIG GIS ZER NA, DE YANG DE BZHIN DU BRJOD CING ZHEN PAR BYAR MI RUNG NGO,,
corpus_segments:32520.wylie: rab 'byor byang chub sems dpa' gang zhig 'di snyam du, bdag gis gang du 'tshang rgya ba'i gnas kyi zhing gi bkod pa phun sum tshogs pa rnam par don dam par bsgrub par bya'o zhes zhen cing tshig gis zer na, de yang de bzhin du brjod cing zhen par byar mi rung ngo
corpus_segments:32520.english: And suppose, o Subhuti, that some bodhisattva were to think to themselves, “I am working to bring about a perfect paradise, the place where I will become enlightened, in a way which is ultimately real.” That is, suppose they were to entertain this kind of belief, and express it in their words. That too would not be spoken rightly; it would not be a right sort of belief.

That too would not be spoken rightly; it would not be a right sort of belief."}

corpus_segments:32608.acip: GAL TE DE LTA BU'I BLO ZHIG DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA YOD NA NI, DE NYID DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I BDAG DANG SEMS CAN DANG GANG ZAG DANG SROG TU BDEN PAR 'DZIN PA'I SKYON DU 'GYUR NA, DE NI MI RIGS TE, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA BDAG TU 'DZIN CING ZHEN PA SOGS MED PA'I PHYIR TE, DES BDAG TU 'DZIN PA'I MNGON ZHEN THAMS CAD SPANGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
corpus_segments:32608.wylie: gal te de lta bu'i blo zhig de bzhin gshegs pa la yod na ni, de nyid de bzhin gshegs pa'i bdag dang sems can dang gang zag dang srog tu bden par 'dzin pa'i skyon du 'gyur na, de ni mi rigs te, de bzhin gshegs pa la bdag tu 'dzin cing zhen pa sogs med pa'i phyir te, des bdag tu 'dzin pa'i mngon zhen thams cad spangs pa'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:32608.english: If the One Thus Gone ever did entertain this state of mind, there would be the problem that he would be grasping to some self of the One Gone Thus, and to some living being, or to some person, or else to something that lives, of the One Gone Thus. And that would be wrong, for the fact is that the One Gone Thus doesn't have any of these thoughts—any of this grasping to a self, or to any of the rest. This is because he has given up each and every form of the belief where we grasp to some self.

And that would be wrong, for the fact is that the One Gone Thus doesn't have any of these thoughts—any of this grasping to a self, or to any of the rest. This is because he has given up each and every form of the belief where we grasp to some self."}

corpus_segments:32631.acip: MDOR NA, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA MING DANG GZUGS KYI SKUR BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I BDEN 'DZIN GYIS BCINGS PA DE DAG NI, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I CHOS KYI SKU LTA BA LA LOG PAR ZHUGS PA STE, SKYE BO DE DAG GIS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA NGA'I CHOS KYI SKU STONG PA NYID MI MTHONG NGO,,
corpus_segments:32631.wylie: mdor na, de bzhin gshegs pa la ming dang gzugs kyi skur bden par zhen pa'i bden 'dzin gyis bcings pa de dag ni, de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos kyi sku lta ba la log par zhugs pa ste, skye bo de dag gis de bzhin gshegs pa nga'i chos kyi sku stong pa nyid mi mthong ngo
corpus_segments:32631.english: Which is to say—if we were to put it briefly—let us consider those who are shackled by the tendency to look upon the One Gone Thus and believe that he exists, in some real way, within either his name or his body of form. Such persons would be living in error as far as how they were viewing the reality body. People like this can't see me—that is, cannot see the reality body, or emptiness, that belongs to “me”: to the One Gone Thus.

corpus_segments:32650.acip: DES NA THA SNYAD DU BSOD NAMS YONGS SU GZUNG BA ZHES BYA'O ZHES GSUNGS TE, 'DI'I GZUNG BAR MI BYA'O ZHES PAS BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO LA BDEN GRUB TU ZHEN PA'I RTAG LTA DANG, YONGS SU GZUNG MOD KYIS ZHES CHAD PAR LTA BA SEL LO,,
corpus_segments:32650.wylie: des na tha snyad du bsod nams yongs su gzung ba zhes bya'o zhes gsungs te, 'di'i gzung bar mi bya'o zhes pas bsod nams kyi phung po la bden grub tu zhen pa'i rtag lta dang, yongs su gzung mod kyis zhes chad par lta ba sel lo
corpus_segments:32650.english: And this is precisely why, Lord Buddha says, that—nominally speaking—we can call it “gathering the merit in.” When the sutra says here that we are “not to gather,” it is helping us to avoid the view that things are unchanging—where we believe that the mountains of merit exist in truth. When it says that we “should, of course, gather,” then it is helping us to avoid the view that things have simply stopped. The Buddha neither comes nor goes

corpus_segments:36520.acip: BYIS PA RNAMS KYIS RTEN 'BREL GYI MING NYID LAS RANG BZHIN DANG BCAS PA ZHEN PA'I PHYIR 'PHAGS PA'I GZIGS PA LA BLTOS NAS NI RTEN 'BYUNG RANG BZHIN MED PAR CHES GSAL BAR KHONG DU CHUD NUS SO ZHES BSTAN PA'I PHYIR,

corpus_segments:36520.english: As soon as infants only hear the word "dependence," they immediately hold on to the idea that it possesses some sort of self-nature. And so we can ourselves conclude with absolute clarity that-relative to the way a realized being sees things-dependence has no nature of its own. In order to convey this thought, Master Nagarjuna gives us the next verse of the root text.

corpus_segments:36661.english: The fact is that Lord Buddha did talk about a cycle of pain, and a nirvana where we escape it, in a way where these two seemed to exist in & of themselves; he did this in order to overcome the feelings of certain students who had a strong belief that things existed in this way. He was accepting such terms only in the perceptions of those to whom he was giving these teachings.

corpus_segments:36666.english: Let's consider realized beings: those people who are directly seeing suchness-the way things really are. They have no delusions about what is the world-what is to be abandoned; or what is nirvana-what we need to achieve. That is, they have no belief in these things as having their own nature: they are not entertaining these kinds of deluded ideas about the cycle & nirvana.

corpus_segments:21844.acip: SBYIN PA SBYIN PA LA BRTZON PA LTA BU NI JI LTAR GNAS PAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON DANG, DE'I 'KHOR GSUM LA BDEN PAR MI ZHEN PA NI JI LTAR BSGRUB PAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON DANG, BDEN MED DU RTOGS PA'I BLO LA SEMS RTZE GCIG TU BYED PA NI SEMS RAB TU GZUNG BAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON DU BSHAD DE, PHAR PHYIN GZHAN LA'ANG SBYAR BAR BYA'O,,
corpus_segments:21844.wylie: sbyin pa sbyin pa la brtson pa lta bu ni ji ltar gnas par bya zhes pa'i don dang, de'i 'khor gsum la bden par mi zhen pa ni ji ltar bsgrub par bya zhes pa'i don dang, bden med du rtogs pa'i blo la sems rtse gcig tu byed pa ni sems rab tu gzung bar bya zhes pa'i don du bshad de, phar phyin gzhan la'ang sbyar bar bya'o
corpus_segments:21844.english: There are a number of expressions here. One is that "We should stay in our giving just as those who are striving in their giving." Another is "We should try to practice in a way where we have no belief that the three spheres of this act are real." And they are both to be explained as meaning "Maintain, perfectly, a state of mind where you are single-pointedly absorbed in the understanding that nothing is true."

One is that \"We should stay in our giving just as those who are striving in their giving.\" Another is \"We should try to practice in a way where we have no belief that the three spheres of this act are real.\" And they are both to be explained as meaning \"Maintain, perfectly, a state of mind where you are single-pointedly absorbed in the understanding that nothing is true.\""}

corpus_segments:21848.acip: RAB 'BYOR CHOS THAMS CAD THA SNYAD BTAGS PA TZAM DU YOD PA MA GTOGS, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA RDUL TZAM YANG MED PA'I PHYIR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA NI PHYIN CI LOG TU ZHEN PA YIN PAS,
corpus_segments:21848.wylie: rab 'byor chos thams cad tha snyad btags pa tsam du yod pa ma gtogs, rang bzhin gyis grub pa rdul tsam yang med pa'i phyir rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa ni phyin ci log tu zhen pa yin pas
corpus_segments:21848.english: And what Lord Buddha is saying then is: "O Subhuti, every single object in the universe exists only through our projections; they have not a single atom of any other kind of existence—any natural existence. As such, anyone who holds that things could exist through any nature of their own is entertaining a belief which is completely mistaken.

As such, anyone who holds that things could exist through any nature of their own is entertaining a belief which is completely mistaken."}

corpus_segments:21849.acip: CI NAS KYANG RANG BZHIN KYIS GRUB PAR ZHEN PA'I MTSAN MAR 'DZIN PA'I 'DU SHES LA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPAS GNAS PAR MI BYA'O,,
corpus_segments:21849.wylie: ci nas kyang rang bzhin kyis grub par zhen pa'i mtshan mar 'dzin pa'i 'du shes la byang chub sems dpas gnas par mi bya'o
corpus_segments:21849.english: "And bodhisattvas never stay in any kind of conception where they hold to the signs of things: where they believe in any way at all that things could exist through any nature of their own."
corpus_segments:21849.raw: {"course": "Sunlight", "acip": "CI NAS KYANG RANG BZHIN KYIS GRUB PAR ZHEN PA'I MTSAN MAR 'DZIN PA'I 'DU SHES LA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPAS GNAS PAR MI BYA'O,,", "wylie": "ci nas kyang rang bzhin kyis grub par zhen pa'i mtshan mar 'dzin pa'i 'du shes la byang chub sems dpas gnas par mi bya'o", "english": "\"And bodhisattvas never stay in any kind of conception where they hold to the signs of things: where they believe in any way at all that things could exist through any nature of their own.\""}

corpus_segments:21984.acip: MI SKYE BA'I CHOS LA BZOD PA THOB PAS CHOS THAMS CAD BDEN MED DU MNGON SUM DU GZIGS SHING GANG LUNG BSTAN PA DANG THOB PAR BYA BA DANG 'TSANG RGYA BAR 'GYUR BA THAMS CAD KYANG RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG PAR GZIGS PAS, MAR ME MDZAD LAS BDEN GRUB KYI CHOS GANG YANG BLANGS SNYAM DU ZHEN PA MED DO,,
corpus_segments:21984.wylie: mi skye ba'i chos la bzod pa thob pas chos thams cad bden med du mngon sum du gzigs shing gang lung bstan pa dang thob par bya ba dang 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ba thams cad kyang rang bzhin gyis stong par gzigs pas, mar me mdzad las bden grub kyi chos gang yang blangs snyam du zhen pa med do
corpus_segments:21984.english: When one reaches the stage of the great mastery of things that never grow, one directly perceives that no object at all has any true existence. One perceives that what was predicted to finally happen, and the thing one is to achieve, and becoming enlightened—all of them—are empty of any natural existence. As such the Buddha had no belief that he was taking up any truly existing Dharma at all from the Buddha, Light Maker.

corpus_segments:22073.acip: YANG DAG PA'I 'DU SHES ZHES BSHAD PA GANG YIN PA DE NI BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DU SHES MA MCHIS PA'I SLAD DU STE, DES NA BDEN ZHEN MED CING BDEN MED RTOGS PA'I 'DU SHES DE LA YANG DAG PA'I 'DU SHES ZHES DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS SO,,
corpus_segments:22073.wylie: yang dag pa'i 'du shes zhes bshad pa gang yin pa de ni bden par zhen pa'i 'du shes ma mchis pa'i slad du ste, des na bden zhen med cing bden med rtogs pa'i 'du shes de la yang dag pa'i 'du shes zhes de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs so
corpus_segments:22073.english: And this is because this same "correct thinking" is something that could never exist as a kind of thinking where one believed in things as being real. This is precisely why Those Gone Thus have used the expression "thinking correctly" to describe a kind of thinking where one no longer believes in things as being real: where one rather thinks in a way where they have realized that things have no reality.

corpus_segments:22098.acip: NGAS BZOD PA'I 'KHOR GSUM BDEN MED DU SHES NAS BZOD PA BSGOMS PAS, THA SNYAD PA'I NGA LA DMIGS NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU BDAG TU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DU SHES NAS GANG ZAG TU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DU SHES KYANG MA BYUNG
corpus_segments:22098.wylie: ngas bzod pa'i 'khor gsum bden med du shes nas bzod pa bsgoms pas, tha snyad pa'i nga la dmigs nas nga'o snyam du bdag tu bden par zhen pa'i 'du shes nas gang zag tu bden par zhen pa'i 'du shes kyang ma byung
corpus_segments:22098.english: ZHING,At that moment I practiced patience, keeping my mind on an understanding of the lack of true existence to each of the three elements to the act of patience. As I focused on the "me" which exists nominally, there came into my mind no conception where I held any belief in some truly existing "me": and so I had no conception of anything from a truly existing "self" up to a truly existing "person."[320]

corpus_segments:22107.english: On this idea that—if we entertain some belief in a self where we say to ourselves, "This is me, " we will begin as well to entertain thoughts of harming someone—the Commentary on Valid Perception states: Once there is a self,There is the idea of "other";And then we hold tightTo the "self" sideAnd we feel dislikeFor the "other" side.Once we become enmeshedIn these two different sides,Every other problem possibleThen starts to come to us.[106]

corpus_segments:22238.acip: RAB 'BYOR BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG ZHIG 'DI SNYAM DU, BDAG GIS GANG DU 'TSANG RGYA BA'I GNAS KYI ZHING GI BKOD PA PHUN SUM TSOGS PA RNAM PAR DON DAM PAR BSGRUB PAR BYA'O ZHES ZHEN CING TSIG GIS ZER NA, DE YANG DE BZHIN DU BRJOD CING ZHEN PAR BYAR MI RUNG NGO,,And suppose, o Subhuti,
corpus_segments:22238.wylie: rab 'byor byang chub sems dpa' gang zhig 'di snyam du, bdag gis gang du 'tshang rgya ba'i gnas kyi zhing gi bkod pa phun sum tshogs pa rnam par don dam par bsgrub par bya'o zhes zhen cing tshig gis zer na, de yang de bzhin du brjod cing zhen par byar mi rung ngo,,aND SuppoSe, o subhuTi
corpus_segments:22238.english: that some bodhisattva were to think to themselves, "I am working to bring about a perfect paradise, the place where I will become enlightened, in a way which is ultimately real." That is, suppose they were to entertain this kind of belief, and express it in their words. That too would not be spoken rightly; it would not be a right sort of belief.[443]

corpus_segments:22347.acip: GAL TE DE LTA BU'I BLO ZHIG DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA YOD NA NI, DE NYID DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I BDAG DANG SEMS CAN DANG GANG ZAG DANG SROG TU BDEN PAR 'DZIN PA'I SKYON DU 'GYUR NA, DE NI MI RIGS TE, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA BDAG TU 'DZIN CING ZHEN PA SOGS MED PA'I PHYIR TE, DES BDAG TU 'DZIN PA'I MNGON ZHEN THAMS CAD SPANGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,If the One Thus Gone
corpus_segments:22347.wylie: gal te de lta bu'i blo zhig de bzhin gshegs pa la yod na ni, de nyid de bzhin gshegs pa'i bdag dang sems can dang gang zag dang srog tu bden par 'dzin pa'i skyon du 'gyur na, de ni mi rigs te, de bzhin gshegs pa la bdag tu 'dzin cing zhen pa sogs med pa'i phyir te, des bdag tu 'dzin pa'i mngon zhen thams cad spangs pa'i phyir ro,,if The oNe thuS goNe
corpus_segments:22347.english: ever did entertain this state of mind, there would be the problem that he would be grasping to some self of the One Gone Thus, and to some living being, or to some person, or else to something that lives, of the One Gone Thus. And that would be wrong, for the fact is that the One Gone Thus doesn't have any of these thoughts—any of this grasping to a self, or to any of the rest. This is because he has given up each and every form of the belief where we grasp to some self.[528]

corpus_segments:22376.acip: MDOR NA, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA MING DANG GZUGS KYI SKUR BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I BDEN 'DZIN GYIS BCINGS PA DE DAG NI, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I CHOS KYI SKU LTA BA LA LOG PAR ZHUGS PA STE, SKYE BO DE DAG GIS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA NGA'I CHOS KYI SKU STONG PA NYID MI MTHONG NGO,,Which is to say—if we
corpus_segments:22376.wylie: mdor na, de bzhin gshegs pa la ming dang gzugs kyi skur bden par zhen pa'i bden 'dzin gyis bcings pa de dag ni, de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos kyi sku lta ba la log par zhugs pa ste, skye bo de dag gis de bzhin gshegs pa nga'i chos kyi sku stong pa nyid mi mthong ngo,,which iS To Say—if we
corpus_segments:22376.english: were to put it briefly—let us consider those who are shackled by the tendency to look upon the One Gone Thus and believe that he exists, in some real way, within either his name or his body of form. Such persons would be living in error as far as how they were viewing the reality body. People like this can't see me—that is, cannot see the reality body, or emptiness, that belongs to "me": to the One Gone Thus.[553]

corpus_segments:22401.acip: DES NA THA SNYAD DU BSOD NAMS YONGS SU GZUNG BA ZHES BYA'O ZHES GSUNGS TE, 'DI'I GZUNG BAR MI BYA'O ZHES PAS BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO LA BDEN GRUB TU ZHEN PA'I RTAG LTA DANG, YONGS SU GZUNG MOD KYIS ZHES CHAD PAR
corpus_segments:22401.wylie: des na tha snyad du bsod nams yongs su gzung ba zhes bya'o zhes gsungs te, 'di'i gzung bar mi bya'o zhes pas bsod nams kyi phung po la bden grub tu zhen pa'i rtag lta dang, yongs su gzung mod kyis zhes chad par
corpus_segments:22401.english: LTA BA SEL LO,,And this is precisely why, Lord Buddha says, that—nominally speaking—we can call it "gathering the merit in." When the sutra says here that we are "not to gather," it is helping us to avoid the view that things are unchanging—where we believe that the mountains of merit exist in truth. When it says that we "should, of course, gather," then it is helping us to avoid the view that things have simply stopped. The Buddha neither comes nor goes

corpus_segments:9190.acip: ,BAN BUN GYI 'JIG RTEN BYA BA 'DI, ,AA 'THAS SU ZHEN PAS SDUG LA BKOD, ,BAG CHAGS KYIS BSLAD PA'I RMI LAM BZHIN, ,NYIN MTSAN KUN 'KHRUL PA'I BYA BAS 'DAS,

corpus_segments:9190.english: You rush here and there in your worldly work; believe it is something worth something, but it sends you to pain. A dream you once had because of some random thoughts; a life of days and nights spent chasing a mirage.

corpus_segments:9609.english: If in that hour you leave behind Even the name you used to be called, Then what need mention everything else? Oh here we are, me and the others of you Who perhaps are the same as me myself, Ignoring this one great terror to come, Completely engrossed in this life's affairs, Which having nothing to do with anything. Come please look after us, I pray, My Lama, look on us with love; We are every suffering person there is, And we have no one else to help us. * * * To Give Up Every Hope With this class we reach the final section in our review of the root bodhisattva vows.  This includes the last transgression of all, which is that unthinkable act of deciding that your will not one day become and enlightened Angel who can travel to all worlds and help all living beings.

corpus_segments:11008.wylie: thun mong ma yin pa rlung la ngag tu gsungs pa'i dri ma rlung sngags so sor snang zhing zhen pa'i dri ma 'khrud pas na gsung rdo rje sbyong
corpus_segments:11008.english: The unique result of this initiation is that cleaned free the diamond of your words: your enlightened speech.  You are cleaned of a very special impurity relating to the statement that "the inner winds are what you say"; that is, you are cleaned of the tendency for your inner winds and your mantras to appear to you as things which are separate from each other--and you are cleaned of your tendency to believe it when they appear this way.

corpus_segments:11702.acip: ,GZHUG PA TZAM LA NI SNOD DANG LDAN MI LDAN BRTAG MI DGOS PAR GSUNGS TE RTZE MO LAS, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA THAMS CAD KYI GSANG BA'I DKYIL 'KHOR GYI RGYAL PO CHEN PO 'DIR NI MA LUS SHING LUS PA MED PA'I SEMS CAN GYI KHAMS THAMS CAD 'JUG TU RUNG NGO, ,SNOD DANG SNOD MA YIN PA YONGS SU BRTAG PAR MI BYA STE, GZHUG PA LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PA YONGS SU GZUNG BAR BYA'O, ,DE CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYIS MTHONG BA TZAM GYI MOD LA PHYIR MI LDOG PA NYID DU 'GYUR RO, ,DAD PA MED PA DANG DGE BA'I RTZA BA MA BSAGS PA DANG RGYUD YONGS SU MA SMIN PA DANG MOS PA MED PA MANG DU ZIN KYANG 'ON KYANG MTHONG BA TZAM GYIS SO, ,ZHES GSUNGS TE DKYIL 'KHOR DU GZHUG PA DANG ZHUGS PA LA DBANG BSKUR BA GNYIS LAS GZHUG PA NI SNOD DANG MI LDAN PA LA'ANG MA BKAG PA YIN GYI DBANG BSKUR BA MI 'GOG PA NI MIN,
corpus_segments:11702.wylie: gzhug pa tsam la ni snod dang ldan mi ldan brtag mi dgos par gsungs te rtse mo las, de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi gsang ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi rgyal po chen po 'dir ni ma lus shing lus pa med pa'i sems can gyi khams thams cad 'jug tu rung ngo, ,snod dang snod ma yin pa yongs su brtag par mi bya ste, gzhug pa la mngon par zhen pa yongs su gzung bar bya'o, ,de ci'i phyir zhe na, sems can thams cad kyis mthong ba tsam gyi mod la phyir mi ldog pa nyid du 'gyur ro, ,dad pa med pa dang dge ba'i rtsa ba ma bsags pa dang rgyud yongs su ma smin pa dang mos pa med pa mang du zin kyang 'on kyang mthong ba tsam gyis so, ,zhes gsungs te dkyil 'khor du gzhug pa dang zhugs pa la dbang bskur ba gnyis las gzhug pa ni snod dang mi ldan pa la'ang ma bkag pa yin gyi dbang bskur ba mi 'gog pa ni min
corpus_segments:11702.english: It is stated in scripture that--in a case where we are bringing the person into the secret world, and nothing more--then we need not examine them to see whether or not they are a proper vessel to actually fully enter into the secret teachings.  As the Tip of Diamond says, It is completely proper for every living being--each and every living being, of every different propensity--to enter into this great king, this secret world of all the Ones who have Gone To Bliss.  You need not perform that examination to see whether or not they are a worthy vessel; lead them in, anyone who has a true desire to do so. Why is this so?  Because in the very instant that any single living being in the entire universe lays eyes upon this world, the seed in them becomes totally unstoppable.  They may be someone who has a great many problems: they may be a person with no faith at all; or someone who has failed to collect any quantity of good karma at all; or whose heart is not at all ripened; or who simply has no interest in these things.  But still they become unstoppable, simply by laying eyes upon this world. And so there are two possibilities here: simply bringing someone into the secret world, or empowering them to enter the secret world.  The former of the two is not disallowed, even for those who are not a worthy vessel.  This is not of course to say that it is not disallowed to grant such a person empowerment. ***

corpus_segments:11768.english: The first section of the second part of the secret book called Samputa says, Abandoning any hope of being acknowledged, Take any little beautiful thing you find And present it into your Lama's hands. The Lama too, out of sheer compassion, Should accept the gift, thinking that this Will be of benefit for the disciple, And help them prevent attachment. ***
