corpus_segments:11864.acip: SH'AN+TI PAS RTZOD PA'I DUS 'DIR 'GRO BA RNAMS BUD MED LA RAB TU ZHEN PAS, DE RNAMS GDUL PA'I PHYIR BUD MED DU SPRUL PA'I LHA RNAMS 'DI NA GNAS PAS MI SMOD CES SAM BUD MED KYI KHROD NA RDO RJE PHAG MO SOGS GNAS PAS DES NA GANG YIN MI SHES PAS BUD MED RNAMS LA MI SMOD PAR BZHED PA'I PHYIR BCAS PA'I SPYI MTSAMS 'DZIN PA LA BUD MED TZAM NAS BYED PAR GSAL LO,
corpus_segments:11864.wylie: shAn+ti pas rtsod pa'i dus 'dir 'gro ba rnams bud med la rab tu zhen pas, de rnams gdul pa'i phyir bud med du sprul pa'i lha rnams 'di na gnas pas mi smod ces sam bud med kyi khrod na rdo rje phag mo sogs gnas pas des na gang yin mi shes pas bud med rnams la mi smod par bzhed pa'i phyir bcas pa'i spyi mtshams 'dzin pa la bud med tsam nas byed par gsal lo
corpus_segments:11864.english: Shantipa here points out that "Here in the days of strife, people have a particular attachment to the female form; and so in order to tame these beings, Angels emanate as human women.  They are then here in the world with us, and we must never disparage Them."  So too we see, "Holy beings like the Diamond Sow are present here in the world, mixed among the human women.  As such, we never know which woman might be Them; and so we should never disparage women." Given this view of the vow, it is clear that the overall constraints of the rule refer only to women, [and not to men]. ***

corpus_segments:12027.english: These lines are saying that one should live in such a way that you pass your hours with your Messenger, enjoying this sacred practice.  And you should do so "always," meaning constantly.  The practice should as well be done out of a love for the goal of reaching freedom.  You must, finally, assure that no one every ever leads you away from this particular path: and this then is the fourth of the pledges. ************

corpus_segments:12333.acip: SNANG BA DE'I GNYEN POR DAG PA'I RTEN DANG BRTEN PAR 'CHAR BA'I SNANG BA DANG , THA MAL GYI ZHEN PA'I GNYEN POR DAG PA'I RTEN DANG BRTEN PA'I NGA RGYAL SGOM PA YIN LA, DE YANG NGA RGYAL SGOM PA NI GTZO BO DANG , SNANG BA SGOM PA NI DE'I YAN LAG YIN PAR GSUNGS SO,,
corpus_segments:12333.wylie: snang ba de'i gnyen por dag pa'i rten dang brten par 'char ba'i snang ba dang , tha mal gyi zhen pa'i gnyen por dag pa'i rten dang brten pa'i nga rgyal sgom pa yin la, de yang nga rgyal sgom pa ni gtso bo dang , snang ba sgom pa ni de'i yan lag yin par gsungs so
corpus_segments:12333.english: The antidote for things appearing as normal is to purposely bring to mind a world and its inhabitants which appear as totally pure.  The antidote for our tendency to see things as normal is to practice identifying ourselves with the divine, living in a divine world inhabited by beings who are divine.  It is stated that this identification with the divine is the main thing, and that bringing to mind the appearance of things as being pure is auxiliary to it.

It is stated that this identification with the divine is the main thing, and that bringing to mind the appearance of things as being pure is auxiliary to it."}

corpus_segments:12430.acip: RANG BZHIN GYI BZLAS PA RLUNG LDANG 'JUG GNAS GSUM NI DBEN GZHI'I NGAG DANG , DE GSUM DANG YI GE GSUM GYI GDANGS THA DAD DU ZHEN PA NI DBEN RGYU'I DGAG BYA DANG , RLUNG LDANG 'JUG GNAS GSUM GYI GDANGS DANG YI GE GSUM GYI GDANGS DBYER MI PHYED PAR SBYOR BA NI DBEN PA'I DON YIN PA'I PHYIR DANG ,

corpus_segments:12430.english: And this is the case because the speech here which is transcendent is the natural recitation: the three steps of the rising, the entering, and the staying of the inner winds.  And what we seek to transcend--the thing we wish to stop--is our tendency to believe that these three are somehow things which are different from the song of the three syllables.  The essence of transcendence here then is where the song of the rising, the entering, and the staying of the winds is joined indivisibly with the song of the three syllables.

corpus_segments:13564.acip: KHO NA RE, ,SGYU LUS ZHEN PA MED GYI MDA', ,'OD GSAL NYAMS KYIS GZHU BKANG NAS, ,NGAR 'DZIN LUS KYI RI BO LA, ,BZUNG 'DZIN RI DVAGS RGYUG PA DE, ,BSOD LAS MOS PA'I RNGON PA BDAG ,SANG NI NYA PA RGYA MTSO SNYOG ZER, MI SNANG BAR GYUR TO, YANG SANG GSOL BA 'DEBS BZHIN TSOL DU PHYIN PAS,

corpus_segments:13564.english: And the Dark Man says to Him, The wild deer Of holding that what we see And the one that sees it Both come from themselves Is racing up the mountain Of our bodies: our tendency To think they must be "me". I am the Hunter Who wants nothing more Than the kill: I take the arrow Of the rainbow body, The belief that nothing Is as it seems, And I use the bow Of the state of being In clear and simple light. Seek me then tomorrow, The fisherman At the ocean's shore. And with this He disappears.  And so the next day Naropa is walking still, praying still, seeking still.

corpus_segments:14368.acip: 'GRO BA CHAGS PAS MYOS SHING, DE LA ZHEN PA RNAMS 'DUL BA'I SLAD DU RNAL 'BYOR MA MI MO'I RNAM PAS BUD MED KYI KHROD DU BYON TE RGYUD BYIN GYIS RLOB PA SOGS KYIS DNGOS GRUB LHAG PAR MYUR BA'I KHYAD CHOS TE KHYAD CHOS GSUM DANG,
corpus_segments:14368.wylie: 'gro ba chags pas myos shing, de la zhen pa rnams 'dul ba'i slad du rnal 'byor ma mi mo'i rnam pas bud med kyi khrod du byon te rgyud byin gyis rlob pa sogs kyis dngos grub lhag par myur ba'i khyad chos te khyad chos gsum dang
corpus_segments:14368.english: Finally, these are times when beings are crazed with desire; and because She wants to tame those who have a craving for that sort of thing, the Angel comes to us in the form of a human female, mixing with the women of the world, so She can give Her blessings to our being.  Things like this give our path its third unique quality: that it brings the attainments with incredible speed.

Things like this give our path its third unique quality: that it brings the attainments with incredible speed."}

corpus_segments:15089.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, NGA RGYAL GYI SEMS 'DZIN DANG, RNAM PA'I SEMS 'DZIN NO, DANG PO NI, GSAL SNANG YANG DGOS LA GTZO BO NI NGA RGYAL YIN TE, SNANG BAS MI 'CHING ZHEN PAS 'CHING, ZHES THA MAL GYI ZHEN PAS 'KHOR BAR 'CHING BA YIN PAS RANG GI PHUNG KHAMS SKYE MCHED DE RNAL 'BYOR MAR BSGOM PA YIN TE,
corpus_segments:15089.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, nga rgyal gyi sems 'dzin dang, rnam pa'i sems 'dzin no, dang po ni, gsal snang yang dgos la gtso bo ni nga rgyal yin te, snang bas mi 'ching zhen pas 'ching, zhes tha mal gyi zhen pas 'khor bar 'ching ba yin pas rang gi phung khams skye mched de rnal 'byor mar bsgom pa yin te
corpus_segments:15089.english: Here then is the second part from above: actually carrying out the directions.  This too has two parts.  The first is keeping your mind on identifying with Her, and the second is keeping your mind on looking like Her; here is the first.  It is true that you need to see yourself as Her, but the most important thing is to feel like Her, because--as they say--you aren't fettered by how you look, by rather by what you believe.  What this is saying is that we are fettered to circle of pain by our belief that things are normal; therefore we must practice seeing our heaps, categories, and gateways as the Angel of Diamond.

corpus_segments:15316.acip: DBANG PO RAB RNAMS KYIS DAG PA SBRAGS NAS BSGOM PA DANG, ZHEN PA RNAMS KYIS MNGON RTOGS TSIG ZIN LTAR BSKYANG,

corpus_segments:15316.english: Those of highest spiritual intellect should at this point connect the visualization to a vision of their own daily world as something totally pure.  Those of lesser power can simply follow the wording of the ritual text.

corpus_segments:15704.acip: GONG GI 'PHRO LAS, ,CHU BO RGYA MTSO RDZING BU DANG, ,RI BO DANG NI BZHI MDO DANG, ,LTENG KA DANG NI KHRON PA MTSE'U, ,KHANG STONG DANG NI LAM SRANG DAG ,THAMS CAD DU NI MKHA' 'GRO MA, ,KUN TU ZHEN PAR BLTA LA GNAS, ,ZHES DANG,

corpus_segments:15704.english: The truth of this we see in the lines that take up where the ones above left off: On rivers, or oceans, or ponds as well, On top of a mountain, or at a crossroads, Near a spring, or a well, or else a lake, In empty houses, or on the road, Everywhere do the Holy Angels Stay to watch you, with affection.

corpus_segments:15736.acip: DE LTAR GSAL SNANG SGRUB PA NI THA MAL GYI SNANG BA'I GNYEN PO DANG, NGA RGYAL SGRUB PA NI THA MAL GYI ZHEN PA'I GNYEN PO YIN PAS NGA RGYAL LA'ANG SLOB DGOS,
corpus_segments:15736.wylie: de ltar gsal snang sgrub pa ni tha mal gyi snang ba'i gnyen po dang, nga rgyal sgrub pa ni tha mal gyi zhen pa'i gnyen po yin pas nga rgyal la'ang slob dgos
corpus_segments:15736.english: Practicing to achieve the clarity of the vision described above serves as an antidote against things appearing as normal, everyday.  Practicing to reach the supreme level of confidence provides the antidote to believing that things are normal, just everyday.  Therefore we must train ourselves in supreme confidence as well.

Practicing to reach the supreme level of confidence provides the antidote to believing that things are normal, just everyday.  Therefore we must train ourselves in supreme confidence as well."}

corpus_segments:16640.acip: MDO LUGS LA THA MAL PA'I ZHEN PA 'BA' ZHIG GIS SBYIN GTONG SOGS BYAS PAS PHAN YON CHUNG BA DANG, PHA MA MA GTOGS PAS GRVA PA'I RDZAS GZHAN GYIS MI 'JU NA YANG,
corpus_segments:16640.wylie: mdo lugs la tha mal pa'i zhen pa 'ba' zhig gis sbyin gtong sogs byas pas phan yon chung ba dang, pha ma ma gtogs pas grva pa'i rdzas gzhan gyis mi 'ju na yang
corpus_segments:16640.english: The reason for this is that in the open teachings we are always performing our good deeds--charity and the like--with a vision of everything as normal.  And thus these deeds are of little benefit.  And in these open teachings too they say that food meant for monks and nuns is so karmically charged that no one but the particular ordained person's mother or father could ever eat it without problems.

And thus these deeds are of little benefit.  And in these open teachings too they say that food meant for monks and nuns is so karmically charged that no one but the particular ordained person's mother or father could ever eat it without problems."}

corpus_segments:17669.acip: ,'DOD YON SKYON DU MA BLTAS SHING, ,ZHEN PA NANG NAS MA LOG NA, ,'KHOR BA'I BTZON RA MI SGROL BAS, ,THAMS CAD SGYU MAR SHES PA'I BLOS, ,KUN 'BYUNG GNYEN PO BSTEN YANG 'TSAL,
corpus_segments:17669.wylie: 'dod yon skyon du ma bltas shing, ,zhen pa nang nas ma log na, ,'khor ba'i btson ra mi sgrol bas, ,thams cad sgyu mar shes pa'i blos, ,kun 'byung gnyen po bsten yang 'tshal
corpus_segments:17669.english: Suppose you fail to see the problems Of the objects of the senses, and never Deeply feel disgust for them; You will never escape then from the prison Of the circle of life.  Seek then to use the knowledge That all things are an illusion As an antidote for the source of all pain.

Seek then to use the knowledge That all things are an illusion As an antidote for the source of all pain."}

corpus_segments:17789.acip: THA MAL PA'I SNANG BA YID NGOR DAG PAR BYED NUS PA YIN LA, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I BCOS MIN GYI NGA RGYAL 'PHO NUS PA BYUNG BA NA, THA MAL PA'I ZHEN PA YID NGOR DAG PAR BYED NUS PA YIN NO,,
corpus_segments:17789.wylie: tha mal pa'i snang ba yid ngor dag par byed nus pa yin la, sngar bshad pa'i bcos min gyi nga rgyal 'pho nus pa byung ba na, tha mal pa'i zhen pa yid ngor dag par byed nus pa yin no
corpus_segments:17789.english: At this stage we say that you have reached the capacity to purify your mind of any tendency to see things as normal.  And when you are able, as we just described, to put your mind in a place where you identify yourself with the Angel in a way that comes to you quite naturally, then you have found the ability to purify your mind of any tendency to believe that things could be normal.

And when you are able, as we just described, to put your mind in a place where you identify yourself with the Angel in a way that comes to you quite naturally, then you have found the ability to purify your mind of any tendency to believe that things could be normal."}

corpus_segments:18742.acip: RANG YI DAM GYI LHAR GSAL BTAB LA THA MAL GYI LUS KYI ZHEN PA DOR NAS, SNANG SRID KYI CHOS THAMS CAD SGYU MA LTA BUR SHES PAR BYAS LA, THA MAL GYI 'KHRUL RTOG GI BAG CHAGS SPANGS NAS,
corpus_segments:18742.wylie: rang yi dam gyi lhar gsal btab la tha mal gyi lus kyi zhen pa dor nas, snang srid kyi chos thams cad sgyu ma lta bur shes par byas la, tha mal gyi 'khrul rtog gi bag chags spangs nas
corpus_segments:18742.english: Bring up the vision again of yourself as your Close Angel, relinquishing all attachment to your body as something normal.  Recollect now how each and every thing that appears in this world around us is just like an illusion, and thus eliminate every propensity within you for the mistaken idea that things are everyday.

Recollect now how each and every thing that appears in this world around us is just like an illusion, and thus eliminate every propensity within you for the mistaken idea that things are everyday."}

corpus_segments:20083.acip: JI SRID DU LUS CAN THAMS CAD KYANG THABS SHES DBYER MED DU SBYOR BA'I RNAL 'BYOR GYI LHAN SKYES KYI YE SHES LA ZHEN PA STE DGA' BAR MA GYUR PA DE SRID DU, 'KHOR BAR RING DU 'KHOR BAR 'GYUR ZHING, LUS KYI SDUG BSNGAL DANG, MYA NGAN TE YID MI BDE BAS YONGS SU GA-YENGS PAR 'GYUR RO,,
corpus_segments:20083.wylie: ji srid du lus can thams cad kyang thabs shes dbyer med du sbyor ba'i rnal 'byor gyi lhan skyes kyi ye shes la zhen pa ste dga' bar ma gyur pa de srid du, 'khor bar ring du 'khor bar 'gyur zhing, lus kyi sdug bsngal dang, mya ngan te yid mi bde bas yongs su ga-yengs par 'gyur ro
corpus_segments:20083.english: Until such time as they are able to develop a "hankering for"--meaning "an attraction towards"--the simultaneous form of wisdom which comes from the deep practice where method [the man] and wisdom [the woman] join in an indivisible union, each and every being in the universe will continue to spin in this interminable cycle of pain; they will be torn away by pain in their bodies, and by "grief" (which here refers to unhappiness) in their minds.
corpus_segments:20083.raw: {"course": "TCS17", "acip": "JI SRID DU LUS CAN THAMS CAD KYANG THABS SHES DBYER MED DU SBYOR BA'I RNAL 'BYOR GYI LHAN SKYES KYI YE SHES LA ZHEN PA STE DGA' BAR MA GYUR PA DE SRID DU, 'KHOR BAR RING DU 'KHOR BAR 'GYUR ZHING, LUS KYI SDUG BSNGAL DANG, MYA NGAN TE YID MI BDE BAS YONGS SU GA-YENGS PAR 'GYUR RO,,", "wylie": "ji srid du lus can thams cad kyang thabs shes dbyer med du sbyor ba'i rnal 'byor gyi lhan skyes kyi ye shes la zhen pa ste dga' bar ma gyur pa de srid du, 'khor bar ring du 'khor bar 'gyur zhing, lus kyi sdug bsngal dang, mya ngan te yid mi bde bas yongs su ga-yengs par 'gyur ro", "english": "Until such time as they are able to develop a \"hankering for\"--meaning \"an attraction towards\"--the simultaneous form of wisdom which comes from the deep practice where method [the man] and wisdom [the woman] join in an indivisible union, each and every being in the universe will continue to spin in this interminable cycle of pain; they will be torn away by pain in their bodies, and by \"grief\" (which here refers to unhappiness) in their minds."}

corpus_segments:20147.acip: 'GRO BA CHAGS PAS MYOS SHING, DE LA ZHEN PA RNAMS 'DUL BA'I SLAD DU RNAL 'BYOR MA MI MO'I RNAM PAS BUD MED KYI KHROD DU BYON TE RGYUD BYIN GYIS RLOB PA SOGS KYIS DNGOS GRUB LHAG PAR MYUR BA'I KHYAD CHOS TE KHYAD CHOS GSUM
corpus_segments:20147.wylie: 'gro ba chags pas myos shing, de la zhen pa rnams 'dul ba'i slad du rnal 'byor ma mi mo'i rnam pas bud med kyi khrod du byon te rgyud byin gyis rlob pa sogs kyis dngos grub lhag par myur ba'i khyad chos te khyad chos gsum
corpus_segments:20147.english: Finally, these are times when beings are crazed with desire; and because She also wants to help those who have a craving for that sort of thing, the Angel comes to us in the form of a human female, mixing with the women of the world, so She can give Her blessings to our being.  Things like this give our path its third unique quality: that it brings the attainments with incredible speed. * * * Choney Lama asks some extraordinary questions on the use of desire as a path, and as always answers them masterfully, in His Lamp that Illuminates the Essence: An Explanation of Critical Points in the "Harvest of Attainments" [of Je Tsongkapa], itself a Treatise on the Great, Deep Practice of the Stage of Completion, according to the System of that Great and Accomplished Saint, Luhipa (ACIP digital text S00299, ff. 42a-42b):
corpus_segments:20147.raw: {"course": "TCS17", "acip": "'GRO BA CHAGS PAS MYOS SHING, DE LA ZHEN PA RNAMS 'DUL BA'I SLAD DU RNAL 'BYOR MA MI MO'I RNAM PAS BUD MED KYI KHROD DU BYON TE RGYUD BYIN GYIS RLOB PA SOGS KYIS DNGOS GRUB LHAG PAR MYUR BA'I KHYAD CHOS TE KHYAD CHOS GSUM", "wylie": "'gro ba chags pas myos shing, de la zhen pa rnams 'dul ba'i slad du rnal 'byor ma mi mo'i rnam pas bud med kyi khrod du byon te rgyud byin gyis rlob pa sogs kyis dngos grub lhag par myur ba'i khyad chos te khyad chos gsum", "english": "Finally, these are times when beings are crazed with desire; and because She also wants to help those who have a craving for that sort of thing, the Angel comes to us in the form of a human female, mixing with the women of the world, so She can give Her blessings to our being.  Things like this give our path its third unique quality: that it brings the attainments with incredible speed. * * * Choney Lama asks some extraordinary questions on the use of desire as a path, and as always answers them masterfully, in His Lamp that Illuminates the Essence: An Explanation of Critical Points in the \"Harvest of Attainments\" [of Je Tsongkapa], itself a Treatise on the Great, Deep Practice of the Stage of Completion, according to the System of that Great and Accomplished Saint, Luhipa (ACIP digital text S00299, ff. 42a-42b):"}

corpus_segments:20655.acip: DE DAG BSGOMS PAS DE KHO NA NYID LA 'JUG TSUL NI LHA'I SKU LA SEMS BRTAN PA NA SEMS NYID LHAR SNANG GI PHYI ROL NI MED PAS, ,BSGOM BYA SOGS KYI 'KHOR GSUM DU ZHEN PAR MI BYA'O ZHES SHES PAR BYAS PA NA,
corpus_segments:20655.wylie: de dag bsgoms pas de kho na nyid la 'jug tshul ni lha'i sku la sems brtan pa na sems nyid lhar snang gi phyi rol ni med pas, ,bsgom bya sogs kyi 'khor gsum du zhen par mi bya'o zhes shes par byas pa na
corpus_segments:20655.english: The way in which we engage in emptiness through visualizing these Angels is that--when we reach a point where our mind stays firmly on the holy body of the Angel--then the mind itself is appearing as an Angel; it's not that They're on the outside.  At this point we must keep in mind the instructions that we should "never grasp on to the three elements of the object of our meditation, or any of the rest."
corpus_segments:20655.raw: {"course": "TCS17", "acip": "DE DAG BSGOMS PAS DE KHO NA NYID LA 'JUG TSUL NI LHA'I SKU LA SEMS BRTAN PA NA SEMS NYID LHAR SNANG GI PHYI ROL NI MED PAS, ,BSGOM BYA SOGS KYI 'KHOR GSUM DU ZHEN PAR MI BYA'O ZHES SHES PAR BYAS PA NA,", "wylie": "de dag bsgoms pas de kho na nyid la 'jug tshul ni lha'i sku la sems brtan pa na sems nyid lhar snang gi phyi rol ni med pas, ,bsgom bya sogs kyi 'khor gsum du zhen par mi bya'o zhes shes par byas pa na", "english": "The way in which we engage in emptiness through visualizing these Angels is that--when we reach a point where our mind stays firmly on the holy body of the Angel--then the mind itself is appearing as an Angel; it's not that They're on the outside.  At this point we must keep in mind the instructions that we should \"never grasp on to the three elements of the object of our meditation, or any of the rest.\""}

corpus_segments:20764.acip: 'O NA JI LTAR BYA ZHE NA, PHO NYA MO LA RTAG TU ZHEN PA STE CHAGS PAS BSTEN NA, THAR BA STE GROL BAR 'GYUR RO, ,ZHES 'CHAD DO,,
corpus_segments:20764.wylie: 'o na ji ltar bya zhe na, pho nya mo la rtag tu zhen pa ste chags pas bsten na, thar ba ste grol bar 'gyur ro, ,zhes 'chad do
corpus_segments:20764.english: Well then, how are we supposed to act?  Maintain always your craving for your Messenger woman--practice with Her in desire.  And then, it is explained, we will come to reach our freedom.
corpus_segments:20764.raw: {"course": "TCS17", "acip": "'O NA JI LTAR BYA ZHE NA, PHO NYA MO LA RTAG TU ZHEN PA STE CHAGS PAS BSTEN NA, THAR BA STE GROL BAR 'GYUR RO, ,ZHES 'CHAD DO,,", "wylie": "'o na ji ltar bya zhe na, pho nya mo la rtag tu zhen pa ste chags pas bsten na, thar ba ste grol bar 'gyur ro, ,zhes 'chad do", "english": "Well then, how are we supposed to act?  Maintain always your craving for your Messenger woman--practice with Her in desire.  And then, it is explained, we will come to reach our freedom."}

corpus_segments:20765.acip: BHA BA NI, PHO NYA MO BSRUNGS RTAG THAR PA, ,ZHES 'DON PA'I DON PHO NYA MO STE LAS RGYA LA GO CHA'I BSRUNG BA BYAS TE, DE YIS THAMS CAD DU MNGON PAR ZHEN PA ZHI BAR BYA'O,,
corpus_segments:20765.wylie: bha ba ni, pho nya mo bsrungs rtag thar pa, ,zhes 'don pa'i don pho nya mo ste las rgya la go cha'i bsrung ba byas te, de yis thams cad du mngon par zhen pa zhi bar bya'o
corpus_segments:20765.english: Bhava says "Protect the Messenger woman; and then always is there freedom."  What this is describing is how we protect our Messenger woman--meaning our actual partner--with the armor.  This then puts a final end to our craving for every other object.
corpus_segments:20765.raw: {"course": "TCS17", "acip": "BHA BA NI, PHO NYA MO BSRUNGS RTAG THAR PA, ,ZHES 'DON PA'I DON PHO NYA MO STE LAS RGYA LA GO CHA'I BSRUNG BA BYAS TE, DE YIS THAMS CAD DU MNGON PAR ZHEN PA ZHI BAR BYA'O,,", "wylie": "bha ba ni, pho nya mo bsrungs rtag thar pa, ,zhes 'don pa'i don pho nya mo ste las rgya la go cha'i bsrung ba byas te, de yis thams cad du mngon par zhen pa zhi bar bya'o", "english": "Bhava says \"Protect the Messenger woman; and then always is there freedom.\"  What this is describing is how we protect our Messenger woman--meaning our actual partner--with the armor.  This then puts a final end to our craving for every other object."}

corpus_segments:20797.acip: LAS KYI PHYAG RGYA LA BRTEN NAS 'JUG PA'I TSUL LA PHYAG RGYA'I MTSAN NYID BRTAG THABS, DE 'KHOR BA LA ZHEN PA LOG NAS THAR PA THOB 'DOD KYI BLO BCOS MA MA YIN PA BSKYED DE, BYAMS SNYING RJE BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS BSKYED,
corpus_segments:20797.wylie: las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas 'jug pa'i tshul la phyag rgya'i mtshan nyid brtag thabs, de 'khor ba la zhen pa log nas thar pa thob 'dod kyi blo bcos ma ma yin pa bskyed de, byams snying rje byang chub kyi sems bskyed
corpus_segments:20797.english: Concerning the method where we get the winds to enter by practicing with an actual partner, there are first of all certain ways of examining a potential partner to see if they possess the requisite characteristics.  They must have gained an aversion for this cycle of pain; they must have reached an uncontrived state of mind where they truly hope to attain freedom from this suffering.  And they must as well have developed within themselves the attitudes of love, compassion, and the Wish for enlightenment.
corpus_segments:20797.raw: {"course": "TCS17", "acip": "LAS KYI PHYAG RGYA LA BRTEN NAS 'JUG PA'I TSUL LA PHYAG RGYA'I MTSAN NYID BRTAG THABS, DE 'KHOR BA LA ZHEN PA LOG NAS THAR PA THOB 'DOD KYI BLO BCOS MA MA YIN PA BSKYED DE, BYAMS SNYING RJE BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS BSKYED,", "wylie": "las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas 'jug pa'i tshul la phyag rgya'i mtshan nyid brtag thabs, de 'khor ba la zhen pa log nas thar pa thob 'dod kyi blo bcos ma ma yin pa bskyed de, byams snying rje byang chub kyi sems bskyed", "english": "Concerning the method where we get the winds to enter by practicing with an actual partner, there are first of all certain ways of examining a potential partner to see if they possess the requisite characteristics.  They must have gained an aversion for this cycle of pain; they must have reached an uncontrived state of mind where they truly hope to attain freedom from this suffering.  And they must as well have developed within themselves the attitudes of love, compassion, and the Wish for enlightenment."}

corpus_segments:20827.acip: TEE LO PAS, ,GZUGS SGRA DRI RO'I 'DOD YON LA, ,SEMS LA ZHEN PA BYUNG BA'I TSE, ,SBRANG MA RTZI LA SBYAR DANG MTSUNGS, ,ZHEN PA THONG ZHIG N'A RO PA,
corpus_segments:20827.wylie: tee lo pas, ,gzugs sgra dri ro'i 'dod yon la, ,sems la zhen pa byung ba'i tshe, ,sbrang ma rtsi la sbyar dang mtshungs, ,zhen pa thong zhig nA ro pa
corpus_segments:20827.english: Master Tilopa has put it in the following way: If your mind gets attracted To the objects of the senses-- To things to see or hear, smell or taste-- Then it's just as if a honey bee Has gotten himself stuck in the honey.
corpus_segments:20827.raw: {"course": "TCS17", "acip": "TEE LO PAS, ,GZUGS SGRA DRI RO'I 'DOD YON LA, ,SEMS LA ZHEN PA BYUNG BA'I TSE, ,SBRANG MA RTZI LA SBYAR DANG MTSUNGS, ,ZHEN PA THONG ZHIG N'A RO PA,", "wylie": "tee lo pas, ,gzugs sgra dri ro'i 'dod yon la, ,sems la zhen pa byung ba'i tshe, ,sbrang ma rtsi la sbyar dang mtshungs, ,zhen pa thong zhig nA ro pa", "english": "Master Tilopa has put it in the following way: If your mind gets attracted To the objects of the senses-- To things to see or hear, smell or taste-- Then it's just as if a honey bee Has gotten himself stuck in the honey."}

corpus_segments:20863.acip: MKHA' 'GRO MA MCHOG STE GTZO BO NYI SHU RTZA BZHIS, SPYOD PA STE MNGON MTHO MCHOG DANG DNGOS POR ZHEN PA'I 'CHING BA LAS GROL BA'I 'BRAS BU RAB TU STER BAR BYED DO,,
corpus_segments:20863.wylie: mkha' 'gro ma mchog ste gtso bo nyi shu rtsa bzhis, spyod pa ste mngon mtho mchog dang dngos por zhen pa'i 'ching ba las grol ba'i 'bras bu rab tu ster bar byed do
corpus_segments:20863.english: And then the "highest of the Angels of the Sky," meaning those of the 24 holy places, will practice with them, and grant them the spiritual goal of the higher realms, and of a liberation where they are freed from the chains of believing in the things around them. * * * Je Rinpoche supplies us more detail on the different physical configurations of a partner in The Golden Harvest of Attainments: An Explication of the Stage of Completion for the Secret Teaching of Highest Bliss (Sanvara), according to the System of the Lord of Secret Practitioners, Luhipa (ACIP digital text S05325, ff. 25a-25b):
corpus_segments:20863.raw: {"course": "TCS17", "acip": "MKHA' 'GRO MA MCHOG STE GTZO BO NYI SHU RTZA BZHIS, SPYOD PA STE MNGON MTHO MCHOG DANG DNGOS POR ZHEN PA'I 'CHING BA LAS GROL BA'I 'BRAS BU RAB TU STER BAR BYED DO,,", "wylie": "mkha' 'gro ma mchog ste gtso bo nyi shu rtsa bzhis, spyod pa ste mngon mtho mchog dang dngos por zhen pa'i 'ching ba las grol ba'i 'bras bu rab tu ster bar byed do", "english": "And then the \"highest of the Angels of the Sky,\" meaning those of the 24 holy places, will practice with them, and grant them the spiritual goal of the higher realms, and of a liberation where they are freed from the chains of believing in the things around them. * * * Je Rinpoche supplies us more detail on the different physical configurations of a partner in The Golden Harvest of Attainments: An Explication of the Stage of Completion for the Secret Teaching of Highest Bliss (Sanvara), according to the System of the Lord of Secret Practitioners, Luhipa (ACIP digital text S05325, ff. 25a-25b):"}

corpus_segments:20923.acip: ,ZHES RANG GI PHO NYA LA THAR PA'I DON DU ZHEN PAS RTAG TU STE RGYUN DU BYA BA DES 'DA' BA'I TSUL GYIS LONGS SPYOD PAR GSUNGS PA LTAR BYA BA LA, DE 'DRA BA'I LAM LAS GANG GIS KYANG BKRI BAR MI NUS PAR BYA BA STE DAM TSIG BZHI PA'O,,
corpus_segments:20923.wylie: zhes rang gi pho nya la thar pa'i don du zhen pas rtag tu ste rgyun du bya ba des 'da' ba'i tshul gyis longs spyod par gsungs pa ltar bya ba la, de 'dra ba'i lam las gang gis kyang bkri bar mi nus par bya ba ste dam tshig bzhi pa'o
corpus_segments:20923.english: These lines are saying that one should live in such a way that you pass your hours with your Messenger, enjoying this sacred practice.  And you should do so "always," meaning constantly.  The practice should as well be done out of a love for the goal of reaching freedom.  You must, finally, assure that no one every ever leads you away from this particular path: and this then is the fourth of the pledges. *  *  *  *  *

And you should do so \"always,\" meaning constantly.  The practice should as well be done out of a love for the goal of reaching freedom.  You must, finally, assure that no one every ever leads you away from this particular path: and this then is the fourth of the pledges. *  *  *  *  *"}

corpus_segments:20975.acip: SH'ANTI PAS RTZOD PA'I DUS 'DIR 'GRO BA RNAMS BUD MED LA RAB TU ZHEN PAS, DE RNAMS GDUL PA'I PHYIR BUD MED DU SPRUL PA'I LHA RNAMS 'DI NA GNAS PAS MI SMOD CES SAM BUD MED KYI KHROD NA RDO RJE PHAG MO SOGS GNAS PAS DES NA GANG YIN MI SHES PAS BUD MED RNAMS LA MI SMOD PAR BZHED PA'I PHYIR BCAS PA'I SPYI MTSAMS 'DZIN PA LA BUD MED TZAM NAS BYED PAR GSAL LO, ,
corpus_segments:20975.wylie: shAnti pas rtsod pa'i dus 'dir 'gro ba rnams bud med la rab tu zhen pas, de rnams gdul pa'i phyir bud med du sprul pa'i lha rnams 'di na gnas pas mi smod ces sam bud med kyi khrod na rdo rje phag mo sogs gnas pas des na gang yin mi shes pas bud med rnams la mi smod par bzhed pa'i phyir bcas pa'i spyi mtshams 'dzin pa la bud med tsam nas byed par gsal lo,
corpus_segments:20975.english: Shantipa here points out that "Here in the days of strife, people have a particular attachment to the female form; and so in order to tame these beings, Angels emanate as human women.  They are then here in the world with us, and we must never disparage Them."  So too we see, "Holy beings like the Diamond Sow are present here in the world, mixed among the human women.  As such, we never know which woman might be Them; and so we should never disparage women." * * * The famed Fifty Verses on Lamas by Master Ashvaghosha (c. 150 AD) is a source of a great number of our secret vows and pledges.  Je Rinpoche relates one of these to partner practice; we first hear the vow itself, from Geshe Tsewang Samdrup's String of Shining Jewels (ACIP digital text S00201, f. 24a), and then read Je Tsongkapa's comments on it, from His Elucidation of the "Fifty Verses on Lamas" (ACIP digital text S05269, f. 19a).

They are then here in the world with us, and we must never disparage Them.\"  So too we see, \"Holy beings like the Diamond Sow are present here in the world, mixed among the human women.  As such, we never know which woman might be Them; and so we should never disparage women.\" * * * The famed Fifty Verses on Lamas by Master Ashvaghosha (c. 150 AD) is a source of a great number of our secret vows and pledges. corpus_segments:33705.acip: GSAL CHA DANG DVANGS CHA NI YUL LA MI BYED PAR, YUL CAN SHES PA LA GSAL CHA'AM DVANGS CHA YOD MED LA BYA DGOS, GSAL CHA MI 'BYUNG BA'I TSE SGRIB BYED KYIS SGRIB PA LTAR YOD,
corpus_segments:33705.wylie: gsal cha dang dvangs cha ni yul la mi byed par, yul can shes pa la gsal cha'am dvangs cha yod med la bya dgos, gsal cha mi 'byung ba'i tshe sgrib byed kyis sgrib pa ltar yod
corpus_segments:33705.english: It's important to say here that—when we talk about clarity, or clearness—we're not talking about a quality of the object. Rather, it's a distinction that you have to make about the subject state of mind in meditation: does the mind itself feel clear—is there mental clarity, or not? When we can't get clarity to come, it feels almost like we've moved under a dark shadow.

corpus_segments:28371.english: The sentence that talks about acting to obscure things is meant to convey the idea of “deceiving about the actual”—meaning that deceptive reality is being referred to as an obscuration, and something which blocks us from perceiving actual reality.

corpus_segments:28852.english: What is it that this reality veils? Given the wording “deceived about what is actually there,” what we're referring to is deception—a veil—in the sense of what covers & conceals actual reality. This is not meant to be a reference to a “correct” form of deceptive reality, in the division of that reality into correct & mistaken.

corpus_segments:1585.acip: TSIG KYAL BA'I NI, 'BRAS BU'I LJON SHING LA 'BRAS BU MI 'CHAGS PA DANG DUS MIN PAR YANG 'BRAS BU 'CHAGS PA DANG DUS SU MI 'CHAGS PA DANG MA SMIN PA SMIN PAR SNANG BA DANG RTZA BA MI BRTAN PA DANG RING DU MI GNAS PA DANG KUN DGA' RA BA'AM NAGS TSAL LAM RDZING BU NYAMS DGA' BA MI MANG BA DANG 'JIGS PA'I RGYU MANG PO DANG LDAN PA DANG ,
corpus_segments:1585.wylie: tshig kyal ba'i ni, 'bras bu'i ljon shing la 'bras bu mi 'chags pa dang dus min par yang 'bras bu 'chags pa dang dus su mi 'chags pa dang ma smin pa smin par snang ba dang rtsa ba mi brtan pa dang ring du mi gnas pa dang kun dga' ra ba'am nags tshal lam rdzing bu nyams dga' ba mi mang ba dang 'jigs pa'i rgyu mang po dang ldan pa dang
corpus_segments:1585.english: Because you have talked meaninglessly, fruits refuse to grow on the trees, or they start to grow at the wrong times, never at the right times, and seem ripe when they're still not ripe, or their roots are frail, or they can't stay long; there are no places to take your leisure, no parks, no glades, no pools of cool water, and many things around to make you afraid.

corpus_segments:3056.english: All other good deeds are like the plantain tree, That gives its fruits and always dies away; The wish for enlightenment though is an evergreen That never dies by giving its fruits, But rather ever increases.

corpus_segments:3057.acip: ,GSUM PA NI, DGE BA MI ZAD CING 'PHEL BAR 'DOD PAS KYANG BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS BSGOM PAR RIGS TE, BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS KYIS MA ZIN PA'I DGE BA GZHAN KUN CHU SHING BZHIN DU NI 'BRAS BU BSKYED NAS SLAR YANG 'BRAS BU BSKYED PA'I NUS PA ZAD PAR 'GYUR BA NYID YIN LA, DPAG BSAMS GYI SHING BZHIN DU BYANG CHUB SEMS KYI LJON SHING RTAG PAR YANG 'BRAS BU 'BYIN PAS MI ZAD CING GONG NAS GONG DU 'PHEL BAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,
corpus_segments:3057.wylie: gsum pa ni, dge ba mi zad cing 'phel bar 'dod pas kyang byang chub kyi sems bsgom par rigs te, byang chub kyi sems kyis ma zin pa'i dge ba gzhan kun chu shing bzhin du ni 'bras bu bskyed nas slar yang 'bras bu bskyed pa'i nus pa zad par 'gyur ba nyid yin la, dpag bsams gyi shing bzhin du byang chub sems kyi ljon shing rtag par yang 'bras bu 'byin pas mi zad cing gong nas gong du 'phel bar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:3057.english: Practicing the wish for enlightenment is moreover a right thing to do for those who hope to see their good deeds never die, but increase ever further. This is because all other good deeds, meaning those that are not imbued by this wish, are like the plantain tree: they give their fruits and, once they have done so, it is always the case that their ability to produce further fruits dies away. The wish for enlightenment though is an evergreen: it is like a wish-giving tree, in that it never dies by giving its fruits, but rather ever increases, higher and higher.

This is because all other good deeds, meaning those that are not imbued by this wish, are like the plantain tree: they give their fruits and, once they have done so, it is always the case that their ability to produce further fruits dies away. corpus_segments:3072.acip: ,ME TOG 'BRAS BU JI SNYED YOD PA DANG , ,SMAN GYI RNAM PA GANG ZHIG YOD PA DANG , ,'JIG RTEN RIN CHEN JI SNYED YOD PA DANG , ,CHU GTZANG YID DU 'ONG BA CI YOD DANG , ,RIN CHEN RI BO DANG NI DE BZHIN DU, ,NAGS TSAL SA PHYOGS DBEN ZHING NYAMS DGA' DANG , ,LJON SHING ME TOG RGYAN SPRAS SPUD PA DANG , ,SHING GANG 'BRAS BZANG YAL GA DUD PA DANG , ,LHA SOGS 'JIG RTEN NA YANG DRI DANG NI, ,SPOS DANG DPAG BSAM SHING DANG RIN CHEN SHING , ,MA RMOS 'KHRUNGS PA'I LO TOG RNAM PA DANG , ,GZHAN YANG MCHOD PAR 'OS PA'I RGYAN RNAMS NI, ,MTSO DANG RDZING BU PAD MAS BRGYAN PA DAG,NGANG PA SHIN TU SKAD SNYAN YID 'ONG LDAN,
corpus_segments:3072.wylie: me tog 'bras bu ji snyed yod pa dang , ,sman gyi rnam pa gang zhig yod pa dang , ,'jig rten rin chen ji snyed yod pa dang , ,chu gtsang yid du 'ong ba ci yod dang , ,rin chen ri bo dang ni de bzhin du, ,nags tshal sa phyogs dben zhing nyams dga' dang , ,ljon shing me tog rgyan spras spud pa dang , ,shing gang 'bras bzang yal ga dud pa dang , ,lha sogs 'jig rten na yang dri dang ni, ,spos dang dpag bsam shing dang rin chen shing , ,ma rmos 'khrungs pa'i lo tog rnam pa dang , ,gzhan yang mchod par 'os pa'i rgyan rnams ni, ,mtsho dang rdzing bu pad mas brgyan pa dag,ngang pa shin tu skad snyan yid 'ong ldan
corpus_segments:3072.english: Give flowers, and fruits, as many as exist; And all the different herbs, as many as there may be. Give each and every precious substance contained in the planet, All the pure and lovely water that exists. Give the precious mountains, and so too The forests, quiet places of refuge, and lovely spots; Give the plants, studded with flowers, and adorned, The trees whose branches are bent low under fine ripe fruit. Give fragrances and incenses, even those which are found In the worlds of pleasure beings and the like; The wishing tree, and the tree of precious substances. Give grain that grows without ever being planted, And any other lovely object which is worthy of presenting-- Lovely lakes and bathing ponds bedecked with lotus blossoms And water birds of beauty, singing their splendid songs.

corpus_segments:3073.acip: ,DANG PO NI, 'JIG RTEN NA BDAG POS MA BZUNG BA'I ME TOG PAD MA SOGS ME TOG DANG , AA RU RA SOGS 'BRAS BU JI SNYED YOD PA DANG , GA PUR SOGS SMAN GYI RIGS KYI RNAM PA GANG DAG YOD PA DANG , 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS NA GSER DNGUL SOGS RIN CHEN JI SNYED YOD PA DANG MTSO DANG RDZING BU SOGS CHU GTZANG YID DU 'ONG BA CI YOD PA DANG , GSER LA SOGS PA'I RIN CHEN RI BO BRGYAD LA SOGS PA DANG NI DE BZHIN DU NAGS TSAL DANG SA PHYOGS DBEN ZHING NYAMS DGA' BA DANG LJON SHING RANG GI ME TOG SNA TSOGS PA'I RGYAN GYIS SPRAS SHING MDZES PAR SPUD PA DANG , SHING GANG 'BRAS BU BZANG PO SMIN PA LCI BAS YAL GA THUR LA DUD PA DANG LHA DANG KLU LA SOGS PA'I 'JIG RTEN NA YANG LHAN CIG SKYES PA DANG SBYAR BA LAS BYUNG BA DANG , GYUR PA LAS BYUNG BA'I DRI BZANG PO DANG NI BDUG PA'I SPOS DANG DGOS 'DOD 'BYUNG BA'I DPAG BSAM LJON SHING DANG RIN CHEN SNA TSOGS LAS GRUB PA'I SHING DANG , YID BZHIN GYI MTSO DANG KHRUS KYI RDZING BU PAD MAS BRGYAN PA DANG DE NA NGANG PA SHIN TU SGRA SNYAN PA SGROG PA YID DU 'ONG BA DANG , THONG BSHOL GYIS MA RMOS PA RANG 'KHRUNGS PA'I LO TOG GI RNAM PA DANG DE LA SOGS PA'I GZHAN YANG DKON MCHOG LA MCHOD PAR 'OS PA'I RGYAN MDZES PA RNAMS NI DBUL BAR BGYI'O, , 'GREL PA'I DON MA GO BA KHA CIG GIS GZHUNG GI GO RIMS GZHAN DU BSHAD DO,

corpus_segments:3073.english: You should first give those things in the world which have no owner. Give flowers, flowers like the lotus, and give the fruits of the trees, like the olive, as many as exist everywhere. Then give all the different herbs of the earth, camphor and the like, as many as there may be. Give each and every precious substance contained in the planet: gold, silver, and anything of the sort. Give all the pure and lovely water of every ocean, lake, and other bodies of water that exists. Give the eight precious mountains of gold and all the rest, and so too give all the forests, give all the quiet places of refuge, all the lovely spots, all the many kinds of plants, each studded with a variety of jewel flowers, each adorned in beauty. Give all the trees whose branches are bent low under the weight of fine ripe fruit. Give all the fine fragrances and incenses that exist, whether they be natural, or concocted, or transformed, and include even those which are found in the worlds of pleasure beings, serpent-beings, and the like. Give the wishing tree, which supplies your every wish, and give the tree made of precious substances. Give lovely lakes and bathing ponds, ones that grant your every desire, bedecked with lotus blossoms, and give the waterbirds who live upon them, in all their beauty, singing their splendid songs. Give every kind of grain, growing of its own accord, without ever being planted. Offer these, and offer any other lovely object which is worthy of presenting to the Jewels.

corpus_segments:3756.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, GNAS BRAG DANG SA'I PHUG GAM LHA KHANG STONG PA'AM LJON SHING GI DRUNG DU JI SRID 'DOD PAR GNAS BCAS TE KHYIM LA SOGS PA SNGAR SPANGS PA DE DAG PHYIR LEN PAR MI 'DOD PAS NA NAM ZHIG RGYAB TU MI BLTA ZHING , DE DAG LA CHAGS PA MED PAR NAM ZHIG 'GYUR ZHIG GU SNYAM DU SMON PAR BYA'O,
corpus_segments:3756.wylie: gnyis pa ni, gnas brag dang sa'i phug gam lha khang stong pa'am ljon shing gi drung du ji srid 'dod par gnas bcas te khyim la sogs pa sngar spangs pa de dag phyir len par mi 'dod pas na nam zhig rgyab tu mi blta zhing , de dag la chags pa med par nam zhig 'gyur zhig gu snyam du smon par bya'o
corpus_segments:3756.english: Here is the second point, on where I should go into isolation. Make to yourself the following prayer as well: "May I come to live exactly as I please, in a cave somewhere, or in some hollow, or perhaps in some abandoned temple, or else at the foot of a forest tree. May the day never come that I look back at all, when I think of the home and other things that I used to have and then gave up; may I never get any wish at all to have them back. May I reach, in short, a place where I've finished with every kind of attachment for any of these things."

corpus_segments:7603.acip: ,DGE BA GZHAN KUN CHU SHING BZHIN DU NI, ,'BRAS BU BSKYED NAS ZAD PAR 'GYUR BA NYID, ,BYANG CHUB SEMS KYI LJON SHING RTAG PAR YANG , ,'BRAS BU 'BYIN PAS MI ZAD 'PHEL BAR 'GYUR,
corpus_segments:7603.wylie: dge ba gzhan kun chu shing bzhin du ni, ,'bras bu bskyed nas zad par 'gyur ba nyid, ,byang chub sems kyi ljon shing rtag par yang , ,'bras bu 'byin pas mi zad 'phel bar 'gyur
corpus_segments:7603.english: All other good deeds are like the plantain tree, That gives its fruits and always dies away; The wish for enlightenment though is an evergreen That never dies by giving its fruits, But rather ever increases.
corpus_segments:7603.raw: {"course": "C17", "acip": ",DGE BA GZHAN KUN CHU SHING BZHIN DU NI, ,'BRAS BU BSKYED NAS ZAD PAR 'GYUR BA NYID, ,BYANG CHUB SEMS KYI LJON SHING RTAG PAR YANG , ,'BRAS BU 'BYIN PAS MI ZAD 'PHEL BAR 'GYUR,", "wylie": "dge ba gzhan kun chu shing bzhin du ni, ,'bras bu bskyed nas zad par 'gyur ba nyid, ,byang chub sems kyi ljon shing rtag par yang , ,'bras bu 'byin pas mi zad 'phel bar 'gyur", "english": "All other good deeds are like the plantain tree, That gives its fruits and always dies away; The wish for enlightenment though is an evergreen That never dies by giving its fruits, But rather ever increases."}

corpus_segments:7604.acip: ,GSUM PA NI, DGE BA MI ZAD CING 'PHEL BAR 'DOD PAS KYANG BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS BSGOM PAR RIGS TE, BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS KYIS MA ZIN PA'I DGE BA GZHAN KUN CHU SHING BZHIN DU NI 'BRAS BU BSKYED NAS SLAR YANG 'BRAS BU BSKYED PA'I NUS PA ZAD PAR 'GYUR BA NYID YIN LA, DPAG BSAMS GYI SHING BZHIN DU BYANG CHUB SEMS KYI LJON SHING RTAG PAR YANG 'BRAS BU 'BYIN PAS MI ZAD CING GONG NAS GONG DU 'PHEL BAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,
corpus_segments:7604.wylie: gsum pa ni, dge ba mi zad cing 'phel bar 'dod pas kyang byang chub kyi sems bsgom par rigs te, byang chub kyi sems kyis ma zin pa'i dge ba gzhan kun chu shing bzhin du ni 'bras bu bskyed nas slar yang 'bras bu bskyed pa'i nus pa zad par 'gyur ba nyid yin la, dpag bsams gyi shing bzhin du byang chub sems kyi ljon shing rtag par yang 'bras bu 'byin pas mi zad cing gong nas gong du 'phel bar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:7604.english: Practicing the wish for enlightenment is moreover a right thing to do for those who hope to see their good deeds never die, but increase ever further. This is because all other good deeds, meaning those that are not imbued by this wish, are like the plantain tree: they give their fruits and, once they have done so, it is always the case that their ability to produce further fruits dies away. The wish for enlightenment though is an evergreen: it is like a wish-giving tree, in that it never dies by giving its fruits, but rather ever increases, higher and higher.

This is because all other good deeds, meaning those that are not imbued by this wish, are like the plantain tree: they give their fruits and, once they have done so, it is always the case that their ability to produce further fruits dies away. The wish for enlightenment though is an evergreen: it is like a wish-giving tree, in that it never dies by giving its fruits, but rather ever increases, higher and higher."}

corpus_segments:7610.wylie: me tog 'bras bu ji snyed yod pa dang , ,sman gyi rnam pa gang zhig yod pa dang , ,'jig rten rin chen ji snyed yod pa dang , ,chu gtsang yid du 'ong ba ci yod dang , ,rin chen ri bo dang ni de bzhin du, ,nags tshal sa phyogs dben zhing nyams dga' dang , ,ljon shing me tog rgyan spras spud pa dang , ,shing gang 'bras bzang yal ga dud pa dang , ,lha sogs 'jig rten na yang dri dang ni, ,spos dang dpag bsam shing dang rin chen shing , ,ma rmos 'khrungs pa'i lo tog rnam pa dang , ,gzhan yang mchod par 'os pa'i rgyan rnams ni, ,mtsho dang rdzing bu pad mas brgyan pa dag,ngang pa shin tu skad snyan yid 'ong ldan
corpus_segments:7610.english: Give flowers, and fruits, as many as exist; And all the different herbs, as many as there may be. Give each and every precious substance contained in the planet, All the pure and lovely water that exists. Give the precious mountains, and so too The forests, quiet places of refuge, and lovely spots; Give the plants, studded with flowers, and adorned, The trees whose branches are bent low under fine ripe fruit. Give fragrances and incenses, even those which are found In the worlds of pleasure beings and the like; The wishing tree, and the tree of precious substances. Give grain that grows without ever being planted, And any other lovely object which is worthy of presenting-- Lovely lakes and bathing ponds bedecked with lotus blossoms And water birds of beauty, singing their splendid songs. ************

corpus_segments:30911.acip: ,BUM PA SNAM BU RE LDE DMAG DANG NAGS TSAL PHRENG BA LJON SHING DANG, ,[212b] KHANG KHYIM SHING RTA PHRAN DANG 'GRON GNAS LA SOGS DNGOS RNAMS GANG DAG DANG, ,DE BZHIN GANG DAG SGO NAS SKYE 'DIS BSNYAD PA DE RNAMS RTOGS BYA STE, ,GANG PHYIR THUB DBANG DE NI 'JIG RTEN LHAN CIG RTZOD MI MDZAD PHYIR RO,
corpus_segments:30911.wylie: bum pa snam bu re lde dmag dang nags tshal phreng ba ljon shing dang, ,[212b] khang khyim shing rta phran dang 'gron gnas la sogs dngos rnams gang dag dang, ,de bzhin gang dag sgo nas skye 'dis bsnyad pa de rnams rtogs bya ste, ,gang phyir thub dbang de ni 'jig rten lhan cig rtsod mi mdzad phyir ro
corpus_segments:30911.english: Let's consider Things like Water pitchers And bolts of cloth And rolls of felt; As well as Armies and forests, And strings of Beads, and trees [f. 212b]. Or houses and carts, And meeting places, And guest houses, And all such entities; And in the same vein, We should understand These things as well: All those things which These same people Would ascribe. And why is This the case? It's because this Lord of the Able Ones Has no argument With the world.

corpus_segments:34347.english: The book called The Bodhisattva's Life too has lines like the following: All the other Kinds of virtue Are like a bamboo tree; They give their fruits And then they always Die and go away. But the Wish For Buddhahood Is an evergreen that always Gives forth its fruits, And instead of fading Flourishes even more.

corpus_segments:34793.acip: RDZUN GYIS LAS KYI MTHA' RGYAS PAR MI 'GYUR PHRA MAS SA PHYOGS MI SNYOMS SHING, BGROD DKA' TSIG RTZUB KYIS SDONG DU MA DANG TSER MA DANG RDO GSEG SOGS MANG, NGAG BKYAL GYIS LJON SHING LA 'BRAS BU DUS SU MI CHAGS
corpus_segments:34793.wylie: rdzun gyis las kyi mtha' rgyas par mi 'gyur phra mas sa phyogs mi snyoms shing, bgrod dka' tshig rtsub kyis sdong du ma dang tsher ma dang rdo gseg sogs mang, ngag bkyal gyis ljon shing la 'bras bu dus su mi chags
corpus_segments:34793.english: The result of lying is that the your labors fail to have any extensive fruits. Divisive talk makes the land around you uneven and broken, and hard to travel over. corpus_segments:13508.acip: RGYAL PO PAnA CHEN SPYAN MNGA' RU, ,NA LEN DRA RU SPYAN SNGAR NAS, ,MU STEGS LJON SHING RTZAD NAS DREGS, ,SANGS RGYAS BSTAN PA'I SPU GRI YIS, ,MU RTEGS RGOL NGAN SKRA RNAMS SPYANG , ,SANGS RGYAS BSTAN PA'I RGYAL MTSAN GTZUGS  CES GSUNGS NAS,
corpus_segments:13508.wylie: rgyal po paNa chen spyan mnga' ru, ,na len dra ru spyan sngar nas, ,mu stegs ljon shing rtsad nas dregs, ,sangs rgyas bstan pa'i spu gri yis, ,mu rtegs rgol ngan skra rnams spyang , ,sangs rgyas bstan pa'i rgyal mtshan gtsugs ces gsungs nas
corpus_segments:13508.english: In the presence of the King And all the assembled sages, In the presence of all the wise At Nalendra Monastery, I have ripped out the very roots Of the trees of the non-Buddhist thinkers. With the razor of Lord Buddha's word I have shaved the hair from the heads Of these ignorant debaters, And raised the victory banner Of the Buddhist teachings over all.

corpus_segments:14248.english: It doesn't matter how many riches, how much money or how many things, you can manage to collect in this life since, as the sutra called The Tree says, The king leaves behind his kingdom and goes; The beggar leaves behind his stave and goes.

corpus_segments:930.acip: MDOR NA, BSHES GNYEN BSTEN TSUL GYI CHOS SKOR RNAMS NAS JI SKAD BSHAD PA'I BLANG DOR MTHA' DAG MA NOR BAR BYED PA ZHIG DGOS SHING , DE LTAR TSUL BZHIN DU BSTEN PAS NI DPER NA, KHANG PA'I 'GRAM RTZA'AM RTZIG RMANG BRTAN NA KHANG PA BRTAN PO 'ONG BA DANG , SHING GI RTZA BA BRTAN NA YAL GA LO 'BRAS SOGS 'BYUNG BA BZHIN DU
corpus_segments:930.wylie: mdor na, bshes gnyen bsten tshul gyi chos skor rnams nas ji skad bshad pa'i blang dor mtha' dag ma nor bar byed pa zhig dgos shing , de ltar tshul bzhin du bsten pas ni dper na, khang pa'i 'gram rtsa'am rtsig rmang brtan na khang pa brtan po 'ong ba dang , shing gi rtsa ba brtan na yal ga lo 'bras sogs 'byung ba bzhin du
corpus_segments:930.english: To put it briefly, you must absolutely conduct yourself correctly in this regard; you must follow precisely every one of the classical descriptions of how to find and follow a Lama. If the cornerstone of a house--the walls of its foundation--are solid, then the house itself is solid. If the roots of a tree are planted firmly in the soil, then the branches and fruit and all the rest grow strong.

corpus_segments:2684.acip: ,'CHI BDAG LA BROS PAS MI THAR ZHING SNGAGS LA SOGS PAS BZLOG TU MED PA NI, RGYAL PO LA GDAMS PA LAS, DPER NA, PHYOGS BZHI NAS RI CHEN PO SRA BA BRTAN PA SNYING PO DANG LDAN PA MA ZHIG PA MA GAS PA 'PHAN MED PA SHIN TU MKHREGS PA GCIG TU STUG PO BZHI GNAM LA REG CING SA BRLOG STE, RTZVA DANG SHING DANG SHING GEL PA DANG YAL GA DANG LO MA THAMS CAD DANG SEMS CAN SROG CHAGS 'BYUNG PO THAMS CAD PHYE MAR 'THAG CING 'ONG BA LA NI MGYOGS PAS 'BROS PA'AM STOBS KYIS BZLOG PA'AM NOR GYIS BZLOG PA'AM RDZAS DANG SNGAGS DANG SMAN RNAMS KYIS BZLOG PAR SLA BA NI MA YIN NO,
corpus_segments:2684.wylie: 'chi bdag la bros pas mi thar zhing sngags la sogs pas bzlog tu med pa ni, rgyal po la gdams pa las, dper na, phyogs bzhi nas ri chen po sra ba brtan pa snying po dang ldan pa ma zhig pa ma gas pa 'phan med pa shin tu mkhregs pa gcig tu stug po bzhi gnam la reg cing sa brlog ste, rtsva dang shing dang shing gel pa dang yal ga dang lo ma thams cad dang sems can srog chags 'byung po thams cad phye mar 'thag cing 'ong ba la ni mgyogs pas 'bros pa'am stobs kyis bzlog pa'am nor gyis bzlog pa'am rdzas dang sngags dang sman rnams kyis bzlog par sla ba ni ma yin no
corpus_segments:2684.english: Beyond this is the fact that no one can free themselves from the Lord of Death by outrunning him, nor turn him back with magic words or the like. As the scripture known as Advice to the King states, Suppose for example that you were surrounded on all four sides by four great mountains, solid, firm, hard to the core, indestructible, unbreakable, indomitable, adamantine and massive, stretching to the highest limits of the sky. And then suppose suddenly that they caved in on you. Every trace of vegetation--from the roots, to the stalks, to the branches, to the twigs, and out to the leaves, would be crushed to powder. And every living creature there, every sentient being, every spirit too, would be smashed to dust. And as the mountains fell in it would happen in a minute, and no one would be able to outrun them, or force them back, or buy them off. Nor but with the greatest difficulty could you use any kind of magic substance, or magic words, or any sort of elixir to stop them.

corpus_segments:35504.acip: ,DE NI NGA YI NGA RGYAL YIN, ,RANG BZHIN DAG LA DGOS PA CI, ,MED NA NGA RGYAL GANG DU 'JOG
corpus_segments:35504.wylie: de ni nga yi nga rgyal yin, ,rang bzhin dag la dgos pa ci, ,med na nga rgyal gang du 'jog
corpus_segments:35504.english: And then that would be A divine pride That belonged to me! And then what need Would you have for Some pure sort of nature? But if there were Nothing there, Then what would Your divine pride Ever focus upon? The Devil is having trouble understanding that we can entertain a mistaken notion about something that is coming from our own seed-pictures, and yet still that thing can be something good for us.  Wisdom itself—understanding where these things are really coming from—is part of deceptive reality, but is at the same time our savior.

corpus_segments:35547.english: That metaphor we used Is the same as well For our example here— For the feeling of great bliss. But what then is it That the divine pride Holds on to? For that divine pride Is doing its holding During this period Of deep meditation. The "metaphor" which the Angel is referring to here is that of pouring water into water: the subject state of mind—intense bliss—is indivisibly engrossed in sheer emptiness. At the same time, we are supposed to be identifying with some divine elements here, holding that they are my "me" at this moment.  What exactly are those elements? A single song

corpus_segments:34613.english: Every trace of vegetation— from the roots, to the stalks, to the branches, to the twigs, and out to the leaves, would be crushed to powder. And every livingcreature there, would be smashed to dust. And as the mountains fell in it would happen in a minute, and no one would be able to outrun them, or force them back, or buy them off. Nor but with the greatest difficulty could you use any kind of magic substance, or magic words, or any sort of elixir to stop them.

corpus_segments:21284.acip: 'O NA GDAN GYI KHYAD PAR JI 'DRA BA'I STENG DU SGOM PAR BYED CE NA, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I MCHOD SPRIN GYI DBUS DER, YAL GA (LO MA ME TOG 'BRAS BU) RNAMS KYI(S YONGS) SU (MDZES) SHING, ('DOD DGU) STE CI 'DOD 'BYUNG (BA'I DPAG BSAM) GYI SHING (LJON PA'I RTZE) MOR,
corpus_segments:21284.wylie: 'o na gdan gyi khyad par ji 'dra ba'i steng du sgom par byed ce na, sngar bshad pa'i mchod sprin gyi dbus der, yal ga (lo ma me tog 'bras bu) rnams kyi(s yongs) su (mdzes) shing, ('dod dgu) ste ci 'dod 'byung (ba'i dpag bsam) gyi shing (ljon pa'i rtse) mor
corpus_segments:21284.english: "Well then," one may ask, "what kind of cushions are there for us to seat our Lama upon here?"  There within the center of the cloud of offering which we've just described stands the trunk of a tree which grants whatever we want: our thousand wishes.  Its boughs are lovely with different kinds of leaves and flowers and fruit.

Its boughs are lovely with different kinds of leaves and flowers and fruit."}

corpus_segments:21378.acip: ME TOG CI 'DRA BA ZHIG 'BUL BA YIN ZHE NA, DE YANG (SDONG PO) STE GZHUNG SHING CHE CHUNG YAL GA SOGS MANG NYUNG CI RIGS PA'I ME TOG RNAMS DANG, MA BRGYUS PAR BCAL DU BKRAM PA'I (SIL MA) RNAMS DANG, BRGYUS TE (PHRENG BA)R BYAS PA DANG, SNA TSOGS PA BSRES SHING (SPEL) MAR (LEGS PA)R BSHAMS PA RNAMS DANG,
corpus_segments:21378.wylie: me tog ci 'dra ba zhig 'bul ba yin zhe na, de yang (sdong po) ste gzhung shing che chung yal ga sogs mang nyung ci rigs pa'i me tog rnams dang, ma brgyus par bcal du bkram pa'i (sil ma) rnams dang, brgyus te (phreng ba)r byas pa dang, sna tshogs pa bsres shing (spel) mar (legs pa)r bshams pa rnams dang
corpus_segments:21378.english: "What kinds of flowers," you may ask, "do we offer here?"  Now the flowers appear on stems--that is, on a certain number of branches that come off of main trunks of various sizes.  Some of the flowers are scattered everywhere, strewn across the expanse, without being made into garlands.  Some though are strung or tied into garlands, while others form a patchwork of colors, mixed in profusion.

corpus_segments:25153.acip: GANG ZAG DE GANG GI TSE MI RNAMS KYI NANG DU SKYES NA, DBUL PO BZA' BA DANG BTUNG BA NYUNG BA SDUG BSNGAL BAS 'TSO BA'I RIGS SU SKYE BAR GYUR TE, DE DER SKYES NAS TSEGS CHEN POS BZA' BA DANG BGO BA RNYED PAR 'GYUR LA, DE'I LONGS SPYOD DE DAG PHYIS KYANG MA 'PHEL BA STE,
corpus_segments:25153.wylie: gang zag de gang gi tshe mi rnams kyi nang du skyes na, dbul po bza' ba dang btung ba nyung ba sdug bsngal bas 'tsho ba'i rigs su skye bar gyur te, de der skyes nas tshegs chen pos bza' ba dang bgo ba rnyed par 'gyur la, de'i longs spyod de dag phyis kyang ma 'phel ba ste
corpus_segments:25153.english: And then suppose that such a person is reborn as a human being.  In this case, they will be born poor—without enough to eat or drink, and supporting themselves only with great difficulty.  That is, they must undergo tremendous troubles to find food, or clothing; and for the length of their life they will never be able to accumulate any material security. Refusing to give, then living in poverty

corpus_segments:1140.acip: MDO SNGAGS SAM, LTA SPYOD KYI GDAMS PA ZAB CING RGYA CHE BA'I CHOS KYI DPAL 'BYOR LA NGOMS PA MED PAR LONGS SPYOD CING ,
corpus_segments:1140.wylie: mdo sngags sam, lta spyod kyi gdams pa zab cing rgya che ba'i chos kyi dpal 'byor la ngoms pa med par longs spyod cing
corpus_segments:1140.english: And in these lives may I bask in the glory of the Dharma: may I seek unceasingly to drink of the Dharma either in the sense of the open and secret teachings, or the teachings that are "deep" and "wide"--the instructions on correct view and living the life of a bodhisattva.

corpus_segments:2429.acip: ,LONGS SPYOD DAG LA PHYI DANG NANG DANG NI, ,ZAS SKOM SGRIB PA CAN GYI BYE BRAG GIS, ,RNAM GSUM KUN KYANG BKRES SKOM LHAG PA YI, ,ME YIS RAB GDUNG SDUG BSNGAL BGRANG LAS 'DAS,
corpus_segments:2429.wylie: longs spyod dag la phyi dang nang dang ni, ,zas skom sgrib pa can gyi bye brag gis, ,rnam gsum kun kyang bkres skom lhag pa yi, ,me yis rab gdung sdug bsngal bgrang las 'das
corpus_segments:2429.english: They're of three types, distinguished by the obstacles to what They live on: outer problems and inner, problems with food Or drink. All of them share though the infinite pain Of hunger and thirst, intense as the flames of a fire.

All of them share though the infinite pain Of hunger and thirst, intense as the flames of a fire."}

corpus_segments:2430.acip: ,'DI LA SDUG BSNGAL GYI KHYAD PAR MDOR BSDU NA GSUM LAS LONGS SPYOD DAG LA PHYI'I SGRIB PA CAN NI CHU MIG DANG MTSE'U DANG CHU KLUNG LA SOGS PAR BZA' BA DANG , BTUNG BA DAG MTHONG ZHING DE DANG DER BRGYUG PA NA LAG NA RAL GRI DANG DBYUG PA LA SOGS PA THOGS PAS 'GOG PA DANG , CHU LA SOGS PA'ANG RNAG LA SOGS PAR MTHONG BAS SPYAD DU MED PA'O,
corpus_segments:2430.wylie: 'di la sdug bsngal gyi khyad par mdor bsdu na gsum las longs spyod dag la phyi'i sgrib pa can ni chu mig dang mtshe'u dang chu klung la sogs par bza' ba dang , btung ba dag mthong zhing de dang der brgyug pa na lag na ral gri dang dbyug pa la sogs pa thogs pas 'gog pa dang , chu la sogs pa'ang rnag la sogs par mthong bas spyad du med pa'o
corpus_segments:2430.english: The sufferings of these craving spirits can all be reduced to three different kinds. First are those with outer obstacles to what they need to live on. People like this approach a place like a mountain spring, or a pond or stream, and catch sight of something that they could eat or drink. They race ahead to get it, only to be forced back by beings cutting them with knives, or beating them with clubs and such. Or else they come to the side of some water and find themselves unable to drink of it, for then it looks to them like blood and pus or the like.
corpus_segments:2430.raw: {"course": "C08", "acip": ",'DI LA SDUG BSNGAL GYI KHYAD PAR MDOR BSDU NA GSUM LAS LONGS SPYOD DAG LA PHYI'I SGRIB PA CAN NI CHU MIG DANG MTSE'U DANG CHU KLUNG LA SOGS PAR BZA' BA DANG , BTUNG BA DAG MTHONG ZHING DE DANG DER BRGYUG PA NA LAG NA RAL GRI DANG DBYUG PA LA SOGS PA THOGS PAS 'GOG PA DANG , CHU LA SOGS PA'ANG RNAG LA SOGS PAR MTHONG BAS SPYAD DU MED PA'O,", "wylie": "'di la sdug bsngal gyi khyad par mdor bsdu na gsum las longs spyod dag la phyi'i sgrib pa can ni chu mig dang mtshe'u dang chu klung la sogs par bza' ba dang , btung ba dag mthong zhing de dang der brgyug pa na lag na ral gri dang dbyug pa la sogs pa thogs pas 'gog pa dang , chu la sogs pa'ang rnag la sogs par mthong bas spyad du med pa'o", "english": "The sufferings of these craving spirits can all be reduced to three different kinds. First are those with outer obstacles to what they need to live on. People like this approach a place like a mountain spring, or a pond or stream, and catch sight of something that they could eat or drink. They race ahead to get it, only to be forced back by beings cutting them with knives, or beating them with clubs and such. Or else they come to the side of some water and find themselves unable to drink of it, for then it looks to them like blood and pus or the like."}

corpus_segments:5994.acip: DE LTAR BYAS NA, ZAS SKOM NYID LA YOD PA'I SGRIB PA CAN GYI YI DVAGS KYIS LONGS SPYOD PA LA MA BRTZAMS KYI BAR DU BZA' BTUNG DNGOS YIN KYANG , DES LONGS SPYOD PAR BRTZAMS PA NA, ZAS DE'I RIGS 'DRA PHYI MA RNAG KHRAG TU SKYE BA YIN GYI, RNAG KHRAG TU SNANG BA'I SNANG BA TZAM GYIS BZA' BTUNG GI BYA BA BYED PA MA YIN TE, DE YIN NA LAS 'BRAS LA SKUR BA BTAB PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, DE LTA BU'I YI DVAGS KYIS LAS 'BRAS LA SKUR BA BTAB PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR,
corpus_segments:5994.wylie: de ltar byas na, zas skom nyid la yod pa'i sgrib pa can gyi yi dvags kyis longs spyod pa la ma brtsams kyi bar du bza' btung dngos yin kyang , des longs spyod par brtsams pa na, zas de'i rigs 'dra phyi ma rnag khrag tu skye ba yin gyi, rnag khrag tu snang ba'i snang ba tsam gyis bza' btung gi bya ba byed pa ma yin te, de yin na las 'bras la skur ba btab par 'gyur ba'i phyir, der thal, de lta bu'i yi dvags kyis las 'bras la skur ba btab par 'gyur ba'i phyir
corpus_segments:5994.english: Given all this, consider craving spirits that have obstacles that relate to their food and drink itself. The food and drink there really is food and drink, until such time as the spirit starts trying to eat or drink it. When he does try to do so, then the continuum of the food into the next moment starts becoming pus and blood. It is not though that it is the simple appearance of something as pus and blood that could ever function as something to eat or drink. If this were the case, then the rules of karma and its consequences would have to be less than what they really are. And this is true, for if a craving spirit like this ever existed it would represent a failure of the laws of karma and its consequences.

corpus_segments:5998.acip: KHO NA RE, DE'I TSE NA CHU DNGOS GNAS PA YOD DE, CHUS LUS 'KHRUD PA DANG 'TSOD PAR BYED PA MI RANG GIS MYONG BAS 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR ZER NA, 'O NA, DE'I TSE NA, RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS YOD PAR THAL, DE'I TSE NA, RNAG KHRAG LA LONGS SPYOD PA DANG , LTO BA DANG MGRIN PA LA SOGS PA 'TSIG PA YI DVAGS RANG GIS MYONG BAS 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR,
corpus_segments:5998.wylie: kho na re, de'i tshe na chu dngos gnas pa yod de, chus lus 'khrud pa dang 'tshod par byed pa mi rang gis myong bas 'grub pa'i phyir zer na, 'o na, de'i tshe na, rnag khrag dngos gnas yod par thal, de'i tshe na, rnag khrag la longs spyod pa dang , lto ba dang mgrin pa la sogs pa 'tshig pa yi dvags rang gis myong bas 'grub pa'i phyir
corpus_segments:5998.english: Someone might now make the following claim: In this situation, there does exist some real water there. This is because the human can confirm the water with his own experience, as it performs all the functions of water--as he uses it to wash himself, or as he uses it to cook something. Well then, in the same situation there must exist some real pus and blood there as well, because in this same situation the craving spirit can confirm the pus and blood with his own experience as they perform their functions--as he drinks them, and then as the sizzle in his throat and stomach, and so on.

corpus_segments:7314.english: The sufferings of these craving spirits can all be reduced to three different kinds. First are those with outer obstacles to what they need to live on. People like this approach a place like a mountain spring, or a pond or stream, and catch sight of something that they could eat or drink. They race ahead to get it, only to be forced back by beings cutting them with knives, or beating them with clubs and such. Or else they come to the side of some water and find themselves unable to drink of it, for then it looks to them like blood and pus or the like.

First are those with outer obstacles to what they need to live on. People like this approach a place like a mountain spring, or a pond or stream, and catch sight of something that they could eat or drink. They race ahead to get it, only to be forced back by beings cutting them with knives, or beating them with clubs and such. corpus_segments:27897.acip: DANG PO NI, SKYE BO 'DI RNAMS KUN NI, BKRES SKOM DANG NAD DANG TSA GRANG SOGS KYI SDUG BSNGAL PHYIR BCOS PA'I BDE BA THOB PAR MNGON PAR 'DOD CING, MI LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYI BDE BA DE'ANG 'DOD PA'I YUL GYI LONGS SPYOD BZA' BTUNG DANG, NAD GSO BA'I CHAS DANG GOS DANG GNAS KHANG SOGS LA, SPYAD PA MED PAR SKYE BA MIN LA,
corpus_segments:27897.wylie: dang po ni, skye bo 'di rnams kun ni, bkres skom dang nad dang tsha grang sogs kyi sdug bsngal phyir bcos pa'i bde ba thob par mngon par 'dod cing, mi la sogs pa rnams kyi bde ba de'ang 'dod pa'i yul gyi longs spyod bza' btung dang, nad gso ba'i chas dang gos dang gnas khang sogs la, spyad pa med par skye ba min la
corpus_segments:27897.english: Here is the first. All people here have a hope for happiness, first in the form of alleviating their hunger & thirst; of comfort when they are too hot or too cold; and so on. And without enjoying the use of things, in the form of the things that they want—be it things to drink or eat; or the things they need to treat some illness; or clothing; or houses to stay in; or all the like—human beings do not feel happy.

corpus_segments:22833.acip: BDAG GI MTHUS BDAG GI MING YID LA GNAS SHING BDAG GI MING YID KYIS BRJOD PAS DE DAG BLA NA MED PA YANG DAG PAR RDZOGS PA'I BYANG CHUB MNGON PAR RDZOGS PAR SANGS RGYAS KYI BAR DU BSAMS MA THAG TU BGO BA DANG, BZA' BA DANG, BTUNG BA DANG, LONGS SPYOD DANG, YONGS SU SPYAD PA DANG, NOR DANG, 'BRU DANG, DBYIG DANG, GSER RNAMS 'BYUNG BAR GYUR CIG
corpus_segments:22833.wylie: bdag gi mthus bdag gi ming yid la gnas shing bdag gi ming yid kyis brjod pas de dag bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas kyi bar du bsams ma thag tu bgo ba dang, bza' ba dang, btung ba dang, longs spyod dang, yongs su spyad pa dang, nor dang, 'bru dang, dbyig dang, gser rnams 'byung bar gyur cig
corpus_segments:22833.english: May all these beings, by my mystic power, have ready in their minds my name; and may they speak that name in their hearts.  And by doing so, may they—all the way up to the day that they attain their own total enlightenment, matchless, as a pure and total Buddha—come to have all the clothes that they require; and all they need to eat, or drink; and every other needed possession, and enjoyment; and all the money, and crops; all the prosperity and gold that they ever hope for, in the moment after they first feel such hope.

corpus_segments:34928.acip: DE LTAR BYAS NA ZAS SKOM NYID LA YOD PA'I SGRIB PA CAN GYI YI DWAGS KYIS LONGS, SPYOD PA LA MA BRTZAMS KYI BAR DU BZA' BTUNG DNGOS YIN KYANG DES LONGS SPYOD PAR BRTZAMS PA NA ZAS DE'I RIGS 'DRA PHYI MA RNAG KHRAG TU SKYE BA YIN GYI RNAG KHRAG TU SNANG BA'I SNANG BA TZAM GYIS BZA' BTUNG GI BYA BA BYED PA MA YIN TE DE YIN NA LAS 'BRAS LA SKUR BA BTAB PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR DER THAL DE LTA BU'I YI DWAGS KYIS LAS 'BRAS LA SKUR BA BTAB PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR

corpus_segments:34928.english: Given all this, consider craving spirits that have obstacles that relate to their food and drink itself. The food and drink there really is food and drink, until such time as the spirit starts trying to eat or drink it. When he does try to do so, then the continuum of the food into the next moment starts becoming pus and blood. It is not though that it is the simple appearance of something as pus and blood that could ever function as something to eat or drink. If this were the case, then the rules of karma and its consequences would have to be less that what they really are. And this is true, for if a craving spirit like this ever existed it would represent a failure of the laws of karma and its

corpus_segments:34930.acip: KHO NA RE DE'I TSE NA CHU DNGOS GNAS PA YOD DE CHUS LUS 'KHRUD PA DANG 'TSOD PAR, BYED PA MI RANG GIS MYONG BAS 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR ZER NA 'O NA DE'I TSE NA RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS YOD PAR THAL DE'I TSE NA RNAG KHRAG LA LONGS SPYOD PA DANG LTO BA DANG MGRIN PA LA SOGS PA 'TSIG PA YI DWAGS RANG GIS MYONG BAS 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR
corpus_segments:34930.wylie: kho na re de'i tshe na chu dngos gnas pa yod de chus lus 'khrud pa dang 'tshod par, byed pa mi rang gis myong bas 'grub pa'i phyir zer na 'o na de'i tshe na rnag khrag dngos gnas yod par thal de'i tshe na rnag khrag la longs spyod pa dang lto ba dang mgrin pa la sogs pa 'tshig pa yi dwags rang gis myong bas 'grub pa'i phyir
corpus_segments:34930.english: Someone might now make the following claim: In this situation, there does exist some real water there. This is because the human can confirm the water with his own experience, as it performs all the functions of water—as he uses it to wash himself, or as he uses it to cook something. Well then, in the same situation there must exist some real pus and blood there as well, because in this same situation the craving spirit can confirm the pus and blood with his own experience as they perform their functions—as he drinks them, and then as the sizzle in his throat and stomach, and so on.

corpus_segments:11986.acip: BZA' BA'I DAM TSIG SHA LNGA DANG BDUD RTZI LNGA BSTEN DGOS PAR RNAL 'BYOR BLA MED KYI SKABS SU GSUNGS PA RNAMS LA GRUB NA LAS DANG PO PAS RI LU BYAS NAS NYI MA RE RE ZHING BSTEN PAR GSUNGS PA LTAR BYA LA, MA GRUB NA BZA' BTUNG LA DE DAG BSAM GTAN TZAM GYIS BSKYED NAS LONGS SPYOD PAR BYAS PAS KYANG 'GRUB,
corpus_segments:11986.wylie: bza' ba'i dam tshig sha lnga dang bdud rtsi lnga bsten dgos par rnal 'byor bla med kyi skabs su gsungs pa rnams la grub na las dang po pas ri lu byas nas nyi ma re re zhing bsten par gsungs pa ltar bya la, ma grub na bza' btung la de dag bsam gtan tsam gyis bskyed nas longs spyod par byas pas kyang 'grub
corpus_segments:11986.english: We also have a pledge which relates to eating; that is, it is spoken in the secret teachings of the unsurpassed class that we are required to partake of the five types of flesh and the five types of nectar.  If it is possible, those who are just starting out should follow the advice in scripture about partaking, each day, of these substances in the form of a sacred pill.  In a case where it is not possible, we can also perform this practice by transforming our regular food and drink with our concentration into these substances, and then partaking of them. ***

corpus_segments:12036.wylie: khro med bu gar kun tu spyod, ,ces pa ni, bu gar kun tu spyod pa ste yum gyi pad+ma nas byang sems lces len pa'i dus su khro ba med pa ste gtsog pa'i 'du shes mi bya bar 'thung zhing longs spyod par bya'o zhes pa ste dam tshig brgyad pa'o
corpus_segments:12036.english: The folllowing line [in the Tibetan] advises us to "Partake of the opening without dislike."  This is a reference to times when we are "partaking of the opening" in the sense of using our tongue to take the element of enlightenment out of our consort's lotus.  We must drink of this essence, we must partake of it,  "without dislike"--meaning without any kind of idea that it is something dirty.  This is the eighth of the pledges. ************

corpus_segments:14153.acip: (CES BRJOD, DE NAS LAS KYI RDO RJES LAG PA GNYIS PADMA'I PHYAG RGYA LAS SRIN LAG GA-YAS KYIS STENG GI BA LA 'DZIN PAS RDO RJE SLOB DPON NAS MAS RIM BZHIN MA DA NA BRIMS TSAR BA DANG, TSOGS KYI RDZAS NAS MA TSANG BA MED PA SLOB DPON LA NYIS 'GYUR SOGS DPON SLOB THAMS CAD LA LAG PA GNYIS KAS 'BUL ZHING, LEN PA POS KYANG, AA HO MA H'A SU KHA HO: ZHES BRJOD CING, LAG PA GNYIS PAD KOR GYIS BLANGS, 'DI DAG GI SKABS SNOD MIN GYIS DBEN PAR BYAS, SGRUB PA PO RNAMS KYIS KYANG GTZANG RME'I RNAM RTOG MI BYA BAR SNYING GA'I BAm YIG SANGS RGYAS THAMS CAD 'DUS PA'I NGO BO MCHOD PAR BSAMS LA RDZAS THAMS CAD TSIM PAR LONGS SPYOD, KHYAD PAR DGE SLONG RDO RJE 'DZIN PA LTA BUS, MA DA NA DANG TSOGS RDZAS KHYAD DU BSAD NA RTZA LTUNG BCU GSUM PAR 'GYUR BAR GSUNGS PAS LCE LA NANG MCHOD REG TZAM BYAS NAS BDUD RTZI MYONG BA NGES PAR BYA YI, BAG MED DU BTUNG BA NI KHYIM PA LA'ANG BKAG NA RAB TU BYUNG BA LA LTA CI SMOD PA'I PHYIR RO,
corpus_segments:14153.wylie: (ces brjod, de nas las kyi rdo rjes lag pa gnyis padma'i phyag rgya las srin lag ga-yas kyis steng gi ba la 'dzin pas rdo rje slob dpon nas mas rim bzhin ma da na brims tshar ba dang, tshogs kyi rdzas nas ma tshang ba med pa slob dpon la nyis 'gyur sogs dpon slob thams cad la lag pa gnyis kas 'bul zhing, len pa pos kyang, aa ho ma hA su kha ho: zhes brjod cing, lag pa gnyis pad kor gyis blangs, 'di dag gi skabs snod min gyis dben par byas, sgrub pa po rnams kyis kyang gtsang rme'i rnam rtog mi bya bar snying ga'i baM yig sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus pa'i ngo bo mchod par bsams la rdzas thams cad tshim par longs spyod, khyad par dge slong rdo rje 'dzin pa lta bus, ma da na dang tshogs rdzas khyad du bsad na rtsa ltung bcu gsum par 'gyur bar gsungs pas lce la nang mchod reg tsam byas nas bdud rtsi myong ba nges par bya yi, bag med du btung ba ni khyim pa la'ang bkag na rab tu byung ba la lta ci smod pa'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:14153.english: (Then the Diamond Attendant puts his hands in the Sign of the Lotus, using the ring finger of his right hand to hold up the bala.  He distributes the bala to the Master and disciples, in order of seniority.  Then the madana is distributed, and then the offerings of the Gathering, with nothing left incomplete, following such customs as presenting the Master with a double portion. The Attendants offer these things to the Master and all the disciples using both their hands, and upon accepting the things they also say, ah ho maha suka ho, and pick them up with both hands, using the Sign of the Circling Lotus. During these performances, all those who are not proper vessels should be excluded.  The practitioners should avoid any wrong notions that the substances might be something unclean; instead they should partake of them all, heartily, and think that they are making an offering to the letter bam in their heart, a letter which is, in reality, a combination of all the Buddhas there are. This applies especially to ordained persons who are keeping the practice of the Diamond: it is spoken that, if someone rejects the madana and offerings of the Gathering, then he has committed the thirteenth root downfall.  Therefore the ordained must be sure to touch a drop of the madana to their tongues, and thereby perform the partaking of nectar.  But drinking these things carelessly is prohibited even for laymen, much less for those who have left the home life.)

thams cad tshim par longs spyod, khyad par dge slong rdo rje 'dzin pa lta bus, ma da na dang tshogs rdzas khyad du bsad na rtsa ltung bcu gsum par 'gyur bar gsungs pas lce la nang mchod reg tsam byas nas bdud rtsi myong ba nges par bya yi, bag med du btung ba ni khyim pa la'ang bkag na rab tu byung ba la lta ci smod pa'i phyir ro", "english": "(Then the Diamond Attendant puts his hands in the Sign of the Lotus, using the ring finger of his right hand to hold up the bala.  He distributes the bala to the Master and disciples, in order of seniority.  Then the madana is distributed, and then the offerings of the Gathering, with nothing left incomplete, following such customs as presenting the Master with a double portion. The Attendants offer these things to the Master and all the disciples using both their hands, and upon accepting the things they also say, ah ho maha suka ho, and pick them up with both hands, using the Sign of the Circling Lotus. During these performances, all those who are not proper vessels should be excluded.  The practitioners should avoid any wrong notions that the substances might be something unclean; instead they should partake of them all, heartily, and think that they are making an offering to the letter bam in their heart, a letter which is, in reality, a combination of all the Buddhas there are. This applies especially to ordained persons who are keeping the practice of the Diamond: it is spoken that, if someone rejects the madana and offerings of the Gathering, then he has committed the thirteenth root downfall.  Therefore the ordained must be sure to touch a drop of the madana to their tongues, and thereby perform the partaking of nectar.  But drinking these things carelessly is prohibited even for laymen, much less for those who have left the home life.)"}

corpus_segments:16066.acip: SPYI PO RA BDE BA'I RTEN BYANG SEMS GTZO BOR GNAS PAS NA SPYI BO BDE CHEN GYI 'KHOR LO, MGRIN PA'I LAM NAS KHA ZAS LONGS SPYOD PAS NA LONGS SPYOD KYI 'KHOR LO, CHOS THAMS CAD KYI RTZA BA SHIN TU PHRA BA'I RLUNG SEMS SNYING KHAR GNAS PAS NA SNYING KHA CHOS KYI 'KHOR LO, LTE BAR MA LAS THOB PA'I KHAMS DMAR PO YOD PA LAS LUS BSKYED CING BDE BA CHEN PO BSKYED PA'I GZHI LTE BAR GNAS PAS NA SPRUL PA'I 'KHOR LO ZHES BRJOD,
corpus_segments:16066.wylie: spyi po ra bde ba'i rten byang sems gtso bor gnas pas na spyi bo bde chen gyi 'khor lo, mgrin pa'i lam nas kha zas longs spyod pas na longs spyod kyi 'khor lo, chos thams cad kyi rtsa ba shin tu phra ba'i rlung sems snying khar gnas pas na snying kha chos kyi 'khor lo, lte bar ma las thob pa'i khams dmar po yod pa las lus bskyed cing bde ba chen po bskyed pa'i gzhi lte bar gnas pas na sprul pa'i 'khor lo zhes brjod
corpus_segments:16066.english: The chakra at the tip of your head is called the chakra of great bliss because it is there where the white element primarily stays and is thus the foundation of bliss.  The chakra at your throat is called the chakra of experience because it is at your throat where you experience food and drink.  The chakra at your heart is called the chakra of existing phenomena because the most subtle mind and winds which are the root of all existing things stay at the heart.  The chakra at your navel is called the emanation chakra because it is where the red element which you received from your mother that produced your body and is the foundation of great bliss is produced.
