corpus_segments:16590.acip: 'DI LA RGYAS 'BRING BSDUS GSUM YOD, SNGAGS KYI SKABS 'DIR KHA ZAS RNAMS NANG MCHOD LTAR BYIN GYIS BRLAB PA'AM, AOm A'A: H'Um HA HO: HR'I: LTA BU DANG, MA MTHA' 'BRU GSUM GYIS BYIN MA BRLABS PAR LONGS SPYOD NA BZA' BTUNG KHAM RE DANG HUB RE LA SNGAGS KYI SBOM PO RE 'BYUNG TSUL DANG,
corpus_segments:16590.wylie: 'di la rgyas 'bring bsdus gsum yod, sngags kyi skabs 'dir kha zas rnams nang mchod ltar byin gyis brlab pa'am, aoM a'a: hUM ha ho: hrI: lta bu dang, ma mtha' 'bru gsum gyis byin ma brlabs par longs spyod na bza' btung kham re dang hub re la sngags kyi sbom po re 'byung tshul dang
corpus_segments:16590.english: There are three versions of the practice of food: the briefer, the medium, and the more extensive.  Here in the practice of the secret word we must bless our food, either as we do the inner offerings; or else with secret words like Om ah hung ha hoh hrih; or at the very least with the three seed syllables.  Our Lama described how--if we partake of the food without having blessed it in one of these ways--we then commit a serious offense against our tantric vows.  We commit one such offense for each bite of food and each gulp of drink we take.

corpus_segments:16770.acip: LAG MCHOD MI 'GRUB PA'I SKABS KYANG BZA' BTUNG LA LONGS SPYOD TSE GONG GI LAG PA BYIN RLABS DANG, KHA ZAS BDUD RTZIR BYIN BRLABS PA, RNAL 'BYOR MA'I LHA TSOGS RANG LUS LA SPYAN DRANGS TE BZHUGS PA'AM, LUS DKYIL GSAL BTAB PA LA PHUL BAS THUGS ZAG MED KYI BDE BAS TSIM PAR MOS PA SOGS
corpus_segments:16770.wylie: lag mchod mi 'grub pa'i skabs kyang bza' btung la longs spyod tshe gong gi lag pa byin rlabs dang, kha zas bdud rtsir byin brlabs pa, rnal 'byor ma'i lha tshogs rang lus la spyan drangs te bzhugs pa'am, lus dkyil gsal btab pa la phul bas thugs zag med kyi bde bas tshim par mos pa sogs
corpus_segments:16770.english: Even on those occasions when you do not perform the offering of the hand, there are certain steps you should take whenever to partake of food or drink.  As mentioned above, bless your hand, and also bless the food so that it becomes sacred nectar.  Invite the entire Angelic assembly of the Holy Angel to come down and be in you, or else visualize the Angels of the secret world of your body, and offer the nectar to these Beings.  Believe then that Their holy minds have been filled with immaculate bliss.

corpus_segments:16830.acip: TING NGE 'DZIN GYI DKYIL 'KHOR MCHOD PAS TSIM PA, SNYING GA'I YE SHES KYI DKYIL 'KHOR RAM YE SHES SEMS DPA' BDUD RTZI MYANG BAS TSIM PA, RNAL 'BYOR PHO MO RNAMS BZA' BTUNG GI LONGS SPYOD KYIS TSIM PA,
corpus_segments:16830.wylie: ting nge 'dzin gyi dkyil 'khor mchod pas tshim pa, snying ga'i ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor ram ye shes sems dpa' bdud rtsi myang bas tshim pa, rnal 'byor pho mo rnams bza' btung gi longs spyod kyis tshim pa
corpus_segments:16830.english: We must please others to their fill, in six different ways.  The Circle of Concentration should be granted their fill with the offerings.  The Circle of Wisdom at the heart--or the Warriors of Wisdom--should be granted their fill through partaking of the nectar.  The yogis and yoginis should be granted their fill through partaking of the food and drink.

corpus_segments:20932.english: The folllowing line [in the Tibetan] advises us to "Partake of the opening without dislike."  This is a reference to times when we are "partaking of the opening" in the sense of using our tongue to take the element of enlightenment out of our consort's lotus.  We must drink of this essence, we must partake of it, "without dislike"--meaning without any kind of idea that it is something dirty.  This is the eighth of the pledges. *  *  *  *  *

corpus_segments:2434.english: All of them have the look of a scorched piece of wood; the searing pain of hunger and thirst have dried up all their skin and flesh and blood. They run from place to place, terrified, and aimless.

corpus_segments:12167.acip: RTZA LTUNG SPONG BA'I DAM TSIG NI SNGAGS PA RNAMS KYI GNAD DAM PA YIN PAS 'BAD NAS BSRUNGS TE DANG PO NAS MA GOS PAR BYA BA DANG GAL TE NYAMS NA'ANG JI MI SNYAM PAR MI 'JOG PAR PHYIR BCOS TSUL BZHIN DU BYAS NAS GSO DGOS TE DE LTAR MA BYAS NA DE'I LHAG MA RNAL 'BYOR BZHI SGOM PA SOGS KYIS 'BRAS BU 'BYIN MI NUS PA TA LA YA THOG BSKAMS PA'I DPES GSUNGS SO,
corpus_segments:12167.wylie: rtsa ltung spong ba'i dam tshig ni sngags pa rnams kyi gnad dam pa yin pas 'bad nas bsrungs te dang po nas ma gos par bya ba dang gal te nyams na'ang ji mi snyam par mi 'jog par phyir bcos tshul bzhin du byas nas gso dgos te de ltar ma byas na de'i lhag ma rnal 'byor bzhi sgom pa sogs kyis 'bras bu 'byin mi nus pa ta la ya thog bskams pa'i dpes gsungs so
corpus_segments:12167.english: The pledge to give up ever committing one of the root downfalls is a high spiritual key for those who follow the way of the secret way.  As such, we must devote ourselves to honoring our commitments: working never to be sullied by the downfalls in the first place, and--in the event that we do fail on occasion--never just letting it go, but rather restoring our commitments in the proper way.  If we fail in this one mission, then we can throw ourselves into the rest as much as we want--all four of the high yogic practices, or anything of the like--but it will never produce in us the fruits we desire.  We will be like, the scriptures say, the example of the dried-out top of a palm tree. ***
corpus_segments:12167.raw: {"course": "TCS05", "acip": "RTZA LTUNG SPONG BA'I DAM TSIG NI SNGAGS PA RNAMS KYI GNAD DAM PA YIN PAS 'BAD NAS BSRUNGS TE DANG PO NAS MA GOS PAR BYA BA DANG GAL TE NYAMS NA'ANG JI MI SNYAM PAR MI 'JOG PAR PHYIR BCOS TSUL BZHIN DU BYAS NAS GSO DGOS TE DE LTAR MA BYAS NA DE'I LHAG MA RNAL 'BYOR BZHI SGOM PA SOGS KYIS 'BRAS BU 'BYIN MI NUS PA TA LA YA THOG BSKAMS PA'I DPES GSUNGS SO,", "wylie": "rtsa ltung spong ba'i dam tshig ni sngags pa rnams kyi gnad dam pa yin pas 'bad nas bsrungs te dang po nas ma gos par bya ba dang gal te nyams na'ang ji mi snyam par mi 'jog par phyir bcos tshul bzhin du byas nas gso dgos te de ltar ma byas na de'i lhag ma rnal 'byor bzhi sgom pa sogs kyis 'bras bu 'byin mi nus pa ta la ya thog bskams pa'i dpes gsungs so", "english": "The pledge to give up ever committing one of the root downfalls is a high spiritual key for those who follow the way of the secret way.  As such, we must devote ourselves to honoring our commitments: working never to be sullied by the downfalls in the first place, and--in the event that we do fail on occasion--never just letting it go, but rather restoring our commitments in the proper way.  If we fail in this one mission, then we can throw ourselves into the rest as much as we want--all four of the high yogic practices, or anything of the like--but it will never produce in us the fruits we desire.  We will be like, the scriptures say, the example of the dried-out top of a palm tree. ***"}

corpus_segments:385.acip: DPER NA THAG KHRA LA MUN PA BABS PA MTHONG BA NA DANG POR THAG KHRA LA SBRUL LO SNYAM DU PHAR BTAGS, DE RJES PHAR BTAGS PA DE BRJED NAS THAG KHRA'I NGOS NAS SBRUL TSUR GRUB PAR SNANG BAS DE LTAR SNANG BA DE DGAG BYA MA YIN, DE LTAR SNANG BA LTAR DU GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I ZHEN YUL DE DGAG BYA YIN PA BZHIN DU,
corpus_segments:385.wylie: dper na thag khra la mun pa babs pa mthong ba na dang por thag khra la sbrul lo snyam du phar btags, de rjes phar btags pa de brjed nas thag khra'i ngos nas sbrul tshur grub par snang bas de ltar snang ba de dgag bya ma yin, de ltar snang ba ltar du grub par 'dzin pa'i zhen yul de dgag bya yin pa bzhin du
corpus_segments:385.english: Let's say for example that dusk has fallen and you see some piece of rope with a checkered pattern. At first you put a name onto it and think to yourself, "Oh my! A snake!" After that you forget it was you who put the name on it and it starts to look like a snake out there on its own. The way that it looks just then is not what we want to see doesn't exist. Rather what we want to deny is what we grasp: that the thing we hold could really exist the way it looks to us to exist.

corpus_segments:1626.acip: GZHAN YANG DE CHOS CAN, GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED RDZOGS PAR MA RTOGS PAR THAL, GANG ZAG RANG BZHIN MED PAR MNGON SUM DU MA RTOGS PA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, GDAGS GZHI PHUNG PO RANG NGOS NAS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN 'BYIN MI NUS PA'I TSUL GYI PHYIN CI LOG GIS BCINGS PA YIN PA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, PHUNG PO RANG BZHIN MED PAR YONGS SU SHES PA DANG BRAL BA'I PHYIR,
corpus_segments:1626.wylie: gzhan yang de chos can, gang zag gi bdag med rdzogs par ma rtogs par thal, gang zag rang bzhin med par mngon sum du ma rtogs pa'i phyir, der thal, gdags gzhi phung po rang ngos nas grub par 'dzin pa'i zhen yul sun 'byin mi nus pa'i tshul gyi phyin ci log gis bcings pa yin pa'i phyir, der thal, phung po rang bzhin med par yongs su shes pa dang bral ba'i phyir
corpus_segments:1626.english: Consider these same enemy destroyers. It is true that they have not yet realized, entirely, the fact that the person has no self nature. This is because they have yet to perceive directly the fact that the person has no nature. This in itself is true as well, for they are still chained by total misperceptions, in such a way that they will never be able to root out the object that they think they see when they hold the parts to the person, the thing which gets the label of "me," as existing from its own side. And this too is true, for they lack that comprehensive knowledge where they realize that the parts to the person have no nature of their own.

corpus_segments:1627.acip: THAL 'GYUR SNGA MA LA KHYAB PA YOD DE, GDAGS GZHI PHUNG PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN PHYUNG MI NUS PA JI SRID 'JUG GI BAR DU, BTAGS CHOS GANG ZAG RANG NGOS NAS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN PHYUNG MI NUS PAR 'JUG PA GANG ZHIG, DE JI SRID 'JUG GI BAR DU DE'I DBANG GIS LAS BSOG, LAS DE'I DBANG GIS 'KHOR BAR 'KHOR BA'I PHYIR,
corpus_segments:1627.wylie: thal 'gyur snga ma la khyab pa yod de, gdags gzhi phung po rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa'i zhen yul sun phyung mi nus pa ji srid 'jug gi bar du, btags chos gang zag rang ngos nas grub par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa'i zhen yul sun phyung mi nus par 'jug pa gang zhig, de ji srid 'jug gi bar du de'i dbang gis las bsog, las de'i dbang gis 'khor bar 'khor ba'i phyir
corpus_segments:1627.english: The first of our logical statements above is always true. For suppose that a person is still unable to root out the object that he thinks he sees when he holds the parts to the person, the thing which gets the label of "me," as existing through some nature of its own. As long as he goes on this way, then he will continue to find himself unable to root out the object that he thinks he sees when he holds the thing which gets the label, the "me," as existing from its own side. And as long as he continues with this, then by the power of this misperception he will continue to collect karma. And as long as he collects karma, then he will continue to spin around in this wheel of suffering life. *********

corpus_segments:2022.acip: ,DE LTAR 'TSANG RGYA BA LA GANG DU 'TSANG RGYA BA'I ZHING DAG PA SGRUB DGOS PAR STON PA NI, BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS RAB 'BYOR LA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG LA LA ZHIG BDAG GIS ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS BDEN ZHEN GYIS DON DAM PAR BSGRUB PAR BYA'O SNYAM ZHING ZER NA, TSIG DE NI MI BDEN PAR SMRA BA'O,
corpus_segments:2022.wylie: de ltar 'tshang rgya ba la gang du 'tshang rgya ba'i zhing dag pa sgrub dgos par ston pa ni, bcom ldan 'das kyis rab 'byor la byang chub sems dpa' gang la la zhig bdag gis zhing bkod pa rnams bden zhen gyis don dam par bsgrub par bya'o snyam zhing zer na, tshig de ni mi bden par smra ba'o
corpus_segments:2022.english: Lord Buddha wishes to indicate that, in order for a person to reach the enlightenment described above, he or she must first bring about a paradise in which to achieve the enlightenment. Therefore the Conqueror says to Subhuti, Suppose some bodhisattva were to say or think to himself--while holding a belief in true existence, and referring to ultimate existence--"I am working to bring about paradises." This statement would not be spoken true.

corpus_segments:3768.acip: BUD MED KYI LUS GANG LA YONGS SU 'KHYUD PAS NA MCHOG TU DGA' ZHING CHAGS PAR 'GYUR BA'I LUS DE DAG NYID KENG RUS NYID YIN GYI GZHAN MIN NA DANG PO NAS RANG DBANG DU GYUR PA DANG NI BDAG TU YONGS SU BZUNG BA YANG MIN PA LA DGOS PA CUNG ZAD KYANG MED PAR RAB TU 'DOD CING YONGS SU ZHEN NAS CI'I PHYIR MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PAR MI 'GRO, 'DOD PA SPANGS NAS THAR PA'I LAM LA BRTZON PAR BYA'O,
corpus_segments:3768.wylie: bud med kyi lus gang la yongs su 'khyud pas na mchog tu dga' zhing chags par 'gyur ba'i lus de dag nyid keng rus nyid yin gyi gzhan min na dang po nas rang dbang du gyur pa dang ni bdag tu yongs su bzung ba yang min pa la dgos pa cung zad kyang med par rab tu 'dod cing yongs su zhen nas ci'i phyir mya ngan las 'das par mi 'gro, 'dod pa spangs nas thar pa'i lam la brtson par bya'o
corpus_segments:3768.english: Think though of those objects, the bodies of women, that you hold in your arms to find your feelings of ecstasy, and towards which you feel such attachment. These very same things, these bodies, are nothing more than simple skeletons. Why do you pass up travelling on to nirvana, choosing instead to crave and believe from your heart in a thing which is helpless at the mercy of other conditions, a thing which has never possessed any nature of being itself, despite the fact that you hold it to? You must give up these things you crave for, and make great efforts in practicing the path to freedom.

corpus_segments:3814.acip: ,GAL TE 'BREL MED KYI SDUG BSNGAL CIG SHOS KYIS SEL BA RIGS PA MIN YANG , 'DIR BDAG TU 'DZIN PA GOMS PA LAS SKYE BA SNGA PHYI DANG SNGA DRO PHYI DRO LA SOGS PA'I LUS RNAMS GANG ZAG GCIG PO DE'I BDAG GI BAR 'DZIN PA GOMS PA LAS GCIG GI SDUG BSNGAL CIG SHOS KYIS SEL BA LA 'JUG CE NA, RANG DBANG BA'I BDAG DANG GZHAN DU 'DZIN PA MI RIGS PA GANG YIN PA DE YANG CI NUS PAR NI SPANG BAR BYA BA NYID YIN TE, GANG ZAG GI BDAG TU 'DZIN PA ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL ZHING DES PHUNG KHROL THAMS CAD BSKYED PA'I PHYIR RO,
corpus_segments:3814.wylie: gal te 'brel med kyi sdug bsngal cig shos kyis sel ba rigs pa min yang , 'dir bdag tu 'dzin pa goms pa las skye ba snga phyi dang snga dro phyi dro la sogs pa'i lus rnams gang zag gcig po de'i bdag gi bar 'dzin pa goms pa las gcig gi sdug bsngal cig shos kyis sel ba la 'jug ce na, rang dbang ba'i bdag dang gzhan du 'dzin pa mi rigs pa gang yin pa de yang ci nus par ni spang bar bya ba nyid yin te, gang zag gi bdag tu 'dzin pa zhen yul la 'khrul zhing des phung khrol thams cad bskyed pa'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:3814.english: Suppose you say now the following: Although it is wrong to assert that two objects which are unrelated should work to remove each other's suffering, here it's different. In this case we assume that I have become accustomed to holding to a particular self: I consider the bodies of the previous and succeeding lives, and the bodies of the earlier part of the day and the latter part of the day, and so on, to be one person. And it is due to the fact that I have become accustomed to thinking this way that one of these engages in attempting to remove the pain of the other. It is very wrong though to hold to the existence of this "self" and "other" which are able to perform some action on their own. They are nothing but something you should reject, with all the strength you have. This is because the tendency to hold onto some self-nature of the person is mistaken in what it believes to exist, and is responsible for causing every kind of devastation. Contemplation Twenty Are we only what we control?

corpus_segments:4085.acip: GSUM PA NI, DES NA SNGAR BSHAD PA DE LTAR STONG PA NYID KYI PHYOGS LA SUN 'BYIN PA NI 'THAD PA MA YIN TE 'OG NAS 'CHAD PA'I RIGS PA RNAMS KYIS KYANG GNOD PA'I PHYIR RO, , DES NA NYAN RANG GI BYANG CHUB THOB PAR 'DOD PAS KYANG THE TSOM MI ZA BAR STONG PA NYID NI BSGOM PAR BYA STE, BDEN 'DZIN 'KHOR BA'I RTZA BAR GYUR PA'I NYON MONGS CAN GYI MA RIG PA YIN LA DE'I ZHEN YUL SUN MA PHYUNG BAR THAR PA THOB PA MI SRID PA'I PHYIR RO,
corpus_segments:4085.wylie: gsum pa ni, des na sngar bshad pa de ltar stong pa nyid kyi phyogs la sun 'byin pa ni 'thad pa ma yin te 'og nas 'chad pa'i rigs pa rnams kyis kyang gnod pa'i phyir ro, , des na nyan rang gi byang chub thob par 'dod pas kyang the tshom mi za bar stong pa nyid ni bsgom par bya ste, bden 'dzin 'khor ba'i rtsa bar gyur pa'i nyon mongs can gyi ma rig pa yin la de'i zhen yul sun ma phyung bar thar pa thob pa mi srid pa'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:4085.english: Here is the third point, [which is advice to those who seek to attain liberation, that it is therefore very right that they should meditate upon emptiness]. As such--that is, as we have just explained--the case is that all these attempts to overthrow those who accept the idea of emptiness are completely incorrect. They will also be disproved by the various kinds of reasoning which we will present later on. And so it is that even those who wish no more than to achieve the "enlightenment" which is the goal of the Listener and "Self-Made Buddha" tracks must still, beyond a shadow of a doubt, meditate upon emptiness, for the following reason. The tendency to hold things as existing truly is that form of ignorance, involved with mental affliction, which is the root of the circle of suffering. And it is completely impossible to attain freedom unless one can overthrow the existence of the object which this ignorance thinks it sees.

corpus_segments:6838.acip: GZHAN YANG DE CHOS CAN, GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED RDZOGS PAR MA RTOGS PAR THAL, GANG ZAG RANG BZHIN MED PAR MNGON SUM DU MA RTOGS PA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, GDAGS GZHI PHUNG PO RANG NGOS NAS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN 'BYIN MI NUS PA'I TSUL GYI PHYIN CI LOG GIS BCINGS PA YIN PA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, PHUNG PO RANG BZHIN MED PAR YONGS SU SHES PA DANG BRAL BA'I PHYIR,
corpus_segments:6838.wylie: gzhan yang de chos can, gang zag gi bdag med rdzogs par ma rtogs par thal, gang zag rang bzhin med par mngon sum du ma rtogs pa'i phyir, der thal, gdags gzhi phung po rang ngos nas grub par 'dzin pa'i zhen yul sun 'byin mi nus pa'i tshul gyi phyin ci log gis bcings pa yin pa'i phyir, der thal, phung po rang bzhin med par yongs su shes pa dang bral ba'i phyir
corpus_segments:6838.english: Consider these same enemy destroyers. It is true that they have not yet realized, entirely, the fact that the person has no self nature. This is because they have yet to perceive directly the fact that the person has no nature. This in itself is true as well, for they are still chained by total misperceptions, in such a way that they will never be able to root out the object that they think they see when they hold the parts to the person, the thing which gets the label of "me," as existing from its own side. And this too is true, for they lack that comprehensive knowledge where they realize that the parts to the person have no nature of their own.

corpus_segments:6839.acip: THAL 'GYUR SNGA MA LA KHYAB PA YOD DE, GDAGS GZHI PHUNG PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN PHYUNG MI NUS PA JI SRID 'JUG GI BAR DU, BTAGS CHOS GANG ZAG RANG NGOS NAS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN PHYUNG MI NUS PAR 'JUG PA GANG ZHIG, DE JI SRID 'JUG GI BAR DU DE'I DBANG GIS LAS BSOG, LAS DE'I DBANG GIS 'KHOR BAR 'KHOR BA'I PHYIR,
corpus_segments:6839.wylie: thal 'gyur snga ma la khyab pa yod de, gdags gzhi phung po rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa'i zhen yul sun phyung mi nus pa ji srid 'jug gi bar du, btags chos gang zag rang ngos nas grub par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa'i zhen yul sun phyung mi nus par 'jug pa gang zhig, de ji srid 'jug gi bar du de'i dbang gis las bsog, las de'i dbang gis 'khor bar 'khor ba'i phyir
corpus_segments:6839.english: The first of our logical statements above is always true. For suppose that a person is still unable to root out the object that he thinks he sees when he holds the parts to the person, the thing which gets the label of "me," as existing through some nature of its own. As long as he goes on this way, then he will continue to find himself unable to root out the object that he thinks he sees when he holds the thing which gets the label, the "me," as existing from its own side. And as long as he continues with this, then by the power of this misperception he will continue to collect karma. And as long as he collects karma, then he will continue to spin around in this wheel of suffering life. 28 Lord Maitreya's Six Steps

corpus_segments:7103.acip: ,DE LTAR 'TSANG RGYA BA LA GANG DU 'TSANG RGYA BA'I ZHING DAG PA SGRUB DGOS PAR STON PA NI, BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS RAB 'BYOR LA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG LA LA ZHIG BDAG GIS ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS BDEN ZHEN GYIS DON DAM PAR BSGRUB PAR BYA'O SNYAM ZHING ZER NA, TSIG DE NI MI BDEN PAR SMRA BA'O,
corpus_segments:7103.wylie: de ltar 'tshang rgya ba la gang du 'tshang rgya ba'i zhing dag pa sgrub dgos par ston pa ni, bcom ldan 'das kyis rab 'byor la byang chub sems dpa' gang la la zhig bdag gis zhing bkod pa rnams bden zhen gyis don dam par bsgrub par bya'o snyam zhing zer na, tshig de ni mi bden par smra ba'o
corpus_segments:7103.english: Lord Buddha wishes to indicate that, in order for a person to reach the enlightenment described above, he or she must first bring about a paradise in which to achieve the enlightenment. Therefore the Conqueror says to Subhuti, Suppose some bodhisattva were to say or think to himself--while holding a belief in true existence, and referring to ultimate existence--"I am working to bring about paradises." This statement would not be spoken true.

corpus_segments:7990.acip: ,GAL TE 'BREL MED KYI SDUG BSNGAL CIG SHOS KYIS SEL BA RIGS PA MIN YANG , 'DIR BDAG TU 'DZIN PA GOMS PA LAS SKYE BA SNGA PHYI DANG SNGA DRO PHYI DRO LA SOGS PA'I LUS RNAMS GANG ZAG GCIG PO DE'I BDAG GI BAR 'DZIN PA GOMS PA LAS GCIG GI SDUG BSNGAL CIG SHOS KYIS SEL BA LA 'JUG CE NA, RANG DBANG BA'I BDAG DANG GZHAN DU 'DZIN PA MI RIGS PA GANG YIN PA DE YANG CI NUS PAR NI SPANG BAR BYA BA NYID YIN TE, GANG ZAG GI BDAG TU 'DZIN PA ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL ZHING DES PHUNG KHROL THAMS CAD BSKYED PA'I PHYIR RO,
corpus_segments:7990.wylie: gal te 'brel med kyi sdug bsngal cig shos kyis sel ba rigs pa min yang , 'dir bdag tu 'dzin pa goms pa las skye ba snga phyi dang snga dro phyi dro la sogs pa'i lus rnams gang zag gcig po de'i bdag gi bar 'dzin pa goms pa las gcig gi sdug bsngal cig shos kyis sel ba la 'jug ce na, rang dbang ba'i bdag dang gzhan du 'dzin pa mi rigs pa gang yin pa de yang ci nus par ni spang bar bya ba nyid yin te, gang zag gi bdag tu 'dzin pa zhen yul la 'khrul zhing des phung khrol thams cad bskyed pa'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:7990.english: Suppose you say now the following: Although it is wrong to assert that two objects which are unrelated should work to remove each other's suffering, here it's different. In this case we assume that I have become accustomed to holding to a particular self: I consider the bodies of the previous and succeeding lives, and the bodies of the earlier part of the day and the latter part of the day, and so on, to be one person. And it is due to the fact that I have become accustomed to thinking this way that one of these engages in attempting to remove the pain of the other. It is very wrong though to hold to the existence of this "self" and "other" which are able to perform some action on their own. They are nothing but something you should reject, with all the strength you have. This is because the tendency to hold onto some self-nature of the person is mistaken in what it believes to exist, and is responsible for causing every kind of devastation. Contemplation Sixteen Are we only what we control?

corpus_segments:8085.acip: GSUM PA NI, DES NA SNGAR BSHAD PA DE LTAR STONG PA NYID KYI PHYOGS LA SUN 'BYIN PA NI 'THAD PA MA YIN TE 'OG NAS 'CHAD PA'I RIGS PA RNAMS KYIS KYANG GNOD PA'I PHYIR RO, , DES NA NYAN RANG GI BYANG CHUB THOB PAR 'DOD PAS KYANG THE TSOM MI ZA BAR STONG PA NYID NI BSGOM PAR BYA STE, BDEN 'DZIN 'KHOR BA'I RTZA BAR GYUR PA'I NYON MONGS CAN GYI MA RIG PA YIN LA DE'I ZHEN YUL SUN MA PHYUNG BAR THAR PA THOB PA MI SRID PA'I PHYIR RO,

corpus_segments:8085.english: Here is the third point, [which is advice to those who seek to attain liberation, that it is therefore very right that they should meditate upon emptiness]. As such--that is, as we have just explained--the case is that all these attempts to overthrow those who accept the idea of emptiness are completely incorrect. They will also be disproved by the various kinds of reasoning which we will present later on. And so it is that even those who wish no more than to achieve the "enlightenment" which is the goal of the Listener and "Self-Made Buddha" tracks must still, beyond a shadow of a doubt, meditate upon emptiness, for the following reason. The tendency to hold things as existing truly is that form of ignorance, involved with mental affliction, which is the root of the circle of suffering. And it is completely impossible to attain freedom unless one can overthrow the existence of the object which this ignorance thinks it sees.

corpus_segments:26475.acip: MA GRUB NA, RI BONG RVA CHOS CAN, RI BONG RVA 'DZIN RTOG PA'I YUL YIN PAR THAL, RI BONG RVA 'DZIN RTOG PA'I ZHEN YUL YIN PA'I PHYIR,
corpus_segments:26475.wylie: ma grub na, ri bong rva chos can, ri bong rva 'dzin rtog pa'i yul yin par thal, ri bong rva 'dzin rtog pa'i zhen yul yin pa'i phyir
corpus_segments:26475.english: I disagree that the antlers on top of a rabbit's head are the object of a state of mind that thinks it sees antlers on top of a rabbit's head. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the antlers on top of a rabbit's head. They are too the object of a state of mind that thinks it sees antlers on top of a rabbit's head, Because they are the object that a state of mind that thinks it sees antlers on top of a rabbit's head believes in.

corpus_segments:32810.acip: DE'I PHYIR RNAM RIG PAS SO SKYE'I RGYUD KYI SNGON 'DZIN DBANG PO'I MNGON SUM YANG RANG GI SNANG YUL LA 'KHRUL BAR 'DOD CING, DES DRANGS NAS SKYES PA'I RTOG PA DE ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL PA'I CHOS KYI BDAG 'DZIN DU 'DOD DO,,
corpus_segments:32810.wylie: de'i phyir rnam rig pas so skye'i rgyud kyi sngon 'dzin dbang po'i mngon sum yang rang gi snang yul la 'khrul bar 'dod cing, des drangs nas skyes pa'i rtog pa de zhen yul la 'khrul pa'i chos kyi bdag 'dzin du 'dod do
corpus_segments:32810.english: And so it is that the Mentalists believe that even direct sense perception in the mind of a normal person is mistaken towards its object, as this object appears to the perception. corpus_segments:32814.english: And why is that? Well, first of all, let's look at what they mean, here in the context of the Mentalist School, when they assert that things like visible form are not, by definition, what the thoughts that are holding them think they are.

corpus_segments:32815.acip: RTOG PA'I ZHEN GZHI'I RANG LDOG TZAM LA MI BYED KYI, DE'I GZHI LDOG BAG CHAGS BRTAN BYUNG GI DBANG SHES LA GZUGS SOGS KYI THA SNYAD GANG LA 'JUG PA'I GZHIR SNANG BA'I SNANG TSUL LTAR GYI DON LA 'DOD CING, SNANG BA LTAR RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS MA GRUB PAR 'DOD LA,
corpus_segments:32815.wylie: rtog pa'i zhen gzhi'i rang ldog tsam la mi byed kyi, de'i gzhi ldog bag chags brtan byung gi dbang shes la gzugs sogs kyi tha snyad gang la 'jug pa'i gzhir snang ba'i snang tshul ltar gyi don la 'dod cing, snang ba ltar rang gi mtshan nyid kyis ma grub par 'dod la
corpus_segments:32815.english: When the Mentalists speak this way, they are not just talking about what these thoughts think they see, in a conceptual form. Rather, they are referring to the actual manifestation: they are referring to the visual form which appears to the sense consciousness as it has arisen from a solid seed. And what they say is that it does not exist, as it appears to, by definition.
corpus_segments:32815.raw: {"course": "EM", "acip": "RTOG PA'I ZHEN GZHI'I RANG LDOG TZAM LA MI BYED KYI, DE'I GZHI LDOG BAG CHAGS BRTAN BYUNG GI DBANG SHES LA GZUGS SOGS KYI THA SNYAD GANG LA 'JUG PA'I GZHIR SNANG BA'I SNANG TSUL LTAR GYI DON LA 'DOD CING, SNANG BA LTAR RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS MA GRUB PAR 'DOD LA,", "wylie": "rtog pa'i zhen gzhi'i rang ldog tsam la mi byed kyi, de'i gzhi ldog bag chags brtan byung gi dbang shes la gzugs sogs kyi tha snyad gang la 'jug pa'i gzhir snang ba'i snang tshul ltar gyi don la 'dod cing, snang ba ltar rang gi mtshan nyid kyis ma grub par 'dod la", "english": "When the Mentalists speak this way, they are not just talking about what these thoughts think they see, in a conceptual form. Rather, they are referring to the actual manifestation: they are referring to the visual form which appears to the sense consciousness as it has arisen from a solid seed. And what they say is that it does not exist, as it appears to, by definition."}

corpus_segments:32914.acip: 'JOG PA'I BLO NI GNOD MED ZHIG DGOS KYI, ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL BA'I BLO LA SNANG BA TZAM GYIS 'JOG NUS PAR MI 'DOD DO,,
corpus_segments:32914.wylie: 'jog pa'i blo ni gnod med zhig dgos kyi, zhen yul la 'khrul ba'i blo la snang ba tsam gyis 'jog nus par mi 'dod do
corpus_segments:32914.english: One point to be made here is that the state of mind based on which we can say something is established as existing must be one which is unaffected by problems of perception; that is, the sub-school we're representing here would not say that something we think we see can be established as existing merely on the basis of its appearing to a mistaken state of mind.

corpus_segments:33136.acip: 'DZIN STANGS ZHEN DU SONG NA, RIGS PA DRAN TZAM BYAS TE, SNANG TSUL DE LTAR DU GRUB PA MED MED SNYAM DU BSAM ZHING SKYUR NAS BSGOM PAR BYA LA,
corpus_segments:33136.wylie: 'dzin stangs zhen du song na, rigs pa dran tsam byas te, snang tshul de ltar du grub pa med med snyam du bsam zhing skyur nas bsgom par bya la
corpus_segments:33136.english: When you start sliding into believing in things again, then give yourself just a small reminder. Come back to thinking about how none of these things could ever, ever, possibly exist in this way that they appear to. Continue meditating and practicing this way, where you throw those mistaken beliefs away from you.

Come back to thinking about how none of these things could ever, ever, possibly exist in this way that they appear to. Continue meditating and practicing this way, where you throw those mistaken beliefs away from you."}

corpus_segments:33381.acip: DE LA GANG DAG SHES RAB KYI MIG DANG BRAL BAS PHYIN CI LOG GI BLO CAN DU GYUR CING BDAG TU MNGON PAR ZHEN NAS LAS RNAM PA SNA TSOGS BYED PA DE DAG NI 'KHOR BA NA YONGS SU 'KHYAM MO,
corpus_segments:33381.wylie: de la gang dag shes rab kyi mig dang bral bas phyin ci log gi blo can du gyur cing bdag tu mngon par zhen nas las rnam pa sna tshogs byed pa de dag ni 'khor ba na yongs su 'khyam mo
corpus_segments:33381.english: In these matters, those who lack the eyes of wisdom begin thinking of things in the wrong way. They start to have a strong attachment to the idea of a “me,” and because of that they commit a whole variety of karmas. And then they wander throughout this cycle of suffering.

They start to have a strong attachment to the idea of a “me,” and because of that they commit a whole variety of karmas. And then they wander throughout this cycle of suffering."}

corpus_segments:33406.acip: YANG DAG PAR SO SOR RTOG PA MED PAR RNAL 'BYOR PAS THABS GANG GIS THOG MA MED PA'I DUS NAS GZUGS LA SOGS PA'I DNGOS PO LA MNGON PAR ZHEN CING GOMS PA'I SEMS RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA NYID LA RNAM PAR GZHAG PAR BYA,
corpus_segments:33406.wylie: yang dag par so sor rtog pa med par rnal 'byor pas thabs gang gis thog ma med pa'i dus nas gzugs la sogs pa'i dngos po la mngon par zhen cing goms pa'i sems rnam par mi rtog pa nyid la rnam par gzhag par bya
corpus_segments:33406.english: And so suppose that the deep practitioner lacked an accurate practice of careful examination. How then would they ever learn to stay in this state where one is no longer in thoughts where they strongly believe in, and are used to, the idea—which we have had for time with no beginning—of form and other such entities? The wrong idea that we should never think, or bring anything to mind

corpus_segments:23531.acip: BLO GROS DMAN PA RNAMS KYIS RANG GI STON PA'I RJES SU 'JUG PA DANG DES BSTAN PA'I CHOS BSGRUB BYA YIN PAR BZUNG NAS SKYABS SU 'GRO BA NI, MOS MNO TZAM DANG YID DPYOD TZAM GYIS {%GYI} SGO NAS YIN GYI, BLO CHE BA RNAMS KYIS THOG MA NYID NAS PHYOGS LHUNG DANG 'DOD ZHEN GYIS RANG GI STON PA'O SNYAM PA DANG DES GSUNGS PA'O SNYAM DU MI 'DZIN PAR PHYI NANG GI STON PA GNYIS LAS GANG GI BSHAD PA DE RIGS PA YIN,
corpus_segments:23531.wylie: blo gros dman pa rnams kyis rang gi ston pa'i rjes su 'jug pa dang des bstan pa'i chos bsgrub bya yin par bzung nas skyabs su 'gro ba ni, mos mno tsam dang yid dpyod tsam gyis {%gyi} sgo nas yin gyi, blo che ba rnams kyis thog ma nyid nas phyogs lhung dang 'dod zhen gyis rang gi ston pa'o snyam pa dang des gsungs pa'o snyam du mi 'dzin par phyi nang gi ston pa gnyis las gang gi bshad pa de rigs pa yin
corpus_segments:23531.english: People of lesser intellectual capacity tend to follow their own teacher and practice whatever that teacher teaches, and in this way take their refuge in them.  It's all done out of blind faith and guesswork.  Those of greater intellect don't think in terms of sticking to their teacher and their teacher's words from nothing more than prejudice or favoritism.  Whether they encounter a teacher from an outer belief system or an inner one, in either case they wait to see if the explanations given make sense.

It's all done out of blind faith and guesswork.  Those of greater intellect don't think in terms of sticking to their teacher and their teacher's words from nothing more than prejudice or favoritism.  Whether they encounter a teacher from an outer belief system or an inner one, in either case they wait to see if the explanations given make sense."}

corpus_segments:27762.acip: BDEN PA'I PHUNG PO DMIGS PAR BYAS NAS MI RTAG SOGS SU YID LA BYED PA CIG KYANG YOD LA, DE NI ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL BA'I LOG SHES RKYANG PA YIN PAS, TSAD MAS GRUB PA MIN KYANG
corpus_segments:27762.wylie: bden pa'i phung po dmigs par byas nas mi rtag sogs su yid la byed pa cig kyang yod la, de ni zhen yul la 'khrul ba'i log shes rkyang pa yin pas, tshad mas grub pa min kyang
corpus_segments:27762.english: And so there are people who think they are looking at parts to a person which are real, and who think of them as impermanent and such—but their state of mind is a total misperception, mistaken in the object that it believes it sees. Therefore we can go further and say the object here is not even one which is established by an accurate perception.
corpus_segments:27762.raw: {"course": "ILL", "acip": "BDEN PA'I PHUNG PO DMIGS PAR BYAS NAS MI RTAG SOGS SU YID LA BYED PA CIG KYANG YOD LA, DE NI ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL BA'I LOG SHES RKYANG PA YIN PAS, TSAD MAS GRUB PA MIN KYANG", "wylie": "bden pa'i phung po dmigs par byas nas mi rtag sogs su yid la byed pa cig kyang yod la, de ni zhen yul la 'khrul ba'i log shes rkyang pa yin pas, tshad mas grub pa min kyang", "english": "And so there are people who think they are looking at parts to a person which are real, and who think of them as impermanent and such—but their state of mind is a total misperception, mistaken in the object that it believes it sees. Therefore we can go further and say the object here is not even one which is established by an accurate perception."}

corpus_segments:27792.acip: DE LTAR NA BDEN 'DZIN GYI ZHEN YUL SUN MA PHYUNG BAR DU, 'JIG LTA'I ZHEN YUL SUN MI PHYIN PAS, THEG PA CHE CHUNG GI GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA LA THUN MONG DU GRAGS PA'I GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED NI, RAGS PA'I GANG ZAG GI BDAG TZAM BKAG PA YIN GYI, PHRA BA'I GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED MIN PAR SHES SO,,
corpus_segments:27792.wylie: de ltar na bden 'dzin gyi zhen yul sun ma phyung bar du, 'jig lta'i zhen yul sun mi phyin pas, theg pa che chung gi grub mtha' smra ba la thun mong du grags pa'i gang zag gi bdag med ni, rags pa'i gang zag gi bdag tsam bkag pa yin gyi, phra ba'i gang zag gi bdag med min par shes so
corpus_segments:27792.english: As such, we cannot demolish the object that the view of destruction thinks it sees, until we manage to demolish the object that the tendency to think that things are real thinks it sees. And so you should understand that the version of the lack of a self-nature to the person which is generally understood to be held in common by those who follow the schools of the greater way and those who follow the schools of the lesser way is a denial of a self-nature to the person in no more than its gross form; and is not the subtle form of the lack of a self-nature to the person.

And so you should understand that the version of the lack of a self-nature to the person which is generally understood to be held in common by those who follow the schools of the greater way and those who follow the schools of the lesser way is a denial of a self-nature to the person in no more than its gross form; and is not the subtle form of the lack of a self-nature to the person."}

corpus_segments:27796.acip: DE YANG PHUNG PO LA BDEN 'DZIN GYI ZHEN YUL SUN MA PHYIN PA'I DBANG DU MDZAD KYI, SPYIR 'JIG LTA YOD TZAM LA MIN TE, SA BDUN PA'I BAR DU 'JIG LTA YOD KYANG, SA DANG PO NAS LAS DBANG GIS SKYE BA MI LEN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
corpus_segments:27796.wylie: de yang phung po la bden 'dzin gyi zhen yul sun ma phyin pa'i dbang du mdzad kyi, spyir 'jig lta yod tsam la min te, sa bdun pa'i bar du 'jig lta yod kyang, sa dang po nas las dbang gis skye ba mi len pa'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:27796.english: This statement by the way is made with reference to someone who has failed to demolish the object that the tendency to hold that the parts to a person are real thinks it sees; it is not though a general reference only to anyone who possesses the view of destruction. Up to the seventh bodhisattva level, we still possess this view; but from the first bodhisattva level on up, we no longer take rebirth through the power of karma.

corpus_segments:28307.acip: DE 'DRA BA NI NGES DON MA GO BA RNAMS KYI PHYIR YIN GYI, NGES DON GO BA LA MI DGOS TE, DE DAG THAMS CAD RTOG PAS BYED LA RTOG PA THAMS CAD BDEN ZHEN GYI MTSAN 'DZIN YIN PA'I PHYIR RO SNYAM DU 'DZIN ZHING, RGYA NAG GI HVA SHANG LTAR DGE BA THAMS CAD 'JOMS LA,
corpus_segments:28307.wylie: de 'dra ba ni nges don ma go ba rnams kyi phyir yin gyi, nges don go ba la mi dgos te, de dag thams cad rtog pas byed la rtog pa thams cad bden zhen gyi mtshan 'dzin yin pa'i phyir ro snyam du 'dzin zhing, rgya nag gi hva shang ltar dge ba thams cad 'joms la
corpus_segments:28307.english: When something like this happens, it's all because a person has failed to grasp what the Buddha most intended to say. And they in turn will think to themselves that there's no need to understand what he most intended to say, since (according to them) all this is just the product of our conceptual state of mind, and all such states of mind are actually grasping to signs: believing that things are real. Thus then they will, like the Chinese monk Hashang, destroy all their good deeds.

Thus then they will, like the Chinese monk Hashang, destroy all their good deeds."}

corpus_segments:28449.acip: GNYIS PA NI, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I MING GI THA SNYAD KYI DBANG TZAM GYIS BZHAG PA MIN PA'I YOD PAR 'DZIN PA NI, BDEN PA DANG DON DAM PAR DANG YANG DAG TU GRUB PA DANG, RANG GI NGO BOS DANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS DANG RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PAR 'DZIN PA LHAN SKYES YIN LA, DES BZUNG BA'I ZHEN YUL NI BRTAG PA MTHA' BZUNG GI BDEN TSAD DO,,
corpus_segments:28449.wylie: gnyis pa ni, sngar bshad pa'i ming gi tha snyad kyi dbang tsam gyis bzhag pa min pa'i yod par 'dzin pa ni, bden pa dang don dam par dang yang dag tu grub pa dang, rang gi ngo bos dang rang gi mtshan nyid kyis dang rang bzhin gyis yod par 'dzin pa lhan skyes yin la, des bzung ba'i zhen yul ni brtag pa mtha' bzung gi bden tshad do
corpus_segments:28449.english: Here is the second part from above: a presentation of what it is to hold things as real—as the opposite of something created by ideas. Now suppose we hold on to something as not simply being a creation of names. The version of this tendency that we were born with holds that things exist really; ultimately; purely—it believes that things exist through some essential nature of their own; by definition; naturally. And the object that this belief thinks it sees is the theoretical measure of a thing that could be “real.”

corpus_segments:28743.acip: DANG PO LA BZHI, BDEN GNYIS SU DBYE BAS CHOS RNAMS LA NGO BO GNYIS GNYIS YOD PAR BRJOD PA, BDEN GNYIS KYI RNAM BZHAG GZHAN BSTAN PA, 'JIG RTEN LA BLTOS TE KUN RDZOB KYI DBYE BA BSHAD PA, ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL BA'I ZHEN YUL THA SNYAD DU YANG MED PAR BSTAN PA'O,,
corpus_segments:28743.wylie: dang po la bzhi, bden gnyis su dbye bas chos rnams la ngo bo gnyis gnyis yod par brjod pa, bden gnyis kyi rnam bzhag gzhan bstan pa, 'jig rten la bltos te kun rdzob kyi dbye ba bshad pa, zhen yul la 'khrul ba'i zhen yul tha snyad du yang med par bstan pa'o
corpus_segments:28743.english: The first of these has four parts of its own: A statement about how all objects each possess two different natures, given the division into two realities A description of other ways in which the two realities are set forth An explanation of the divisions of deceptive reality, relative to the everyday world Demonstrating that—when we are mistaken towards the object we think we see—this object that we believe in does not even exist nominally. The two natures of every existing thing

The two natures of every existing thing"}

corpus_segments:28824.acip: BZHI PA NI, DA NI BSHAD ZIN PA'I YID KYI GNOD PAS ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL BA SPYIR BSTAN PA'I DON DE NYID, MTSAN GZHI BYE BRAG LA DPER BRJOD PA'I TSUL GYIS BSTAN PA'I PHYIR BSHAD PA,
corpus_segments:28824.wylie: bzhi pa ni, da ni bshad zin pa'i yid kyi gnod pas zhen yul la 'khrul ba spyir bstan pa'i don de nyid, mtshan gzhi bye brag la dper brjod pa'i tshul gyis bstan pa'i phyir bshad pa
corpus_segments:28824.english: This brings us then to our fourth point from above: demonstrating that—when we are mistaken towards the object we think we see—this object that we believe in does not even exist nominally. And so now we will take this same general topic that we've discussed—the way in which, as we've already described, we make an error about what we think we see, due to some problem in our mind—and give an explanation where we apply to particular classic cases, in a metaphor.

corpus_segments:28832.acip: DE 'DRA BA'I ZHEN YUL RNAMS THA SNYAD DU YANG MED KYANG SNANG YUL LA NI DE LTAR MI BZHED DO,,
corpus_segments:28832.wylie: de 'dra ba'i zhen yul rnams tha snyad du yang med kyang snang yul la ni de ltar mi bzhed do
corpus_segments:28832.english: When we say that things like this which we think are there don't even exist in a nominal way, we are not saying that this is what we accept with regard to the object as it appears to us.
corpus_segments:28832.raw: {"course": "ILL", "acip": "DE 'DRA BA'I ZHEN YUL RNAMS THA SNYAD DU YANG MED KYANG SNANG YUL LA NI DE LTAR MI BZHED DO,,", "wylie": "de 'dra ba'i zhen yul rnams tha snyad du yang med kyang snang yul la ni de ltar mi bzhed do", "english": "When we say that things like this which we think are there don't even exist in a nominal way, we are not saying that this is what we accept with regard to the object as it appears to us."}

corpus_segments:28893.acip: GANG ZAG DANG CHOS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NI, DE 'GOG PA'I RIGS PA RNAMS KYIS KHEGS PAR 'GYUR ZHING, DE'I TSE DE LTAR 'DZIN PA DE ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL PA'I BDEN 'DZIN DU 'GRUB LA, DE GRUB NA GANG ZAG DANG CHOS GNYIS BDEN GRUB TU 'DZIN PA BDAG 'DZIN GNYIS SU 'GRUB BO,,
corpus_segments:28893.wylie: gang zag dang chos rang bzhin gyis grub pa ni, de 'gog pa'i rigs pa rnams kyis khegs par 'gyur zhing, de'i tshe de ltar 'dzin pa de zhen yul la 'khrul pa'i bden 'dzin du 'grub la, de grub na gang zag dang chos gnyis bden grub tu 'dzin pa bdag 'dzin gnyis su 'grub bo
corpus_segments:28893.english: They refute the idea that the person & things could exist through some nature of their own by employing different forms of reasoning which disproves it. They would establish, at this point, the tendency to hold these things this way as being a tendency to hold that things are real where we are mistaken about the object that we think we see. Once this is established, they establish that the tendencies to hold the person and things as being real are what constitute the two forms of holding that things are themselves.

corpus_segments:29798.acip: 'ON KYANG RANG RIG KHAS MI LEN PA LA GZHI DUS KYI YID SHES SNANG BA DANG, ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL BA RNAMS YOD PAR MI 'GRUB STE, DE RNAMS LA RANG GI GZHAL BYA 'JAL BAS YUL CAN GRUB PA MED PA'I PHYIR RO ZHE NA,
corpus_segments:29798.wylie: 'on kyang rang rig khas mi len pa la gzhi dus kyi yid shes snang ba dang, zhen yul la 'khrul ba rnams yod par mi 'grub ste, de rnams la rang gi gzhal bya 'jal bas yul can grub pa med pa'i phyir ro zhe na
corpus_segments:29798.english: One may come then with the following question: But isn't it the case that—with someone who does not accept the idea of apperception—the consciousness of the thought (assuming one is still in their original state of evolution) and types of perception which are mistaken towards what one thinks that they see, cannot be demonstrated to exist? Because it is the case that there is no confirmation of the subject states of mind here, as they take under consideration their particular objects of consideration.

Because it is the case that there is no confirmation of the subject states of mind here, as they take under consideration their particular objects of consideration."}

corpus_segments:29827.acip: DE'I PHYIR BDAG 'DZIN GNYIS LTA BU LA YANG BDAG GNYIS KYI SNANG BA MNGON SUM DU 'CHAR LA, DE'I TSE GZHAL BYA SNANG BA MNGON GYUR DE YUL CAN DES 'GRUB PA SOGS SNGAR DANG 'DRA STE, DES ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL PA GZHAN YANG SHES PAR BYA'O,,
corpus_segments:29827.wylie: de'i phyir bdag 'dzin gnyis lta bu la yang bdag gnyis kyi snang ba mngon sum du 'char la, de'i tshe gzhal bya snang ba mngon gyur de yul can des 'grub pa sogs sngar dang 'dra ste, des zhen yul la 'khrul pa gzhan yang shes par bya'o
corpus_segments:29827.english: As such, we can say even with things like the two forms of the tendency to grasp to some self-nature of things that the appearance of two “selfs” here is made directly. And we can also say at that point things like the fact that the object under consideration is making its appearance directly is confirmed by the subject state of mind; just as we did this earlier. And from this we can also understand moreover that this state of mind is mistaken towards the object that it thinks it sees.

corpus_segments:30392.acip: DE NAS DE'I RTZA BA GANG YIN NGOS 'DZIN PA DANG, DE NAS DE SPONG BAR 'DOD PA NA SPONG THABS KYI THAD DU MA 'PHYUGS PAR DE'I ZHEN YUL BKAG PA'I BDAG MED KYI LTA BA ZHIG NGES PAR RNYED NAS,
corpus_segments:30392.wylie: de nas de'i rtsa ba gang yin ngos 'dzin pa dang, de nas de spong bar 'dod pa na spong thabs kyi thad du ma 'phyugs par de'i zhen yul bkag pa'i bdag med kyi lta ba zhig nges par rnyed nas
corpus_segments:30392.english: With this, we come to identify just what it is that serves as the very root of this circle. If then we hope to eliminate this root, then we have to be sure that we make no errors regarding the proper methodology of doing so. Which is to say, we will beyond any doubt have to ascertain that view of no-self which we can use to put a stop to the object that we think we see here: we will have to identify, with certainty, a correct view of how no self exists.

corpus_segments:31109.acip: DE LA 'DI LTAR ZHES 'BYUNG BA LEGS LA, LHAG MA'I DON NI BDEN PAR 'DZIN PA'I ZHEN YUL GYI DNGOS PO MED PA DANG, KUN RDZOB TU BCOS MA DANG GZHAN LA LTOS PA'I RNAM PA DE LTA BU'I DON BSTAN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
corpus_segments:31109.wylie: de la 'di ltar zhes 'byung ba legs la, lhag ma'i don ni bden par 'dzin pa'i zhen yul gyi dngos po med pa dang, kun rdzob tu bcos ma dang gzhan la ltos pa'i rnam pa de lta bu'i don bstan pa'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:31109.english: Here the presence of the phrase “in that way” is well done. As for the import of the remainder, what's being indicated is that there exists no entity which corresponds to what the tendency to hold things as real thinks it sees—along with the point that there is an aspect of being, in a deceptive way, artificial; and of relying upon something other.

corpus_segments:34901.acip: THAL 'GYUR SNGA MA LA KHYAB PA YOD DE GDAGS GZHI PHUNG PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR, 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN PHYUNG MI NUS PA JI SRID 'JUG GI BAR DU BTAGS CHOS GANG ZAG RANG NGOS NAS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN PHYUNG MI NUS PAR 'JUG PA GANG ZHIG DE JI SRID 'JUG GI BAR DU DE'I DBANG GIS LAS BSOG LAS DE'I DBANG GIS 'KHOR BAR 'KHOR BA'I PHYIR
corpus_segments:34901.wylie: thal 'gyur snga ma la khyab pa yod de gdags gzhi phung po rang bzhin gyis grub par, 'dzin pa'i rtog pa'i zhen yul sun phyung mi nus pa ji srid 'jug gi bar du btags chos gang zag rang ngos nas grub par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa'i zhen yul sun phyung mi nus par 'jug pa gang zhig de ji srid 'jug gi bar du de'i dbang gis las bsog las de'i dbang gis 'khor bar 'khor ba'i phyir
corpus_segments:34901.english: The first of our logical statements above is always true. For suppose that a person is still unable to root out the object that he thinks he sees when he hold the parts to the person, the thing which gets the label of "me," as existing through some nature of its own. As long as he goes on this way, then he will continue to find himself unable to root out the object that he thinks he sees when he holds the thing which gets the label, the "me," as existing from its own side. And as long as he continues with this, then by the power of this misperception he will continue to collect karma. And as long as he collects karma, then he will continue to spin around in this wheel of suffering life.

corpus_segments:34206.acip: BCINGS PA'I DON NI BDEN 'DZIN YOD PA TZAM MIN GYI, CHOS GANG LA YANG BDEN PAR GRUB BAM MA GRUB SNYAM DU SEMS PA NA, DE NYID BDEN PAR GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I BDEN ZHEN LAS MI 'DA' ZHING 'DA' MI NUS NA NI, DES BCINGS PAR 'JOG GO
corpus_segments:34206.wylie: bcings pa'i don ni bden 'dzin yod pa tsam min gyi, chos gang la yang bden par grub bam ma grub snyam du sems pa na, de nyid bden par grub par 'dzin pa'i bden zhen las mi 'da' zhing 'da' mi nus na ni, des bcings par 'jog go
corpus_segments:34206.english: And what does it mean when we say that someone is “chained” like this? It doesn't just refer to the fact that they possess the tendency to believe that things are real. Rather, it means that—when the person who is chained considers the question of whether things exist in a real way or not—they can never go beyond an attachment to thinking that these things are real: they can never go beyond believing that things are, in fact, real. When they cannot go beyond this, then that's what we call being “chained.”

corpus_segments:32337.acip: RAB 'BYOR RGYUN TU ZHUGS PAS 'DI JI SNYAM DU BDAG GI RGYUN TU ZHUGS PA'I 'BRAS BU THOB BO SNYAM DU BDEN PAR ZHEN CING SEMS SNYAM MAM ZHES GSUNGS PA NA, RAB 'BYOR GYIS DE NI MA LAGS SO,,
corpus_segments:32337.wylie: rab 'byor rgyun tu zhugs pas 'di ji snyam du bdag gi rgyun tu zhugs pa'i 'bras bu thob bo snyam du bden par zhen cing sems snyam mam zhes gsungs pa na, rab 'byor gyis de ni ma lags so
corpus_segments:32337.english: Here then the Buddha says, Now Subhuti, what do you think? Do those who have entered the stream ever think to themselves—do they ever grasp to this thing as existing in truth—with the idea, “Now I have attained the goal of entering the stream”? And Subhuti answers, They do not.

corpus_segments:32513.acip: BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG ZHIG 'DI SNYAM DU, BDEN ZHEN GYIS BDAG GIS SEMS CAN RNAMS YONGS SU MYA NGAN LAS BZLA'O ZER NA, DE BDAG MED KYI DON SHES PA'I BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' ZHES MI BYA'O,,
corpus_segments:32513.wylie: byang chub sems dpa' gang zhig 'di snyam du, bden zhen gyis bdag gis sems can rnams yongs su mya ngan las bzla'o zer na, de bdag med kyi don shes pa'i byang chub sems dpa' zhes mi bya'o
corpus_segments:32513.english: Suppose then that some bodhisattva were to think to themselves, “I will bring all living beings to total nirvana in a way where I still imagine that things are real.” We could never then call them a “bodhisattva who understands what it means to say there is no self to things.” [K109b]

corpus_segments:32516.acip: BSDU NA BDAG NI THOB PAR BYED PA'O, ,'DI NI THOB PAR BYA BA'I CHOS SO SNYAM DU BDEN ZHEN GYIS 'JUG NA MED PA LA YOD PAR RLOM PA MNGON PA'I NGA RGYAL CAN DU BSHAD PAS MI RUNG ZHES PA STE BDEN PAR GRUB NA BSGYUR DU MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR CHOS GANG LA'ANG THOB BYA THOB BYED SOGS BZHAG TU MI RUNG NGO ZHES GONG DU BSHAD ZIN TO,,
corpus_segments:32516.wylie: bsdu na bdag ni thob par byed pa'o, ,'di ni thob par bya ba'i chos so snyam du bden zhen gyis 'jug na med pa la yod par rlom pa mngon pa'i nga rgyal can du bshad pas mi rung zhes pa ste bden par grub na bsgyur du mi rung ba'i phyir chos gang la'ang thob bya thob byed sogs bzhag tu mi rung ngo zhes gong du bshad zin to
corpus_segments:32516.english: To sum then, let's take the case of someone who, with a belief that things are real, thinks to themselves that “I am going to achieve this or that,” or “This is the thing that I'm going to achieve.” What's being said in the text is that they would then be a person who had some extreme kind of delusion of grandeur—a delusion where they thought something existed, when in truth it didn't exist at all. This then would be “wrong,” the text is saying—because if things existed in truth then it would be wrong for them ever to exhibit change. Then further it would be wrong to say about any object at all that it could either be achieved or cause us to achieve anything. This point has already been explained previously.

This then would be “wrong,” the text is saying—because if things existed in truth then it would be wrong for them ever to exhibit change. corpus_segments:32518.acip: DE NAS SEMS CAN MYANG 'DAS LA 'GOD PA LA BDEN ZHEN MI BYED PAR MA ZAD, SANGS RGYAS KYI ZHING GZUNG BA YANG THA SNYAD DU BYED KYANG BDEN ZHEN GYIS MI BYA'O ZHES STON PA NI,
corpus_segments:32518.wylie: de nas sems can myang 'das la 'god pa la bden zhen mi byed par ma zad, sangs rgyas kyi zhing gzung ba yang tha snyad du byed kyang bden zhen gyis mi bya'o zhes ston pa ni
corpus_segments:32518.english: The next section of the text is meant to demonstrate the following point. Not only are we never to think about guiding living beings to nirvana in a state of mind where we still believe that things are real. We are further never to think that we could take possession of a Buddha paradise in some way where we were still believing that things were real—even though it is the case that we can take such possession in a nominal sense. We cannot make a paradise

corpus_segments:32605.acip: DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA SEMS CAN DU BDEN ZHEN MED CES STON PA NI, RAB 'BYOR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS RJES THOB NA'ANG 'DI SNYAM DU NGAS GDUL BYA'I SEMS CAN RNAMS BDEN 'DZIN GYIS BCINGS PA LAS DON DAM PAR BGROL BAR BYA'O ZHES THUGS LA DGONGS PA YOD DAM SNYAM NA,
corpus_segments:32605.wylie: de bzhin gshegs pa la sems can du bden zhen med ces ston pa ni, rab 'byor de bzhin gshegs pas rjes thob na'ang 'di snyam du ngas gdul bya'i sems can rnams bden 'dzin gyis bcings pa las don dam par bgrol bar bya'o zhes thugs la dgongs pa yod dam snyam na
corpus_segments:32605.english: Next comes a section which is intended to express how Those Gone Thus have no belief at all that living beings are real. And so Lord Buddha says, “Subhuti, what do you think? Does the One Thus Gone ever think to himself—even in the aftermath of the direct perception of emptiness—”I am going to free, in an ultimate way, all the living beings who are my disciples from the shackles of believing that things are real”? Does he ever have this sort of thought in his mind?

corpus_segments:35869.acip: BDEN 'DZIN GYI ZHEN YUL THAMS CAD 'JIG PAR BYED PA'I RIGS PA YANG DAG PA'I DON LA TSUL BZHIN DU DPYOD PA'I YANGS PA'I SHES RAB KYIS
corpus_segments:35869.wylie: bden 'dzin gyi zhen yul thams cad 'jig par byed pa'i rigs pa yang dag pa'i don la tshul bzhin du dpyod pa'i yangs pa'i shes rab kyis
corpus_segments:35869.english: But these wise ones utilized a form of clear thinking which allowed them to destroy all the objects that their habit of seeing things as real thought it was observing: they found a vast form of wisdom that performed its analysis with total accuracy, regarding the real nature of things.

corpus_segments:36891.acip: DES KYANG YE MED PA DES MED DU RTOGS PA TSAD MA'I DGAG SGRUB KYI DON DU MA GO BAR ZAD DE, BDEN ZHEN 'GOG PA LA DE'I ZHEN YUL YE MED DU RTOGS DGOS PAS SO,,
corpus_segments:36891.wylie: des kyang ye med pa des med du rtogs pa tshad ma'i dgag sgrub kyi don du ma go bar zad de, bden zhen 'gog pa la de'i zhen yul ye med du rtogs dgos pas so
corpus_segments:36891.english: People like this have simply failed to understand that something which was never there in the first place is exactly what we either deny or establish when we talk about using accurate perception to come to an understanding that something doesn't exist. That is, when we undertake to stop our tendency to grasp to things as real, we have to do so by coming to the realization that what this tendency thinks is there was never there in the first place.

That is, when we undertake to stop our tendency to grasp to things as real, we have to do so by coming to the realization that what this tendency thinks is there was never there in the first place.", "course": "SVN", "source_wave": "gmr-volumes-2026-08"}

corpus_segments:37626.acip: RTOG PA DANG RTOG MED KYI TSAD MA GANG YIN KYANG TSAD MAR SONG SA SNANG YUL DANG ZHEN YUL RANG MTSAN LA MA 'KHRUL BA ZHIG DGOS SO,,
corpus_segments:37626.wylie: rtog pa dang rtog med kyi tshad ma gang yin kyang tshad mar song sa snang yul dang zhen yul rang mtshan la ma 'khrul ba zhig dgos so
corpus_segments:37626.english: Whether we are talking about an accurate perception which employs images or does not, the measure of whether it is an accurate perception or not must then be considered to be the question of whether or not it is mistaken towards the actual expression of the object that appears to it, and that it thinks it sees.

corpus_segments:21938.acip: RAB 'BYOR RGYUN TU ZHUGS PAS 'DI JI SNYAM DU BDAG GI RGYUN TU ZHUGS PA'I 'BRAS BU THOB BO SNYAM DU BDEN PAR ZHEN CING SEMS SNYAM MAM ZHES GSUNGS PA NA, RAB 'BYOR GYIS DE NI MA LAGS SO,,Here then the Buddha says,
corpus_segments:21938.wylie: rab 'byor rgyun tu zhugs pas 'di ji snyam du bdag gi rgyun tu zhugs pa'i 'bras bu thob bo snyam du bden par zhen cing sems snyam mam zhes gsungs pa na, rab 'byor gyis de ni ma lags so,,here TheN The buDDha SayS
corpus_segments:21938.english: Now Subhuti, what do you think? Do those who have entered the stream ever think to themselves—do they ever grasp to this thing as existing in truth—with the idea, "Now I have attained the goal of entering the stream"? And Subhuti answers, They do not.

Do those who have entered the stream ever think to themselves—do they ever grasp to this thing as existing in truth—with the idea, \"Now I have attained the goal of entering the stream\"? And Subhuti answers, They do not."}

corpus_segments:21948.acip: DES NA BDEN 'DZIN GYI ZHEN YUL SUN 'BYIN MYONG MA MYONG NI BDEN MED RTOGS MYONG MA MYONG BA'I SGO NAS 'JOG STE,
corpus_segments:21948.wylie: des na bden 'dzin gyi zhen yul sun 'byin myong ma myong ni bden med rtogs myong ma myong ba'i sgo nas 'jog ste
corpus_segments:21948.english: Thus we can say that the question of whether or not someone has been able to debunk the existence of the object that the tendency to see things as real thinks it sees is decided by whether or not the person has been able to perceive the fact that nothing is real.
corpus_segments:21948.raw: {"course": "Sunlight", "acip": "DES NA BDEN 'DZIN GYI ZHEN YUL SUN 'BYIN MYONG MA MYONG NI BDEN MED RTOGS MYONG MA MYONG BA'I SGO NAS 'JOG STE,", "wylie": "des na bden 'dzin gyi zhen yul sun 'byin myong ma myong ni bden med rtogs myong ma myong ba'i sgo nas 'jog ste", "english": "Thus we can say that the question of whether or not someone has been able to debunk the existence of the object that the tendency to see things as real thinks it sees is decided by whether or not the person has been able to perceive the fact that nothing is real."}

corpus_segments:21949.acip: JI SRID GZHI GANG LA BDEN PAR GRUB BAM MA GRUB SNYAM DU SPYOD PA ZHUGS PA NA BDEN ZHEN LAS 'DA' MI NUS PA'I BAR DE SRID DU BDEN 'DZIN GYI ZHEN YUL SUN 'BYIN MI NUS PAS BDEN 'DZIN GYIS BCINGS PAR 'JOG GO ,
corpus_segments:21949.wylie: ji srid gzhi gang la bden par grub bam ma grub snyam du spyod pa zhugs pa na bden zhen las 'da' mi nus pa'i bar de srid du bden 'dzin gyi zhen yul sun 'byin mi nus pas bden 'dzin gyis bcings par 'jog go
corpus_segments:21949.english: As long as a person is still relating to any particular thing with uncertainty in their mind as to whether it exists in truth or not—so long as they are still unable to transcend their belief in things as real—then they remain unable to debunk the existence of the object that our tendency to see things as real thinks is there. And on this basis then we would say they are still chained by the fetters of holding that things are real.
corpus_segments:21949.raw: {"course": "Sunlight", "acip": "JI SRID GZHI GANG LA BDEN PAR GRUB BAM MA GRUB SNYAM DU SPYOD PA ZHUGS PA NA BDEN ZHEN LAS 'DA' MI NUS PA'I BAR DE SRID DU BDEN 'DZIN GYI ZHEN YUL SUN 'BYIN MI NUS PAS BDEN 'DZIN GYIS BCINGS PAR 'JOG GO ,", "wylie": "ji srid gzhi gang la bden par grub bam ma grub snyam du spyod pa zhugs pa na bden zhen las 'da' mi nus pa'i bar de srid du bden 'dzin gyi zhen yul sun 'byin mi nus pas bden 'dzin gyis bcings par 'jog go", "english": "As long as a person is still relating to any particular thing with uncertainty in their mind as to whether it exists in truth or not—so long as they are still unable to transcend their belief in things as real—then they remain unable to debunk the existence of the object that our tendency to see things as real thinks is there. And on this basis then we would say they are still chained by the fetters of holding that things are real."}

corpus_segments:21968.acip: MDOR NA RGYUN ZHUGS SOGS BZHI PO DES THOB MKHAN DANG THOB BYA'I 'BRAS BU LA BDEN ZHEN MI BYED CING, BDEN 'DZIN LHAN SKYES YOD SRID KYANG DE'I ZHEN YUL SUN MA PHYUNG BA NI MED DE, DE THAMS CAD KYANG STONG NYID RTOGS PA SNGON DU SONG BA'I PHYIR RO,,
corpus_segments:21968.wylie: mdor na rgyun zhugs sogs bzhi po des thob mkhan dang thob bya'i 'bras bu la bden zhen mi byed cing, bden 'dzin lhan skyes yod srid kyang de'i zhen yul sun ma phyung ba ni med de, de thams cad kyang stong nyid rtogs pa sngon du song ba'i phyir ro
corpus_segments:21968.english: To sum, we can say that people who have attained these four goals of entering the stream and so on never entertain any belief that either themselves—the person who has attained the particular goal—nor the goal that they have attained could exist in truth. And although it's the case that they could still have the innate form of grasping to things as being real, it is never the case that they have failed to debunk the object that this tendency thinks it sees. And that's because each and every one of them has already had an experience of the perception of emptiness. I am a destroyer of the foe

And although it's the case that they could still have the innate form of grasping to things as being real, it is never the case that they have failed to debunk the object that this tendency thinks it sees. And that's because each and every one of them has already had an experience of the perception of emptiness. I am a destroyer of the foe"}

corpus_segments:21993.acip: DE LTAR 'TSANG RGYA BA LA GANG DU 'TSANG RGYA BA'I ZHING DAG BSGRUB DGOS PAR STON PA NI, BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS RAB 'BYOR LA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG LA LA ZHIG BDAG GIS ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS BDEN ZHEN GYIS DON DAM PAR BSGRUB BAR BYA'O SNYAM ZHES ZER NA, TSIG DE NI MI BDEN PAR SMRA BA'O,,
corpus_segments:21993.wylie: de ltar 'tshang rgya ba la gang du 'tshang rgya ba'i zhing dag bsgrub dgos par ston pa ni, bcom ldan 'das kyis rab 'byor la byang chub sems dpa' gang la la zhig bdag gis zhing bkod pa rnams bden zhen gyis don dam par bsgrub bar bya'o snyam zhes zer na, tshig de ni mi bden par smra ba'o
corpus_segments:21993.english: Lord Buddha wishes to indicate that, in order for a person to reach the enlightenment described above, he or she must first bring about a paradise in which to achieve the enlightenment. Therefore the Conqueror says to Subhuti, Suppose some bodhisattva were to say or think to themselves—while holding a belief in true existence, and referring to ultimate existence—"I am working to bring about paradises." This statement would not be spoken true.

corpus_segments:22072.acip: NGO MTSAR CHE TSUL NI, MDO SDE 'DI BSHAD PA'I TSIG DANG DON LA SEMS CAN GANG DAG BDEN ZHEN MED PA YANG DAG PA'I 'DU SHES SKYED PAR 'GYUR BA'I SEMS CAN DE DAG NI, THAR PA'I BAG CHAGS 'JOG CING SANGS RGYAS THOB PA'I RGYU CHEN PO BZUNG BAS NA NGO MTSAR CHEN PO RAB DANG LDAN PAR 'GYUR RO,,
corpus_segments:22072.wylie: ngo mtshar che tshul ni, mdo sde 'di bshad pa'i tshig dang don la sems can gang dag bden zhen med pa yang dag pa'i 'du shes skyed par 'gyur ba'i sems can de dag ni, thar pa'i bag chags 'jog cing sangs rgyas thob pa'i rgyu chen po bzung bas na ngo mtshar chen po rab dang ldan par 'gyur ro
corpus_segments:22072.english: And just how is it so wondrous? Consider any living being who can think correctly—that is, who can think without believing that things are real—about both the words and the meaning of the sutra that Lord Buddha has just taught. These types of people have planted a seed for freedom—they hold within them now a powerful cause that will bring them to attain enlightenment itself. Thus then they are wondrous in the highest.

corpus_segments:22083.acip: RGYU MTSAN NI DE LTA BU'I BDAG TU 'DU SHES PA SOGS NI ZHEN YUL LA PHYIN CI LOG TU ZHUGS PA YIN PAS, DE NYID YANG DAG PA'I 'DU SHES THAMS CAD DANG BRAL BA'I PHYIR RAM, 'DU SHES DAG DON DAM PAR 'DU SHES SU GRUB PA DANG BRAL BA'I PHYIR ZHES PA'O ZHUS PA NA,
corpus_segments:22083.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni de lta bu'i bdag tu 'du shes pa sogs ni zhen yul la phyin ci log tu zhugs pa yin pas, de nyid yang dag pa'i 'du shes thams cad dang bral ba'i phyir ram, 'du shes dag don dam par 'du shes su grub pa dang bral ba'i phyir zhes pa'o zhus pa na
corpus_segments:22083.english: The reason for this is that conceiving of oneself as oneself and so on in the way described is to be completely mistaken about the object that one thinks one sees. And someone like this then would have lost every correct way of thinking. You could also say that they would lose any correct way of thinking—be free of every kind of this conception—if all these ways of thinking were thought to exist as thinking in some ultimate way.[103] Beyond all fear

corpus_segments:22234.wylie: bsdu na bdag ni thob par byed pa'o, ,'di ni thob par bya ba'i chos so snyam du bden zhen gyis 'jug na med pa la yod par rlom pa mngon pa'i nga rgyal can du bshad pas mi rung zhes pa ste bden par grub na bsgyur du mi rung ba'i phyir chos gang la'ang thob bya thob byed sogs bzhag tu mi rung ngo zhes gong du bshad zin to,,to SuM TheN, leT'S Take
corpus_segments:22234.english: the case of someone who, with a belief that things are real, thinks to themselves that "I am going to achieve this or that," or "This is the thing that I'm going to achieve." What's being said in the text is that they would then be a person who had some extreme kind of delusion of grandeur—a delusion where they thought something existed, when in truth it didn't exist at all. This then would be "wrong," the text is saying—because if things existed in truth then it would be wrong for them ever to exhibit change. Then further it would be wrong to say about any object at all that it could either be achieved or cause us to achieve anything. This point has already been explained previously.[439]

corpus_segments:22236.wylie: de nas sems can myang 'das la 'god pa la bden zhen mi byed par ma zad, sangs rgyas kyi zhing gzung ba yang tha snyad du byed kyang bden zhen
corpus_segments:22236.english: GYIS MI BYA'O ZHES STON PA NI,The next section of the text is meant to demonstrate the following point. Not only are we never to think about guiding living beings to nirvana in a state of mind where we still believe that things are real. We are further never to think that we could take possession of a Buddha paradise in some way where we were still believing that things were real—even though it is the case that we can take such possession in a nominal sense. We cannot make a paradise

corpus_segments:22450.acip: DE LTAR BDEN MED YANG DANG YANG DU BSHAD NAS BDEN 'DZIN NAN TAN DU MDZAD NAS BKAG GO ,'GOG TSUL NI, BDEN 'DZIN GYIS GZUNG BA LTAR DE'I ZHEN YUL LA RIGS PA'I GNOD BYED BSTAN NAS 'GOG PA YIN GYI, TSER MA 'DON PA LTAR MIN TE,
corpus_segments:22450.wylie: de ltar bden med yang dang yang du bshad nas bden 'dzin nan tan du mdzad nas bkag go ,'gog tshul ni, bden 'dzin gyis gzung ba ltar de'i zhen yul la rigs pa'i gnod byed bstan nas 'gog pa yin gyi, tsher ma 'don pa ltar min te
corpus_segments:22450.english: And so we see Lord Buddha here singling out this tendency to hold to things as real and denying that it could be correct—he is speaking over and over about how things have no real nature of their own. The way in which we deny the accuracy of this tendency is to present logical reasoning which would contradict the thing that we think we see when this tendency is doing its holding. It's not though something like the approach that we would take in trying to pluck a thorn from our skin.

corpus_segments:9466.english: Then the sculptor arrived-- The mind, fast as thought itself. It took up in its hands The refined gold of the subtlest element of all, And crafted the image, An Angel's holy body, made of wisdom itself. The body awoke And did miracles beyond the mind to conceive. I grabbed the universe, All three realms, and devoured it in a single swallow. At the very last I murdered the host of Those Who Have Gone That Way, And then had my way With the holy Lord, the Woman of the Buddhas. Aghast at what I had done, I ran off into simple voidness. When I think of this, I think of my Lama's kindness-- And oh how kind you have been to me, My Lama and my Lord.

corpus_segments:10969.english: Because these empowerments wash away the stench of our tendency to think of our own bodies as something ordinary, they help us develop the diamond of enlightened actions.  The initiations further empower us to practice the path of the stage of creation, along with all its associated practices.  Finally, they plant within us an extraordinary seed for the power that will come to us in the end: the power of the Body of Emanation.

corpus_segments:12422.acip: LUS DBEN GYI SGRA BSHAD YOD DE, DBEN GZHI'I LUS NI RAGS PA NYI SHU SOGS DANG , DBEN RGYU NI THA MAL GYI SNANG ZHEN DANG , DBEN PA'I DON NI DE RNAMS BDE STONG GI RNAM 'GYUR RAM LHAR SGOM PA DE YIN PA'I PHYIR,
corpus_segments:12422.wylie: lus dben gyi sgra bshad yod de, dben gzhi'i lus ni rags pa nyi shu sogs dang , dben rgyu ni tha mal gyi snang zhen dang , dben pa'i don ni de rnams bde stong gi rnam 'gyur ram lhar sgom pa de yin pa'i phyir
corpus_segments:12422.english: Now there does exist a literal explanation of the name of this stage: "transcendent body."  This is true because the thing that is transcendent is the body: meaning the twenty gross forms and such.  And what is transcended is the tendency to think of these things as normal.  Finally, what "transcendent" means here is that we think of these things as being a manifestation of bliss and emptiness; or we meditate upon them as being the form of an Angel.

corpus_segments:13562.acip: SGYU MAR MA SHES PAR BDE MCHOG RTZA RGYUD LA BRTEN NAS MTHU BYA'AM BSAM PA DANG , ,NAM MKHA' NA SGRA GCIG NA RE, ,SGYU MA'I SKYES BUS MA SLUS SAM, ,'DOD CHAGS LA ZHEN ZHE SDANG GIS, ,NGAN SONG GSUM DU SKYES PA LAS, ,BLA MA RNYED PAR GA LA 'GYUR, ZER BA DANG , RGYAL SRID LA SOGS PA CI YANG MI 'DUG GO, ,YANG LANGS TE GSOL BA 'DEBS BZHIN PHYIN PAS,
corpus_segments:13562.wylie: sgyu mar ma shes par bde mchog rtsa rgyud la brten nas mthu bya'am bsam pa dang , ,nam mkha' na sgra gcig na re, ,sgyu ma'i skyes bus ma slus sam, ,'dod chags la zhen zhe sdang gis, ,ngan song gsum du skyes pa las, ,bla ma rnyed par ga la 'gyur, zer ba dang , rgyal srid la sogs pa ci yang mi 'dug go, ,yang langs te gsol ba 'debs bzhin phyin pas
corpus_segments:13562.english: "Ah," thinks Naropa to himself.  "I had no idea that this was all just some magic illusion.  Perhaps I had better use some counter-spell to protect myself, something out of the root text of the secret teaching of Highest Bliss." And then a voice came from the sky and says, Doesn't it rather seem, Naropa, That you are always being deceived By people who are no more than a mirage? Craving after the objects of the senses And surrendering to your dislike of other things Can only throw you into a birth In one of the realms of misery. And then how are you ever Going to find Your holy Lama? Suddenly the King and the Princess and the entire kingdom all simply vanish.  And Naropa drags himself up off the ground one more time, to walk on with His prayers.

corpus_segments:14468.acip: RANG GI GNAS KHANG SOGS LA THA MAL GYI SNANG ZHEN MED PAR DAG ZHING BDE BA CAN LTA BU GSER GYI SA GZHI'AM, BEEd'URYA'I SA GZHI NAM MKHA'I RANG MDOG LTA BU LA GSER GYI MIG MANG RIS SU BRIS PA MNAN NA SOR BZHI TZAM NEM BYED PA, BTEG NA SNGAR LTAR MNYAM PA'I SPAR BYED PA, REG NA BDE BA BSKYED PA LAS SRA MKHREGS KYI RNAM PA MI 'BYUNG BA,
corpus_segments:14468.wylie: rang gi gnas khang sogs la tha mal gyi snang zhen med par dag zhing bde ba can lta bu gser gyi sa gzhi'am, beeDUrya'i sa gzhi nam mkha'i rang mdog lta bu la gser gyi mig mang ris su bris pa mnan na sor bzhi tsam nem byed pa, bteg na sngar ltar mnyam pa'i spar byed pa, reg na bde ba bskyed pa las sra mkhregs kyi rnam pa mi 'byung ba
corpus_segments:14468.english: Try to stop any tendency you have to think of your home, and the rest of your surroundings, as being something normal.  See it as being like the paradise of the Heaven of Bliss.  The earth below you is the ground of gold, or else one of lapis, with the color of the sky inscribed with designs of gold. When you place your foot on the ground, it sinks down to a distance of four fingerwidths, and when you lift your foot back up it rises back to the same level.  The ground doesn't feel hard, but instead is pleasant and soft when you touch it.

corpus_segments:14585.acip: DE LAS RAGS PA'I SPRUL SKUR LDANG SNYAM PA'I 'PHEN PA BTANG STE, 'OD DE JE RAGS SU SONG NAS MI TSAD LAS CHE TZAM GYI RJE BTZUN MA RGYAN CHA LUGS YONGS SU RDZOGS PA'I SKUR LAM GYIS BZHENGS PA LA 'BRAS DUS KYI SPRUL SKU DNGOS DE NGA'O SNYAM DU NGA RGYAL BZHAG PA'I SKYE BA SPRUL SKU'I LAM 'KHYER MDOR BSDUS BSGOMS TE SKAD CIG KRONG BSKYED BYED,
corpus_segments:14585.wylie: de las rags pa'i sprul skur ldang snyam pa'i 'phen pa btang ste, 'od de je rags su song nas mi tshad las che tsam gyi rje btsun ma rgyan cha lugs yongs su rdzogs pa'i skur lam gyis bzhengs pa la 'bras dus kyi sprul sku dngos de nga'o snyam du nga rgyal bzhag pa'i skye ba sprul sku'i lam 'khyer mdor bsdus bsgoms te skad cig krong bskyed byed
corpus_segments:14585.english: Resolve then that you will rise up from this state also, but now in a more coarse body, that of emanation.  The light gets more and more concrete, and then suddenly you have taken on the body of the Holy Angel.  You are a little bit larger than a human, and you are complete with all Her adornments and attire.  Look upon Yourself and feel supreme confidence, thinking "This is the actual body of emanation, as it exists when the result is reached.  And it is Me."  Do thus a short meditation on the practice of using rebirth as a path to the body of emanation, and so you have done a complete instantaneous creation. The Rite of Blessing the Inner Offering

corpus_segments:15166.acip: DE YANG BAm YIG LA LONGS SKU'I NGA RGYAL BYA BA LAS GSAL SNANG 'DON MI DGOS, 'DI'I LONGS SKU NI MTSAN DPE SOGS RNAM PA 'DRA BAS DER BZHAG PA MIN PAR, PHRA BA'I LUS KYI SGO NAS BYED DE, 'CHI BA 'OD GSAL PHRA BA LAS BZHENGS PAS YIN, SHIN TU PHRA BA'I RLUNG SEMS NI, GZHI DUS KYI BAR DO DANG, LAM DUS DANG 'BRAS DUS KYI LONGS SKU'I GDAGS GZHI'O,
corpus_segments:15166.wylie: de yang baM yig la longs sku'i nga rgyal bya ba las gsal snang 'don mi dgos, 'di'i longs sku ni mtshan dpe sogs rnam pa 'dra bas der bzhag pa min par, phra ba'i lus kyi sgo nas byed de, 'chi ba 'od gsal phra ba las bzhengs pas yin, shin tu phra ba'i rlung sems ni, gzhi dus kyi bar do dang, lam dus dang 'bras dus kyi longs sku'i gdags gzhi'o
corpus_segments:15166.english: You should note though that you only apply the supreme confidence to the letter; you need not make any special effort to perfect the vision of yourself as a letter, to come to see yourself as an actual vam.  We don't think of the letter as being the Body of Enjoyment because of some physical similarity, because it has the various features and marks and other qualities of that Body, but rather we see it as the Body of Enjoyment by virtue of its being the subtle body.  This is because it has risen out of the subtle clear light of death.  The very subtle inner wind and mind are what are given the name of the state between in the original state, and the name of the Body of Enjoyment during the period of the path and the final result.

corpus_segments:19868.acip: DANG PO NI, SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR BDAG MED PA'I DE KHO NA NYID KYI DON MTHAR THUG PA'I GO BA 'TSOL LUGS LA PHAR PHYIN GYI THEG PA LAS LHAG PA CIG SNGAGS LA MED DE, BDEN 'DZIN GYIS BZUNG BA'I ZHEN YUL RIGS PAS PHU DAG PAR BKAG PA'I SGO NAS BDEN 'DZIN GYI DMIGS GTAD MA BSHIG PAR YID NANG DU BSDUS PA TZAM GYIS NI, BDEN 'DZIN DANG 'DZIN STANGS 'GAL BA MED PAS BDEN 'DZIN LA CI YANG MI GNOD PA'I PHYIR DANG,
corpus_segments:19868.wylie: dang po ni, sngar bshad pa ltar bdag med pa'i de kho na nyid kyi don mthar thug pa'i go ba 'tshol lugs la phar phyin gyi theg pa las lhag pa cig sngags la med de, bden 'dzin gyis bzung ba'i zhen yul rigs pas phu dag par bkag pa'i sgo nas bden 'dzin gyi dmigs gtad ma bshig par yid nang du bsdus pa tsam gyis ni, bden 'dzin dang 'dzin stangs 'gal ba med pas bden 'dzin la ci yang mi gnod pa'i phyir dang
corpus_segments:19868.english: Here is the first.  As we explained before, it's not the case that here in the way of the secret word there is some form of the understanding of the ultimate reality of suchness--of the fact that nothing is itself--which is somehow superior to that found in the way of the open teachings of the perfections. That is, suppose that we are unable to demolish the way in which our tendency to think things are real holds things to be--suppose that we fail to use reasoning to deny, perfectly, the object which this tendency thinks it sees.  Suppose we simply gather the mind inward. In this case the way our own mind holds things to be will in no way contradict the way our tendency to see things as real holds them to be; and we will have done nothing at all to impede this tendency.
